preText:
7.30pm Gaikwad and Conway will open the batting for CSK. Conway has been released by NZC for the entire IPL season. Shami has the new ball for GT. He will operate from round the wicket. Let's go

7.28pm Josh Little is the first Ireland player to feature in the IPL. He was a net bowler for CSK during their prep camp in Surat in IPL 2022.

7.10pm GT win the toss and opt to bowl first. Maharashtra seam-bowling allrounder Hangargekar starts for CSK and makes his IPL debut.

CSK XI: 1 Devon Conway, 2 Ruturaj Gaikwad, 3 Moeen Ali, 4 Ben Stokes, 5 Ravindra Jadeja, 6 Shivam Dube, 7 Ambati Rayudu, 8 MS Dhoni (capt&wk), 9 Mitch Santner, 10 Deepak Chahar, 11 Rajvardhan Hangargekar

Subs: Tushar Deshpande, Subhranshu Senapati, Shaik Rasheed, Ajinkya Rahane, Nishant Sindhu

Titans XI: 1 Shubhman Gill, 2 Wriddhiman Saha (wk), 3 Kane Williamson, 4 Vijay Shankar, 5 Hardik Pandya (capt), 6 Rahul Tewatia, 7 Rashid Khan, 8 Mohammed Shami, 9 Josh Little, 10 Alzarri Joseph, 11 Yash Dayal

Subs: B Sai Sudharsan, Jayant Yadav, Mohit Sharma, Abhinav Manohar, KS Bharat

In this XI, CSK have batting all the way down to No.11. They could potentially bring in Simarjeet Singh or Tushar Deshpande, for instance, in place of a batter during their defence later in the evening.

Hardik: Absolutely! Good to play here and the kind of crowd we get here is exciting. I think almost everyone from the country has got motivation from him and nothing better than starting the season with Dhoni. Impact Player is different, so I've left it to him. Ashu pa was up all night. I don't know and I've passed on the team.

Dhoni: We were also looking to bowl first and I don't think it [the pitch] will change. Last night it rained and I don't know if there will be dew. The preparation has been good and we assembled early [in Chennai]. Overall, it seems as if we've done okay. It [Impact Player rule] is a luxury to have and it becomes slightly easy to use here because in domestic it was at the 14th over. Four foreigners - Moeen, Stokes, Santner and Conway - and the others will fight for that one spot.

7pm There's some grass covering on the pitch and could offer some good bounce, reckons Simon Doull. There were reports on Thursday that Dhoni could miss the IPL opener with an injury, but he is now out for the toss, which has been delayed.

Deepak Samson : "The stadium in a sea of yellow!! Guess everyone realises that there might only be very few more chances to watch MSD on cricket field. Some things transcend team loyalties..."

6.57pm Toss coming up under fire-work filled skies. Do stay tuned. Dhoni embraces Hardik and then shakes hands with former Super King R Sai Kishore near the edge of the boundary. "Dhoni is warming up now," says Shashank. "He's feeling his knee every now and then". He was wearing a kneecap when he was batting at the Chepauk nets earlier this week.

Deepak Samson : "Calendar cleared. CSK Jersey on. Cannot wait."

6.45pm Who are you supporting in today's match? Have your say in our Live report

6.33pm Shashank from Ahmedabad: "Thala sitting all by himself in the CSK dugout, right at the centre, listening to Arjit Singh. The moment he's shown on the big screen the fans erupt in joy."

Sanket: "This impact rule will be headache for the fantasy player like me"

Siva: "Remember a game against Australia where India used Jadeja for batting and Chahal for bowling due to Jadeja getting concussed.. that is the kind of situation you want Impact player for. CSK can use Dube for batting and Simarjeet/Deshpande/Hangargekar instead for bowling"

Afeef: "@sanket I hope Williamson's presence will allow Hardik to bat more freely and revert to his old finisher role from his days at Mumbai Indians "

Ravi: "To be honest, I don't like this impact player rule, perhaps its to early to decide. I would like to see a 11 vs 11 game with allrounders contributing. From CSK's point of view, they have a good playing 11. The bench is not so good and will struggle find an impact player until the remaining overseas players are back. Also they will play 4 overseas players in their first 11, so don't know how MSD will use impact players."

sanket patil: "Kane Williamson could be really good signing for GT. With Gill,Hardik, Miller, Tewatia batting around Kane gives that freedom for him to take his time and pace an innings. And this is big ground where he can easily gets ones , twos and keep the scoreboard ticking."

6.30pm Where should Stokes bat for CSK? Go and vote here

ICYMI: CSK's left-arm seamer Mukesh Choudhary has been sidelined from the entire season with a stress fracture of the back, joining Kyle Jamieson on the sidelines. Former Rajasthan Royal Akash Singh has been roped in as a like-for-like replacement

6.20pm Time for some song and dance at the Motera. The opening ceremony has got underway in Ahmedabad. Shashank sets up the scene from the venue: "It's 80% full already. More CSK supporters than Titans' blue, and they're all wearing Dhoni's No.7 jersey."

6.15pm Over the years, Dhoni has passed on his wisdom to Hardik. Can he use the same to trump the old master in the IPL opener, wonders Shashank Kishore.

Hefaz: "Hello IPL!I was waiting the whole year to see back the blue men once again in action! Rashid Khan will rock this season once again!"

Afeef: "Can't forget the GT vs CSK clash from last season where Miller smacked 94* to seal a tight chase. That became an instant classic. Would be amazing if this season starts off with a similar match."

6.05pm Thanks Monga. Hello, everyone. Are You Ready?

Girish: "Question to Muthu: How was the trip to the other planet?" --- I didn't take that trip. It was my big brother Al Muthu who travelled 3.147 billion lightyears away from earth for a bit of peace and quiet.

Afeef: "I'm wondering where will Stokes and Moeen bat? In my opinion, Moeen should bat at 3 and Stokes at 5, Rayudu slotting in between them." --- Rayudu will be key for CSK against Rashid. has had the wood over Rashid, scoring 79 runs off 65 balls off him without being dismissed in the IPL.

Virpalsinh : "MS will not use Impact Player and will win. At this point no one is expert in this impact player things. With out much data and under intense match-situation this thing for first few matches or season will bring more chaos"

6pm "Am excited to see how each team responds to the new innovations. I can see someone like Ashwin trying to take full advantage of this new strategic opportunity, whilst other players will concentrate on the basics, ignoring the new distractions. We'll see soon!"

Daryll, I am sure there are lots of ins and outs to these, which Deivarayan Muthu will tell you more about while I get myself a cuppa.

5.45pm Are we entering a 12-vs-12 era in T20 cricket through the Impact Player? Nagraj Gollapudi spoke to people who matter, and has this feature for you. This substitution is something every one is looking at this year. My prediction: don't be surprised if MS Dhoni keeps things simple, uses no Impact Player, and still manages to win.

5.30pm The crowds are back, the home-and-away system is back, it is almost like old times. And yet it is new times with a host of innovations: teams can be changed based on the result of the toss, there is an impact player, no-balls and wide balls can be challenged through DRS. The 16th edition of the IPL proves to be an exciting blend of the old and the new. We are in nice and early to bring it in with the first match, between the defending champions Gujarat Titans and Chennai Super Kings in Ahmedabad.

12.05am The opening match started on a Friday, but it is Saturday by the time the presentations are done. not quite clinical, but still a comfortable enough win for the defending champions Gujarat Titans. That's all we have for you tonight, but we will be back before you even get a chance to miss us as tomorrow is a double header. See you then.

Midnight The Player of the Match is Rashid Khan. He says: "So happy to get the Man of the Match. Gives me so much of energy for the rest of the competition. Bowling to the leftie was hard but the more I keep it tight, it is better. I had it in my mind to keep it simple. Just bowl the right areas consistently. Batting is all about time spent in the nets. The kind of opportunity and confidence in me by the coaching staff and the captain does give me a lot of batting time in the nets. It helps me in the middle."

11.55pm We will soon be into day of this match with the presentation not yet done. Hardik Pandya says: "I am obviously very happy, but we did put ourselves in a difficult position. We were very happy with 178 because at one point they looked like going past 200. But we kept getting wickets. Having the impact rule makes my job very difficult. There are too many options. Because of it, someone will always bowl less or late. My shot and Shubman's shot put the team in a difficult position. We have some standards inside the dressing room. We have to finish the games, and not Rash and Rahul all the time."

11.45pm "We were slightly short," says MS Dhoni, the losing captain. "Another 15-20 runs would have been good. We all know there would be a little bit of dew. Also it was a 7.30pm start so the ball holds on a little early on. Also we could have batted properly in the middle overs as opposed to trying to muscle the ball. Rutu is a pleasure to watch. He has groomed himself very well, and makes the eight decisions under pressure. We can't afford to bowl no-balls. That is something in our control."

11.38pm That's a pretty comfortable win for the defending champions, GT. Led by Rashid Khan with the ball, they restricted CSL to 20 short of a par score, and then chased it down fairly easily. In the end, two blows from Rashid Khan turned a possibly tight finish to a walk in the park in the last over. The win will be extra sweet because they couldn't use their Impact Player properly thanks to the injury to Kane Williamson when fielding. The pace of the match hasn't been great with more than four hours taken

Play ESPNcricinfo's first AR-based game - just aim and hit the stumps.

AS: "Whats the point of having overseas players on the impact player list? " -- Just had a re-read of the playing conditions and you are allowed to have overseas players on the bench because the substitute fielders can also come only from the five-man bench. The impact player will also come from that bench, which will definitely be an Indian player.

3.15pm Hello all, welcome to the first double-header of the IPL. Mohali has stayed dry so far, something that was in doubt yesterday. Interesting that V Iyer does not make KKR's XI at the start, not only will that be a blow to his confidence but also the side does not trust him to bowl either. We may see him or Jagadeesan as the impact sub later when KKR bat.

Prabhsimran was the likely opener after a terrific SMAT for the Kings. There's a bunch of different ways they could play the impact sub later in the day, maybe even bringing in a Rishi Dhawan midway through their batting innings for his power hitting.

All right. What do you make of the teams? Let Sreshth know, and also ask him whom he is supporting.

Sifat Khawry: "It's so delightful, and a proud moment for Afghanistan to have its genuine batter Gurbaz making debut in the IPL"

PBKS: 1 Shikhar Dhawan (capt), 2 Prabhsimran Singh, 3 Bhanuka Rajapaksa, 4 Sikandar Raza, 5 Jitesh Sharma (wk), 6 Shahrukh Khan, 7 Sam Curran, 8 Nathan Ellis, 9 Harpreet Brar, 10 Rahul Chahar, 11 Arshdeep Singh. The subs are Rishi Dhawan, Taide, Short, Bhatia and Rathee.

KKR: 1 Rahmanullah Gurbaz, 2 Mandeep Singh, 3 Nitish Rana, 4 Rinku Singh, 5 Andre Russell, 6 Shardul Thakur, 7 Sunil Narine, 8 Tim Southee, 9 Anukul Roy, 10 Umesh Yadav, 11 Varun Chakravarthy. The subs are Suyash, Arora, Jagadeesan, V Iyer and Wiese

3.01pm Time for the coin to be flipped... KKR win the toss and bowl. Rana says rain has been around, and expects moisture. "Very few get this opportunity, so I'm excited to be captain," he says. Southee, Russell, Narine and Gurbaz are his foreign players. Dhawan wanted to bowl first as well. He wants to maintain his consistency in the tournament, and announces Rajapaksa, Curran, Ellis... and *forgets the fourth name*.

"How is the weather in Mohali? Will we have the first rain-affected match this IPL?" --- Looks bright and clear for now, Vinod Rajpal

Micky_Cremona: "Hello from UK! Not a good pre-season for Punjab. Jonny injured, Liam coming back from injury, Dhawan hardly had competitive cricket... but we've got Sikandar Raza in the form of his life! Hopefully he will deliver!"

The pitch looks "light brown in colour" to Daren Ganga, and there isn't much grass. It feels hard too, and there shouldn't be too much of changes while batting first or chasing. There are relatively uneven boundary dimensions at the ground.

2.50pm Dhawan, Raza, Curran and Arshdeep on one side; Russell, Narine, Thakur and Ferguson on the other. Who do you think are the favourites today? Tom Moody has already made up his mind. And ICYMI, Australian Matt Short has replaced Bairstow for PBKS, and might even open with Dhawan.

Neal: "Keen to see how Sammy Curran will be used as a batsman, and expecting big things from Shikhar Dhawan to get his name in front of selectors in an ODI World Cup year" --- I'm afraid Dhawan might never play for India again due to a combination of his own dip in form, Gill's remarkable success, and the plethora of opening options that India have

You can follow ball-by-ball commentary of the game in Hindi, and in Tamil.

2.40pm Both of today's teams have been impacted by injuries or unavailability: no Iyer, Shakib, Litton, Rabada, Livingstone and Bairstow to begin with. So how do KKR cover for Iyer? Sanjay Manjrekar and Tom Moody discuss. But never mind, Iyer's replacement Nitish Rana says captaincy is "not new" to him.

One side has a new captain by accident, another by choice. But they both opted for fresh coaches too, which Sreshth's preview highlights. Both PBKS and KKR will be keen to improve on their performance from last year, when they had ended sixth and seventh, respectively.

Bhargav: "It's the battle between two blow-hot-blow-cold teams."

postText:
Everybody got some sort of score for the Kings today but they needed one of them to get an 80+ total or thereabouts. That didn't happen. Chandrakant Pandit said they'd be happy chasing 180-200, so is that advantage Knight Riders at the break? ESPNcricinfo's forecaster does not agree, with KKR having under 25% chance of victory. Let's see how it turns out when Himanshu joins you on the other side.

5.12pm So Kings make only 91 in the second half after making 100 in the first. Knight Riders will be mighty pleased to restrict Kings to a sub-200 total. Their bowlers struggled up top - barring Umesh, who was rather economical - but Narine, Varun and the rest slid in a few quiet overs at the slog-end of the innings.

Here's Bhanuka Rajapaksa: "See Harsha I don't think it is a typical Mohali wicket. It had something for spinners and fast bowlers in the back end. (His six off Narine) Instinct took over. Told Shikhar I'd take him on. It worked. (191 score) It is a good total because we were aiming for 180-185. We've found the score. (Second season with PBKS, Bayliss' messaging) So clear. He wants me to bat top of the order and bat with a clear mind."

preText:
Curran to Mandeep

5.51pm Okay, it's starting. The PBKS players trickle back out on the field. The lights are all functioning, and it's time for the cricket to take over.

Garv Asnani: "I think they could have played a few overs before going off as it's not too dark yet, but now it's going get much darker as time goes on." --- If only it were gully cricket, then we would be playing even if only a single thread of the ball was visible

Souriddha: "Delay due to floodlight malfunction - what a shame in an age when teams are severely taxed for slow over rates!!" --- I'm not sure if venues or host associations will be penalised for this failure, but I get your point

5.37pm And, and... they are going off. Floodlight failure stops play. Now, after a few minutes, the floodlights at one end seem to be working, although there is no sign yet of those lighting up at the opposite end.

MikeB: "Might be my failing eyes, but it looks like it's broad daylight?!?" --- None at all. The sun has long bid goodbye, and darkness is nearing by the minute

Nisha Uniyal: "Uncapped Indian players have never received so much attention before the impact player rule"

After waiting for a good five minutes and more, the floodlights still don't seem to be glowing. The umpires have a word, Mandeep does some stretching, and the PBKS players too indulge in a discussion. Some real relaxation there.

Curran has the new ball. Mandeep on strike. A slip in place. Deep square and deep point on the rope. But there is a delay in play since the floodlights are yet to come on. We keep waiting, waiting...

Looks like Rishi Dhawan has been brought on as Impact Player for PBKS. Yup, Rishi Dhawan replaces Rajapaksa. And here come Gurbaz and Mandeep to open the innings for KKR.

5.22pm Evening, everyone. You would wonder if PBKS are 10 or 15 short on a pitch where the ball is coming on nicely, and the bounce is even. I wouldn't think dew would come into effect so early - it's not even dark in Mohali yet - and KKR stand a fair chance of starting the season with a win.

postText:
That's it from us from the first of the two matches today. There was considerable time lost due to a floodlight failure at the start of KKR's innings, but I'm not sure if all four remaining overs would have been possible before rain interrupted play. Meanwhile, LSG, against DC, are off to a stable start in Lucknow as the action continues this evening. But for here, it's goodnight and goodbye from Raghav, Thilak, Sreshth and me, Himanshu!

Arshdeep Singh is the Player of the Match

7.51pm Okay, we are done: PBKS beat KKR by seven runs on DLS method. The rain is yet to stop after that interruption, and the umpires decided that was it. KKR fall short despite some late blows by Russell; and they will ruin those two wickets they lost in the last two overs. It was always going to be difficult once they were 29 for 3 in the fifth over, and KKR will want to relook at their top six in the absence of Shreyas Iyer and Shakib Al Hasan. On the contrary, PBKS' win was set up by contributions from their entire top seven. Hang around for the presentations.

Vikram: "I am 20 kms away from stadium. Its raining heavily. Chances of play resuming are very bleak." --- Exactly the post we were missing all this while

7.45pm The umpires are walking on the boundary rope, with umbrellas firmly placed overhead. They enter the KKR dressing room, and have a chat with their captain Rana. They even shook hands with one of the KKR staff members. Is that sign that we are done?

So what if rain has stopped the action here? You can always hop over from Mohali to Lucknow - don't ask me in how much time - as LSG host DC in both teams' season opener. DC have chosen to field after winning the toss.

7.40pm It is still raining steadily in Mohali, with covers in place pretty much all around. The ground looks entirely empty - there is not a soul there - with resumption getting further delayed.

Aditya: "Absolute chaos, this is what I've missed for the past couple of months!" --- And I'm sure this season hasn't disappointed you in just two days of action

TSB: "What blasphemy is this?! Shardul Thakur averages 10 with the bat after 140 T20 games?" --- To be honest, I had never realised this until now. Pretty shocking, yeah

7.18pm It has got much heavier, and rain stops play. As per DLS, KKR are seven runs behind. Two wickets in the last two overs for PBKS, and that must have made all the difference. The pitch and the outfield are quickly covered at the ground. The rain is hammering down, and I don't expect play to resume very soon.

9.24 pm So LSG puts up a very robust total aided by some woeful fielding by Delhi Capitals. The biggest gaffe of them all was Khaleel Ahmed's inexplicable drop of Kyle Mayers on 14 at short third man who went on to blast 73 off 38. Can Delhi chase it down? Stay tuned to find out. Reminder that the impact player subs have been used by both sides. K Gowtham comes in for Badoni on the LSG side while Aman Khan has been swapped in for Khaleel Ahmed for Delhi's chase. Stay tuned for the start of the reply shortly.

Kyle Mayers on the sideline after his 73 off 38: "It was a tricky surface at the start. It kept a bit low and the bounce was variable. But it's still a good wicket. Our bowlers need to use the wicket, it's gripping a bit and I think we'll be in good stead. [On the ball that got him out.] I think that's the drier end of the pitch. There's an area on that pitch that's very dry and the other end is full of grass so I think the spinners need to execute from that end in particular. It's a new surface. I tried to get information from the guys. It's tricky trying to get accustomed as fast as possible. [On being dropped on 14] It's always good to get some luck. Sometimes you play a good shot and a guy takes a blinder. So I'm happy to get an opportunity. I just wanted to do well on my first game and help my team and I did that."

Jos Buttler, Rajasthan Royals batter: We had a really good last year but it is very much about starting fresh. It is about playing what is in front of us and focussing on the here and now. He (Holder) brings some good balance with the bat and the ball - it is fantastic to have in T20 cricket. The Impact Player rule adds another dynamic. Disappointing for him (Prasidh Krishna) to be injured but it gives someone else an opportunity to step up. (On importance of playing spin) Very important. It has been a prevalent part in T20 cricket wherever you play so it is exciting to play in different venues and in different venues - that is part of what makes the IPL special.

Sunrisers Hyderabad XI: Abhishek Sharma, Mayank Agarwal, Rahul Tripathi, Harry Brook, Glenn Phillips (wk), Washington Sundar, Bhuvneshwar Kumar (c), Adil Rashid, Fazalhaq Farooqi, Umran Malik, T Natarajan

He confirms that Brook, Farooqi, Phillips and Rashid are the overseas players. Samson says the wicket looks good for both bowling and batting, and that they need to be confident of whatever they are doing. Buttler, Hetmyer, Holder and Boult are the four overseas players for RR.

2:58pm Not long left now before the toss. The team chasing has only won once so far this season (out of three). What will the captain winning the toss want to do today in this afternoon game? Stay tuned to find out!

Looks like Adil Rashid, Glenn Phillips, Harry Brook and Mayank Agarwal have been handed their SRH caps. Jason Holder and KM Asif, meanwhile, will make their RR debuts today.

Let's see what the conditions have in store for us. The pitch looks pristine and according to Sanjay Manjrekar, it looks very much like an English pitch - white in colour with an even covering of dry grass. It is a black soil surface, meaning that there might not be a lot of turn for the spinners. A few cracks here and there but he does not expect it to play much of a part. RR enter this season, hoping to go one better than 2022. SRH, meanwhile, stitched together a superb mid-season run last campaign, only to lose steam when it really mattered. Both teams have had a chance to plug the holes that surfaced in 2022, and on paper, seem better placed to go the distance than they did twelve months ago.

SRH, though, will have to contend with the unavailability of a few key players today. Aiden Markram (their captain), Heinrich Klaasen and Marco Jansen are currently on national duty. But in Harry Brook, Glenn Phillips, Mayank Agarwal and Rahul Tripathi, they have more than enough firepower to offset it. Keep an eye out for Abhishek Sharma too, who seems to have grown in stature over the past couple of years.

RR, meanwhile, would be hoping that their explosive batting unit comes to the party again. Jos Buttler, Sanju Samson and Yashasvi Jaiswal can tee off from the outset, and with Shimron Hetmyer adding impetus in the middle order, they seem to have most of their batting bases covered.

This, however, is also a contest between two strong bowling units. SRH have packed their bowling attack with top-quality Indian pacers - each of whom have a point to prove. RR are missing Prasidh Krishna but have arguably the best spin-bowling contingent at the IPL.

2:25pm Three games into the season and we have already had several talking points. It began with Ahmedabad being painted yellow, and Hardik Pandya getting the better of MS Dhoni.

Yesterday, we had rain-induced drama in the afternoon fixture, before Mark Wood produced a storm of his own to blow the Delhi Capitals away. Today, the caravan moves to Hyderabad, where the Sunrisers Hyderabad would hope to become the fourth team to register a home win at the first time of asking. But they will have to do so against Rajasthan Royals, who were last season's finalists.

postText:
5:20pm Well, that innings ebbed and flowed throughout. RR raced out of the traps, with Buttler and Jaiswal dominating the powerplay. Samson then took over and ensured that the runs kept coming. Support, though, was not very forthcoming from the other end, with Parag and Padikkal struggling. SRH did well to curb the run-flow towards the end too, conceding only 43 runs off the final five overs.

Speaking of SRH, plenty of bright spots for them. Natarajan was sensational at the death, as was Farooqi. Umran cleaned up Padikkal with an absolute peach, and Rashid held his own brilliantly, throwing the first spanner in RR's works. RR still managed to get over 200 but considering where SRH were at the half-way stage, they will be happy chasing this total. Do join us in a bit for the run-chase!

Adil Rashid: (On the pitch and his bowling) Some gripped, some went through. Generally, it was a good batting pitch. We had to find a way to do a job and after the first six, we did a tremendous job. (On Farooqi and Natarajan) To restrict them to this score, they bowled exceptionally well and it has brought us back into the game. It is nice to play in front of a full house and against the world's best players. (On the score) Maybe 5-10 runs a bit more than we would have liked. But we have world-class players all the way down and hopefully we can hunt this down.

The teams are observing a two-minute silence for Salim Durani, who died this morning.

Parth: "Can't even a regular substitute come apart from the names given in the list?" --- No, and that has always been the case.

Shyam: "Who is Nehal Wadhera and Arshad Khan? 2 new finds of MI scouting network?" --- Nehal Wadhera is a hard-hitting left-hand Punjab batter who can bowl some legspin as well. Arshad Khan is an MP allrounder, bats left-hand and bowls left-arm seam. Both are making their T20 debut as well. Sampath tells me last time a team had two T20 debutants in an IPL game was Delhi Daredevils in 2018 (Sandeep Lammichane and Abhishek Sharma). KKR had two T20 debuts in their first match of the same season (Shubman Gill and Shivam Mavi).

Mohd Irshad: "MI looking better on paper than last year, hope to see that on ground too."

Mumbai have been in a rebuilding phase since the 2022 mega auction. At that auction, they went in with a dream. The dream of having Jofra Archer and Jasprit Bumrah bowl in tandem for them. They knew their dream wouldn't become a reality immediately - Archer was not available for the 2022 season. But now with Bumrah out with a back injury, they will have to wait for yet another season. Having said that, they seemed to have got their batting might back. You can read more about what to expect from today's game in our preview.

RCB have been pretty consistent of late, making the playoffs in each of the last three seasons. This run has also coincided with them not playing at their home ground, M Chinnaswamy Stadium - theirs is one of the poorest home records for an IPL team. This season, they play six of their first eight games in Bengaluru, which could dictate how their campaign goes.

postText:
What a way for RCB to start their campaign. They did not even need an Impact Player, such was their dominance. Hemant is working hard on his report, which should be up yet. The caravan rolls and we have Chennai Super Kings taking on Lucknow Super Giants tomorrow. Till then, this is Ashish Pant, signing off on behalf of Hemant, Ranjith and Raghav. Good night!

Faf du Plessis is the Player of the Match: It was a nice way to start the way we did in the powerplay. Siraj with his tail up is a beautiful thing. The bowler stuck to their task The last two or three overs, was a bit of learning. The cutters were working really well, it was not easy to hit the ball. There was value for your shots. Credit to the groundsman. Even the spinners found something. [On the crowd] It's awesome to play. It's my first time playing here as a home player, especially batting with Virat Kohli. [Fielding] You have to try and stay with the youngsters. I try and push the old hamstrings so that I can move in the field. To start the campaign with a bang, was huge.

Presentation time

Virat Kohli: Phenomenal win. Homecoming after so many years. Credit to their batters for getting to that score. Tilak batted well. We kept backing ourselves. Faf went first, and I joined later. I am very happy with how things went today. The new ball was a bit tricky, but we shifted the momentum by taking them down with the new ball. We nullified all their intensity. The wicket was quite a nice one. We hit good areas and kept putting pressure on the bowlers. [Crowd] Phenomenal, was a packed crowd. Every seat was full and we knew we would get a lot of support. We just ride off that intensity from the crowd They were right behind us. [On Karn Sharma] He was phenomenal, when he got that left-hander out, that was great bowling. He was bowling so well last year. He was ready to play. Even in the nets, he was not getting hit for sixes. He put us on the front foot right away. The first game of the IPL, and to perform like that was great. Apart from Mumbai winning five times and Chennai four times, we have qualified the most number of times, so we do play consistent cricket. It's just about staying focused, and just try to be the best balanced team. We need to play on this momentum. We just need to execute better.

Rohit Sharma: Didn't have a great start but was a good effort from Tilak at the end. But the bowlers didn't bowl well. We didn't bat good enough, it was a good pitch. [On Tilak] Some of the shorts he played today, he showed a lot of courage. We wanted to be courageous enough, and hats off to Tilak for getting us to the total. Was a good pitch to bat on. We did not bat to our potential. 30-40 runs would have been ideal. We were struggling t play the catch-up game. [No Bumrah] For the past six-eight months I am used to play without Bumrah. We can't control things which we can't control. The other guys are also talented. A lot of the guys haven't played IPL before. First game of the season, lot to look forward to.

11.08pm Everything that could have gone right for RCB, did. Everything that could have wrong for Mumbai, did. Think that's the best way to put. Mumbai, bar Tilak Varma were all over the place, and still got to 171. But RCB openers, Virat Kohli and Faf du Plessis just showed how good a surface that was. The duo added 148 runs off 89 balls to set-up the chase. Kohli remained unbeaten on 82 off 49, while du Plessis scored 73 off 43. RCB mopped up the win in just 16.2 overs and that will give their net run-rate a boost.

9.23 pm CSK end on 217 for 7, and yet somehow their last 10 overs were slower than their first 10. The home crowd certainly got their money's worth for this innings. Can LSG chase this down? Stay tuned for the start of the chase.

CSK opener Devon Conway: "I think it was a great start for us tonight. The way Rutu played in that first six was pretty special and he took the pressure off me. He's sneaky strong. He times the ball and holds his shape really well, and he uses good bats. I think the slower ball into the wicket might be a good option for us, pace off and being unpredictable. I also felt for the spinners, some skidded on and some held up. It's a very special feeling [at Chepauk]. When I got here earlier, the crowd was special. They were pretty loud and it just creates a great atmosphere. Seeing MS Dhoni walk out there and do what he did and hearing the crowd is pretty special so it's good to be playing here in front of our fans. He said to go out, express yourself, enjoy, have fun and entertain."

For the IPL stats mavens out there, Dhoni completed 5,000 career IPL runs in his brief but belligerent innings.

preText:
7.27pm The two umpires stride out to the middle. The two Delhi Capitals batters, Prithvi Shaw and David Warner, who is on 5973 IPL runs, also come out. The Titans fielders are in place. Mohammed Shami will take the new ball. Watch out for the nip-backer into Shaw. All set. Warner to take strike. Over the wicket. One slip in place.

Afeef: "Tough call to bench Rovman Powell "

Subs available for Titans: R Sai Kishore, Vijay Shankar, Jayant Yadav, Abhinav Manohar

Subs available for Capitals: Lalit Yadav, Rovman Powell, Chetan Sakariya, Manish Pandey, Khaleel Ahmed

Playing XIs

Gujarat Titans: WP Saha (wk), Shubman Gill, B Sai Sudharsan, HH Pandya (capt), DA Miller, R Tewatia, Rashid Khan, JB Little, AS Joseph, Yash Dayal, Mohammed Shami

Delhi Capitals P Shaw, DA Warner (capt), MR Marsh, SN Khan, RR Rossouw, Aman Hakim Khan, AR Patel, Abishek Porel, Kuldeep Yadav, A Nortje, Mukesh Kumar

Toss: David Warner has the coin. Hardik Pandya calls correctly and Titans will bowl first.

David Miller comes in for Williamson, while Sai Sudharsan replaces Vijay Shankar. For Delhi, Rovman Powell makes way for Anrich Nortje, while Abishek Porel gets his maiden DC cap.

Pandya: Losing Kane, we are gutted as a team but more for him. We have to move on and Miller comes back for Kane, and Sai Sudharsan comes in for Vijay Shankar. We didn't play our best cricket, but we still won in the first game. We just tried to keep things simple. That's something we are focusing on.

Warner: Looks like a nice wicket. We have to come out with a positive intent and put up a good score. [Homeground] Its awesome and hopefully we can put a good score for the crowd. Rovman is out. Abiskeh Porel comes on. Having another left-hander is crucial . There have neem a few harsh calls. We need to bat better, bowl better and field better than the opposition.

Toss in ten minutes. Changes expected in both sides. Both Miller and Nortje are warming up. Titans will have to replace Williamson who has been ruled out of the IPL with a right knee injury he had sustained in the opening game of the tournament. He has head back home for further assessment.

Satyajeet : "There is a certain Australian who is commentating in this IPL. He is a potential replacement for KW "

Dave: "Reeza Hendricks as Kane's replacement. He is in red hot form. "

Glanny: "Travid Head should be a suitable option. Can be used at the top or as an floater. Has recent experience on Indian pitches and can bowl a few handy overs in desperate situations. "

Here's Aaron Finch with his pitch report: The dimensions are 64 metres either side and 70 metres down the ground. It is the centre wicket. Not a blade of grass when the Test was played here, but there is a nice even covering of grass. Unbelievably flat wicket and I expect there to be a little more seam and carry for the fast bowlers. There are a couple of parts on the wicket that are very dry, they are still hard, though and they will not have a huge influence. 165 is the average score here. The trend so far in the IPL has been to chase, but personally, I would not be against batting first, putting a big total and then put pressure on the teams.

6.50pm In other news, KKR's Shreyas Iyer and RCB's Rajat Patidar have been ruled out of IPL 2023. Iyer will undergo surgery on his injured back and will therefore miss the entire 2023 IPL, and the World Test Championship (WTC) final in June. Patidar has been ruled out because of a heel injury.

Nirmal: "@Kataria: Hold our Hello says Buttler and Jaiswal"

Bhavin: "Ashish - have any potential Kane Williamson replacements been lined up by Gujarat?" Nothing at the moment. What are the potential options? Let us know in the comments.

6.45pm David Miller and Anrich Nortje have been spotted on the outfield, smiling away. Miller should come in straight for Kane Williamson, you'd expect. Nortje's pace should come handy on this Delhi surface. But who does he replace is the question.

Kataria: "@Vasanth: Hello Says Virat and Faf!"

Vasanth: "@Shrikant: Hello says Ruturaj and Conway"

6.40pm There was a Test match played between India and Australia not long back at this venue, one that saw the ball turning square from the first session and collapses galore. Certainly, the surface for this game will be expected to be much better for batters. Both sides are also waiting to see if their South Africans will be available: David Miller, Lungi Ngidi and Anrich Nortje were on the same flights from Johannesburg to Delhi, via Dubai. All this and more, in Matt Roller's preview.

Shrikant: "Mark my words - Warner and Shaw will be the most successful opening pair in this IPL "

6.30pm Hello and welcome to Match No.7 of IPL 2023, where we have Delhi Capitals taking on Gujarat Titans as Delhi return to their home territory. Both teams have had contrasting starts to their campaign. While Titans got the better of Chennai Super Kings by five wickets in the opener, Capitals were decimated by Mark Wood's fiery five-for in Lucknow. Can Capitals stage a comeback at home or will the defending champions continue their winning spree? This is Ashish Pant, and S Sudarshanan will soon join me as we bring to you all the updates from the Arun Jaitley Stadium.

9.21pm A middling total at best from Delhi, but they have something and the surface has looked spicy. They finish on 162 for 8, the lowest total so far in the IPL for a team batting first. Delhi's batters did not have the best of days. None of them could get in, bar maybe Axar Patel who scored 36 off 22 balls. David Warner was lucky for his 32-ball 37 while Sarfaraz had a tough day as he scored 30 off 34. The Titans bowlers were on the mark all through the innings. There was a lot of movement available early on, that caused a few extras, but the bowlers came back well. Mohammed Shami and Rashid Khan picked three wickets apiece. Two wins in two, then, for defending champs Titans! That's all we have for you. Hope you enjoyed our coverage. On behalf of Thilak, Ashish, this is Sudarshanan signing off. Good night, take care!

11:38pm Time for the presentation.

Hardik Pandya, Titans captain: "It was little funny at the start. We didn't know what was happening but something was happening. We gave away 15-20 runs more in the powerplay. [On his captaincy] It is my instinct. I like to back myself. I'd rather back me and fall down than taking others' decision. I'd rather land the first punch than take the first punch. We tell the boys to enjoy. It will help to take us right decisions and someone takes us through periods when needed. Whatever happens it is okay but be out happy out there and take care of each other. [Sudharsan] He has been batting beautifully. You can see the fruit of his hard work. In two years he will do something big in franchise cricket and hopefully for India."

B Sai Sudharsan, Player of the Match: "Thanks for backing me, a little nervous. First time here. I was thinking about what has to be done right, was not under pressure. It was a little bit low and skidding low. My turn was to take the game deep. It was about weathering the storm early on, because it was seaming early on."

Sampath Bandarupalli has looked at David Miller's numbers for Gujarat Titans in run-chases: 351 runs at a strike rate of 155!

David Miller, Titans batter: "Didn't have time to get jeglagged. We were within range. It was a matter of three sixes or four fours. But a lot can happen if we leave it for too late. We started well last year, got good momentum. We got mature cricketers in the middle order. Good start gives us a good platform. Very relaxed environment on and off the field."

David Warner, Capitals captain: "It swung more than I anticipated. Losing wickets in the powerplay can be struggle. They showed how to adapt to the situation and it is a learning for us. We have got six more games here and anticipate the swing upfront. They bowled extremely well. We were in the game but Sai batted extremely well and David Miller took it away. [On not using Axar Patel's bowling] Just purely because of the wicket and the match-ups. We thought Kuldeep would be effective and had Mitch Marsh."

Deep: "Very impressed with Sai's batting. I sometimes feel India can play with 2 teams and still be competitive in world cricket. Guys like Rutu, Sai. Future looks very bright"

Samrat Ahuja: "Tenth win chasing in the IPL out of 11 games! : one match they lost, was to Mumbai..chasing only 8 runs in last over and managed to lose!! Should have been a perfect record!"

Rutvik: "The MoM should be Alzarri Joseph imo. DC never recovered from the shock of losing Warner and Roussouw on consecutive bowls. They couldn't capitalize even though they still had 4 more batters and a lot more overs." Fair shout

Gyan : "IPL has started to look more exciting but boring as well same time. Impact player is interesting but 4 hours every match is boring. "

Mustafa Moudi : "Fun Fact: RR and now GT are the only sides to win matches on away venue this season. The Finalists from the last season are continuing exactly from where they left !!"

11:22pm Titans register their tenth win chasing in the IPL out of 11 games! And this has been a canter. The handshakes and hugs in the dugout are as relaxed as they could be. And it is a win that was designed mainly by their bowlers. Rashid and Shami picked up three wickets apiece with Joseph making his presence felt with a couple. Capitals could only puff to 162 and that was hardly going to challenge this Titans line-up. Despite losing three wickets inside the powerplay, Titans never stopped attacking and put up 54. The young and impressive Sai Sudharsan ensured that Titans get home without major hiccups.

7.29 pm The players are out. Prabhsimran on strike to face Boult.

We're not too far off from the start of play. But how long until the match finishes? Matches which now regularly stretch beyond four hours have become a source of frustration for some fans and observers. Sidharth Monga has his say on the issue of the lengthy duration of IPL matches, and franchise T20 games in general across all leagues, with prolonged endings which are starting to become unwieldy.

Punjab subs: Atharva Taide, Harpreet Bhatia, Matthew Short, Mohit Rathee, Rishi Dhawan

7.02 pm The news from the middle is that Rajasthan Royals have won the toss and will bowl first.

Rajasthan are fielding an unchanged XI. Punjab are fielding the same batting XI they used in their first match, reflecting the Impact Player swap.

Punjab Kings XI: 1 Shikhar Dhawan (capt.), 2 Prabhsimran Singh (wk), 3 Bhanuka Rajapaksa, 4 Sikandar Raza, 5 Jitesh Sharma, 6 Shahrukh Khan, 7 Sam Curran, 8 Harpreet Brar, 9 Nathan Ellis, 10 Rahul Chahar, 11 Arshdeep Singh

A couple of new faces, the message is that the consistency around the dressing room is same. We appreciate it is a long tournament, nice to get one under our belt. [Secret to his first-over wickets] You've probably jinxed it! I am clear in my game plan - pitch it up and try and get early wickets."

6.30 pm Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of tonight's 2023 Indian Premier League encounter between Rajasthan Royals and Punjab Kings. I'm Peter Della Penna to take you through all of the action. To set the scene, check out Sreshth Shah's match preview.

Both teams enter today having won their initial matches this season. Rajasthan defeated Sunrisers by 72 runs while Punjab defeated KKR by 7 runs on DLS in a rain-shortened affair. postText:
11.44 pm And so after four hours and 14 minutes.... your winner is the Punjab Kings by five runs. Rajasthan really gave this match away with a series of strategic blunders. The total was well within their reach, especially after conceding just seven runs off the 20th over in the first innings. But they bungled a number of things starting with the batting order followed by two reviews lost - not on lbw decisions but on attempted reversals of legal deliveries into wides/no balls.

Rajasthan captain Sanju Samson: "I think it was a really good track to bat on especially in the Powerplay. There was not much movement. Their batsmen came with a really positive mindset and their momentum carried on with that. Our bowlers tried varying their lengths and speed. It's a high scoring venue but we did reasonably good job pulling them back after the Powerplay start they got. [On sending Ashwin in to open] Jos was not fit. He was getting stitches for his finger after the catch. The thinking was with Padikkal, they have two spinners, a left-arm and a leggie, and we wanted a lefty out there in the middle overs. [On Jurel] It's really a pleasure. He has been with us for the last two seasons. Lots and lots of work has gone behind him. We all are really happy. When you come to the IPL, it's a one-week camp before the IPL starts but these guys put in 5 weeks of work coming to our academy facing thousands of balls. We're happy to have a batsman like that in our team. Dew, I was expecting it come in the second half of the game but it was right there in the first innings. It was a high scoring game and I think we'll be a bit more prepared in the next game."

Punjab allrounder Sam Curran: "[On the final over] I think when it comes to those situations, you know if you nail your yorker, you'll be okay. Some days it works and some days it won't but luckily it was our day. I was trying to get our ball changed because it was like soap. I don't really understand why they got their ball changed but we can't. [On Prabhsimran] He's been amazing. I was with him at Punjab four years ago. He was very young and is still young. The team got off to a great start. Hopefully it's the start of a great campaign for him and the runs keep coming because he's an amazing player. The way we were playing, I was happy sitting in the dugout because the boys were playing beautifully. All that matters is that we won. [On bowling with a wet ball] It's amazingly hard. You try to train by dipping balls in water. It's incredibly hard to hold the seam. You try to bowl cross seam but it's not a natural ball to bowl a yorker cross seam. It's extremely tough but everyone has to do it so there's no real complaining. We just have to keep getting better because the batters are getting better, the bowlers are getting better and that's why this tournament is the best in the world."

Punjab Kings captain Shikhar Dhawan: "There were some nervous moments but I was keeping my calm and the same with the bowlers. There was a lot of dew. The bowlers did a great job. I was happy with the score we put up. They bowled well and bowled very good yorkers. [Asked what was the turning point in the game] My switch hits? [Laughs] Scoring 197 and then my bowlers coming and getting early wickets and keeping the pressure on and then Nathan came on and got wickets. We never let the game get out of our hands. There were some moments that were hard but I think it was a great team effort. These two matches, we've gotten a great start playing well and I'm doing my best to increase my strike rate. The wicket brings momentum back quickly. This year we have a deep batting lineup so we keep momentum going hitting boundaries and put pressure on the other team. You have to respect that the other team has come to play and will bowl some good overs as well but we have to keep the intent and aggression going."

Player of the Match is Nathan Ellis for his 4 for 30, including the wickets of Buttler and Samson: "It's one of those days where you can potentially bowl not your best and get rewards. There's some other guys in the team who probably deserve some rewards, but just stoked to get the win in another tight one with Rajasthan. To me it's just ball-by-ball. Each ball is a moment. I don't want to get too swept up in one over's time, five overs' time, ten overs' time. It's more about that ball's time. T20 is getting to the point where every ball counts and staying in the moment is key. Easier said than done, especially in a game like tonight. When I was bowling in the back end, I was really trying to focus on drying the ball - because it was so wet - and two to get my execution right so for me it was cross seam. I was calculating the best percentage ball for me in that time and to restrict runs. I'm stoked and really happy for Sam to get us over the line."

That's it for our live coverage of tonight's game where I can confirm that the PUNJAB KINGS won by five runs. Come back tomorrow (or is it today? It's now 12:12 am in India with the post-match presentation ending after midnight) for some more IPL action. Until then, take care!

7pm Time for the toss. The match referee seems to have misheard the call. Sanjay Manjrekar, the commentator conducting the toss, helps out. So eventually Faf du Plessis has won the toss, and RCB will be chasing. As expected, David Willey comes in for Reece Topley.

6.40pm Let's jump straight to team news. RCB have got off to a good start with a win in their first match, but have since received news that Rajat Patidar is ruled out of the season. Josh Hazlewood and Wanindu Hasaranga are yet to join the squad, and Reece Topley injured himself too. David Willey should take Topley's place for this match.

postText:
A one-sided game in what was Eden Gardens' first IPL match in four years. KKR cruised to an 81-run win after hitting back from a position where everyone except Thakur had given up. Have a read of Monga's report from today's play, which included RCB collapsing from 44 for 0 to 61 for 5. That's it from us tonight, as this is Himanshu signing off on behalf of Raghav, Thilak and Monga! Good night.

Shardul Thakur is the Player of the Match for his match-turning 68 off 29: "Even I don't know where it came from! Looking at the scorecard, everyone would have said we were struggling. But your subconscious mind takes over. You also have to have skills to do that at the higher level, but we also work hard in the nets. Coaching staff do the throwdowns, and give us the option of range-hitting. And you know the pitches; they always suit the batsmen, don't they? Suyash bowled exceptionally well, and we know the quality Sunil and Varun have. They have fun, take wickets. This was a perfect day"

KKR captain Nitish Rana: "If you look at the last match, there were positives; we were in the game even after seven down. Even today, we collapsed, and credit to Gurbaz. And it was an unbelievable innings from Shardul Thakur! People will talk about Shardul, but Rinku held one end up, as we had planned. We had always planned not to give RCB batters pace in the middle overs. Suyash, playing his first match, bowled brilliant balls to such batters. Not even we have got to know him so far! He backs himself. It was always our plan to add him if we needed a third spinner."

Time for the presentations

Shrikant : "23 extras by RCB was another crime committed "

KKR coach Chandrakant Pandit: "It's a good win. Boys have shown the character. Looking at the initial stage, having lost wickets, and coming back to get 200-plus. We just expected the pitch to help the spinners. But you require enough runs. Shardul and Rinku counterattacked the opposition. We have seen him (Suyash) at trial matches. He is very quick in the air, and it's very tough to pick him. It's just the inexperience; but he showed a fighting attitude."

RCB captain Faf du Plessis after the loss: "We had it set up there in the 12th or 13th over... It was probably 20-25 runs too much. Shardul played well. Their legspinners got on top of us. It was still a good wicket... but the nature of mystery spinners is that they get wickets. They put the squeeze on us. We were pretty average with the bat. You learn lessons. Two or three days ago, you played brilliant cricket. It got away from us."

Afeef: "Shardul's knock will remain one of the best knocks when this season ends"

11.09pm Hardly a challenge here from the Royal Challengers. KKR were 89 for 5 in the 12th over of their innings - including having Russell back in the hut - but Thakur turned the screw thereon, and how! Strangely, only three KKR batters entered double figures, but you can imagine the impact they had as their side ended at 204. Add to that not one, not two, but three mystery spinners: four wickets for Varun, three for debutant Suyash and two for Narine, and that was it. Hang around for the presentation formalities.

7.30pm Mayank Agarwal and Anmolpreet Singh are in the middle. Kyle Mayers, the specialist first-over bowler, will open the bowling. No slip - Thilak reminds me Mayers bowls inswing predominantly.

Gul: "Why was Abishek dropped? Is he also unwell? I dont see any other reason for dropping him :|" --- Think since they needed a keeper, they replaced Abhishek with Anmolpreet.

Prakash: "Finally some innovative use of the impact sub rule. SRH have kept all 3 options open( batter, allrounder or bowler) depending on match situation."

Amit: "Am I the only one confused here? SRH don't have a keeper, unless they sub Klassen" --- Anmolpreet Singh can sort of keep.

Chandan: "They will Substitute Klassen in place of Anmolpreet or Agarwal later in this innings...(that's the only logical way I see his inclusion as Substitute)" --- And if they need a batter for just one or two overs, they can bring in Jansen as well.

Hari: "So Naveen-ul-haq gets the cap but he is not there in the playing XI?" --- Yeah, a bit strange. Maybe he was in bat-first XI - just my guess. I don't think even that makes much sense.

Mannan: "I don't seem to comprehend this SRH lineup. Why use Klaasen as specialist keeper? This is just wastage of impact player rule. Klaasen should've been included in the first innings in the place of Natarajan and Natarajan should've been used as an impact sub for Anmolpreet" --- I think they will call up Klaasen if they collapse, else they get an extra bowler in Jansen or Farooqi in the second innings.

So after all that build-up, there's no de Kock. And SRH have only three overseas players in their XI. So expect one of Klaasen, Farooqi and Jansen to come in as an Impact Player at some stage.

Here are the playing XIs:

Sunrisers Hyderabad: 1 Mayank Agarwal, 2 Anmolpreet Singh (wk), 3 Rahul Tripathi, 4 Aiden Markram (capt), 5 Harry Brook, 6 Washington Sundar, 7 Abdul Samad, 8 Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 9 T Natarajan, 10 Umran Malik, 11 Adil Rashid

Substitues: Ayush Badoni, Swapnil Singh, Daneil Sams, Prerak Mankad, Avesh Khan

7.00pm Sunrisers have won the toss and opted to bat first. "The wicket looks quite dry," says Markram. "Hopefully, we can put up a good total. Everyone seems in good spirits and full of energy. Since we are batting first, Anmolpreet Singh will start."

"Even during the last game I didn't expect it to be a high-scoring one," KL Rahul says. "We will assess the conditions and try to do our best. Wood is down with flu, so he misses out. Avesh injured himself in the last game, so he is taking a break."

6.55pm Pitch Report: We have got a black-soil pitch tonight, which means less pace and bounce as compared to the last game that was played on a red-soil pitch. We are not expecting much dew either, says Simon Katich. He says batting first could be the better option.

6.50pm Looks like LSG have handed caps to Romario Shepherd and Naveen-ul-Haq. I am guessing someone is not fit 100%. Heinrich Klaasen too seems to have got his SRH cap, which was more or less obvious. Does that mean Glenn Phillips sit out?

IPL Super Selec: "Sundar would love to see two lefties open. That would jumpstart his career after the injury hiatus"

6.45pm In the small window Mayers had before Quinton de Kock's arrival, he did everything he could to make it extremely hard for Lucknow Super Giants to drop him. Deivarayan Muthu charts his journey.

If yes, for whom do they come in for? While we wait for the toss, you can read our match preview here.

RajatMaheshwari: "The only option LSG have if they want to play QDK is to drop Stoinis...he hasn't gotten away in both the matches and hasn't bowled either. With contributions from Mayers and Pooran, I don't see it any other way!"

Tauqeer: "Very simple , drop Stoins and let Rahul bat at No 3. That would be the deadliest opening pair of this year's IPL."

6.30pm S16E10. It's Lucknow Super Giants taking on Sunrisers Hyderabad at Ekana Cricket Stadium. Both teams are coming off a defeat but have also been bolstered by the availability of their South Africans players. Quinton de Kock is back for LSG, and have given them a happy headache. Do they drop Mayers, who has smashed two half-centuries in two games. Or do they leave out one of Stoinis or Pooran? And if both de Kock and Mayers play, who should open? Do let us know what you think.

So LSG are now table toppers, well clear of both GT and PBKS on net run rate, although having played a game more than both. They produced a pitch that ended up in their favour today, as Pandya and Amit Mishra turned the screws. That's it from us tonight, as this is Himanshu signing off on behalf of Hemant and Thilak!

Krunal Pandya is the Player of the Match: "Very good day at the office. Both [wickets and runs] pleased me. Everything was special today. [SRH] having more right-handers, I knew I was going to bowl early. Once you have clarity, things automatically fall into place. Last four or five months I took a break from cricket. I just worked on my skills, especially on bowling. Worked on my action... wanted to get that arm ball going. Pretty much enjoying batting. Trying to recollect my first few years in IPL where I was batting at No. 4 for Mumbai. I am absolutely okay with any track!"

LSG captain KL Rahul: "[We realised] yesterday how the wicket was going to play! We knew what we were getting into. We saw in the first couple of overs: when Jaydev bowled a few cutters, they were gripping. I knew KP's better in the powerplay. Both [wins] were hard work... had different challenges. We have been here for a few weeks. Just a general chat with the batsmen; each person plays differently."

Time for the presentations

Amit Mishra, who took 2 for 23 for LSG: "Feeling good. I've done a lot of hard work, especially in fielding. That's my bowling style (bowling slower). I was just trying to vary my pace, and bowl slower. Whatever I can do, I'm doing in the fielding! I got some time on that (the catch)! The red soil has little bounce and less spin; black soil was slower and lower, though not turning much"

SRH captain Aiden Markram after the loss: "Not enough. That 150-160 mark, and we would have been in the game. We realised it wasn't going to be a great wicket for batting... happy to fight it out and scratch away. Good effort [with the ball]. They tried hard, and fought. It's a new game of cricket starting for us on Sunday."

NethraReya: "@Vamsi: you guys jinx even the revenue Gods!!" --- No one is spared here when it comes to a jinx

10.49pm A slow, low pitch where SRH decided to bat first, and it didn't work out. Dew wasn't expected to play a role, and it didn't; in the end, it turned out to be a low-scorer on a track where the ball gripped and turned. The slower you went, the more effective you happened to be. Pandya's all-round show propelled LSG to first restrict SRH to 121, and then keep tickling along in the chase. Hang around for the presentations.

postText:
5.14 pm Well how about that, an innings that clocks in 16 minutes under two hours. We might be in for a match that goes under the four-hour mark today. Woo hoo! Jaiswal was a whirling dervish in the first third of the innings. But after he got out, the innings lost momentum quite badly even though Buttler was at the crease for the majority of the way. He just wasn't getting enough of the strike. Somehow Rajasthan have fallen short of 200. A large amount of credit has to go to the Delhi spinners for reeling in the run rate. This feels like a below par total. We'll see if that is indeed the case when the Delhi chase gets underway. Stay with us for the start of the reply coming up shortly.

Here's Jos Buttler at the innings break: "I cut my finger in the last game, but we've got a good doc here with a few stitches and I actually felt fine to play. [Buttler is given the orange cap as the new scoring leader this season] It's obviously nice to wear. Just glad to start the season well and get up and running. I think we've got a decent score on the board. It's obviously a really good batting wicket with a fast outfield so we'll have to bowl well to defend this. I think in the Powerplay it was a fantastic wicket. Maybe as the ball got a little bit older, the bounce got a little bit lower. There was a little period where we lost a couple of wickets and the two spinners tied us down a little bit. But obviously with Ashwin and Chahal in our team, hopefully they can do the same job for us. It's certainly an option. All the guys are comfortable to bowl with the new ball if they have to. Trent Boult has been really good for us at the start. If we can control the Powerplay as best as we can - I expect Delhi to be really aggressive in the first six overs as they saw the rhythm of our innings - maybe it got a little bit harder outside of the Powerplay."

preText:
7.30pm Kishan walks out to open the batting along with his captain Rohit. Chahar has the new ball for CSK. Can he find some early swing? He will be backed up by two slips. Chahar will operate from over the wicket

Apoorv: "MI had always been good at auction strategy until they decided in 2022 to go crazy for Ishan and Archer. Ishan was never consistent and Archer never consistently fit. They let go the ever consistent QDK and Boult, which was a blunder. MI bowling has looked way below every other team since 1st match of IPL 2022."

7.20pm Sisanda Magala is a death-bowling specialist from SA. He was particularly impressive for Sunrisers Eastern Cape in the SA20. Their analyst Gaurav Sundararaman rates him very highly. Ahead of SA20, Magala broke Jordan Hermann's toe with a yorker, according to former SA analyst Prasanna Agoram who was speaking to R Ashwin on his Youtube channel about Magala. So watch out for those killer yorkers from Sisi.

MI XI: 1 Ishan Kishan (wk), 2 Rohit Sharma (capt), 3 Cameron Green, 4 Tilak Varma, 5 Suryakumar Yadav, 6 Tristan Stubbs, 7 Tim David, 8 Arshad Khan, 9 Hrithik Shokeen, 10 Piyush Chawla, 11 Jason Behrendorff

Subs: Ramandeep Singh, Sandeep Warrier, Arjun Tendulkar, Kumar Karthikeya, Nehal Wadhera

CSK XI: 1 Devon Conway, 2 Ruturaj Gaikwad, 3 Ajinkya Rahane, 4 Ravindra Jadeja, 5 Shivam Dube, 6 MS Dhoni (capt&wk), 7 Dwaine Pretorius, 8 Deepak Chahar, 9 Mitchell Santner, 10 Sisanda Magala, 11 Tushar Deshpande

Subs: Rajvardhan Hangargekar, Ambati Rayudu, Shaik Rasheed, Akash Singh, Subhranshu Senapati

ViragS: "Mumbai's problem goes beyond just Bumrah and Archer. They let Boult go which was a mistake, they lost Pandya brothers in the reshuffle which was a serious blow, combine that with the fact that Rohit, Ishaan and SKY are seriously out of form.. they look like the weakest unit out there. "

Sam: "Cam Green could open with Kishan to maximise his value..."

Jayant Isswani : "CSK should play Pretorius at number 3. He can tonk the ball pretty well!"

Mustafa Moudi : "No Pollard , No Bravo, No Stokes, No Moeen, No Archer.... This El Clasico , we are going to miss too many Overseas Players !!"

7pm Dhoni walks out for the toss along with Rohit. CSK win the toss and opt to chase. Stokes and Moeen are out for CSK. Rahane makes his IPL debut for them, as does Sisi Magala. No Archer for MI.

Dhoni: One of the most memorable venues. Not only because of the 2011 win but the reception we got after the 2007 T20 World Cup. We've had some injury concerns. Stokes has an injury. Mo is not well and in their place we've got Rahane and Pretorius. Other than that, same team.

Rohit: We would've fielded as well. It's a good pitch to bat and will be a good contest between bat and ball. The mood has been upbeat and hopefully we can correct the things we didn't do in Bangalore. One injury - not an injury but just a precaution - Jofra is not playing, but we've got other guys to do the job for us. Great feeling to be back at the Wankhede.

6.40pm Roller sets up the scene from Mumbai: "The Wankhede is starting to fill up, with a fair few yellow shirts in amongst the blue. Jofra Archer is doing some fitness drills, running from one side of the ground to the other, and looks unlikely to play.

Pretorius and Santner are both marking their runs. Haven't seen Stokes yet. Stokes is here, but sitting down away from the team. Told Sky he had bowled "pain-free" against Lucknow but some reports over the last 24 hours that he has been struggling with a sore heel.

Right, that's all from us from today's game. A commanding win for Chennai Super Kings and another deflating loss for Mumbai. A double-header comes to a close, but we will be back again for the two games tomorrow. Till then, this is me Ashish Pant, signing off on behalf of Deiva, Thilak and Ranjith. Good night!

Ravindra Jadeja is the Player of the Match: When we were bowling, the wicket was spinning. Me and Mitch [Santner] just spoke and looked to bowl in good areas. They have power hitters, so we could have gone for runs. The wickets here plays differently everytime. [On bowling with Santner] Whoever bowls at the start, will let each other about the tactics. We keep talking to each other.

First up, here's MS Dhoni who comes in to a rousing reception: It feels good, we lost Deepak [Chahar] in our first over. [Sisanda] Magala it was the first game. Was a bit of an issue to shuffle the bowler. But the spinners bowled really well. It was not turning much after the first six overs. It w as bit two-paced after that. The spinners were able to use that well later. Magala came back well, Pretorius was so good. It was a good bowling effort, despite losing our premier bowler. [On Tushar Deshpande] We believe in him. When you are new, you have a different sort of pressure. He had a very good domestic season, and we have been talking to him about his execution. He bowled a lot of no-balls, last two matches but is improving, The delivery he got Rohit out, was a beauty. [On Rahane] We spoke right at the start and he was like what are you looking for me and I told him what I had in mind. He is not someone who will consistently hit sixes but he is very sound technically. I was very happy with the way he batted. All the games are important. The first target is to win an away game and get to the qualifier. Important to look at the problem in front of you, get wins and gather points.

Time for the presentation

Rahane on his innings: Really enjoyed it. I just got to know before the toss that I am playing. Unfortunately, Moeen was unwell. I had a good domestic season and was batting well in the nets. I was just trying to play good cricketing shots, and not slog it over. It is all about maintaining your shape. You want to prepare mentally well, IPL is a very long tournament, and it all about staying positive and knowing your game. Mahi [MS Dhoni] bhai and Flem [Stephen Fleming] have given the freedom to other players. I was just told to focus on my strengths and focus on preparation. I love playing at the Wankhede, I know the ground well. Have not played a Test here, yet.

Ajinkya Rahane hands the Orange Cap to Ruturaj Gaikwad.

Rohit Sharma: We lost our way in the middle. Did not capitalise on the start. It was a good pitch, we were 30-40 runs short in the middle. Credit to their spinners, they bowled well, kept us under pressure and we did not respond well. We need to try different things, need to attack, need to be brave. We have a couple of guys who are young into the IPL. Gotta give some time to them. It will take time, but we need to back them up and show enough trust in their ability. The senior guys need to step up, starting with me. We know the nature of IPL. We need to get some momentum, and if you don't, it is going to be tough. Just two games, not all is lost, but the senior guys need to step up with the bat. That's the nature of the tournament. If you win, you can win on the trot. If you lose, it will hamper the momentum. We wanted to do a lot of things right. We have not been able to execute the things that we are speaking about in the change room. We have to do those things right. We know we had a very disappointing last season. You always start afresh. When we won the five trophies, we did not think about it. Every opposition is quality and you have to be the best to defeat them. These two games have happened now, you can't change. We have to learn and be more brave in doing stuff out in the field.

10.53pm That was domination personified by Chennai Super Kings who have scored a relatively easy win on Mumbai's home turf. Mumbai Indians got a good start in the powerplay in the first innings, but once Rohit Sharma fell, it all went downhill for them. The spinners strangled them in the middle overs as they finished on 157 for 8. Jason Behrendorff struck early, sending back Devon Conway. But, Ajinkya Rahane on CSK debut, was just sublime. He did not play a shot in anger, yet raced to 61 off 27 balls, in the process also scoring the fastest fifty of IPL 2023. Gaikwad once again remained unbeaten on 40, while he got good support from Shivam Dube and later, Ambati Rayudu. All in all, a complete performance from CSK, who move to fourth position on the points table.

(On adjusting from Test to T20s) It's all about fine-tuning your mind, getting some practice and understanding your role. All of these factors combined is what matters. Let's see what the conditions have in store for us. The sun is out, and there is a slight breeze. A fresh pitch will be used today and the square boundaries are relatively equidistant, with 62m and 65m boundaries on either side. Matthew Hayden reckons it is a beautiful batting surface, saying there is sheen on the surface and no real indentations to worry about. Hayden expects the pacers to play a big role, while Rohan Gavaskar thinks the spinners could be in the game a little more.

Both teams come into this game on the back of wins. The Titans were too strong for the Delhi Capitals, while the Knight Riders blew RCB away at Eden Gardens on Thursday. Such is the IPL that a win today for KKR will take them level on points with the Titans. A Titans victory, though, would ensure a spot at the top of the table, at least until the Punjab Kings' match against the Sunrisers Hyderabad later in the day.

Plenty of interesting match-ups along the way. Last season, these sides faced each other just once, with Gujarat defending a score of 156 at the DY Patil Stadium. Andre Russell, though, was one of the few bright spots for KKR that day. With the Jamaican not having set this campaign alight yet, KKR would hope that he can recreate something similar.

Hardik Pandya also has an excellent personal record against KKR. While his teammates have hit the ground running, he is yet to contribute significantly with the bat. Considering how strong GT look elsewhere, this is perhaps the last thing they would want to check off their bucket list.

7:48pm Okay, that will be a wrap from us for this game, and what a game it was. Arguably one of the best the IPL has seen all these years, and we hope you enjoyed our coverage just as much as we enjoyed bringing it to you. The action, though, does not stop. SRH have gotten off to an excellent start against PBKS in the evening game. Do hop over to our coverage for that game too. Until next time, this is me (Shashwat) signing off on behalf of Ranjith, Thilak and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo! Goodbye and take care!

Rinku Singh, Player of the Match: I had belief that I can do this. Rana bhai said to keep belief and to bat till the end, then we will see what happens. (On the single) I was just trying to hit sixes. (Umesh) Bhaiya was asking me not to think much and just play the ball. I was not thinking a lot, was just reacting to the ball. It kept coming out of the middle, I had belief and it came off in the end.

Nitish Rana, Kolkata Knight Riders captain: We had belief because Rinku had done something similar last year, although we did not win. After the second six, we started to believe more because Yash Dayal was also not executing well. You win one out of a hundred matches this way. We were bowling well for 18 overs but did not bowl well towards the end. Same in the batting department where we allowed Rashid and GT back into the game. This result, though, is only down to Rinku and his brilliance. People asked me why Rinku does not play a bigger role. If this is his secondary role, then imagine what he can do in a primary role. I do not have words to describe Rinku's innings.

Venkatesh Iyer: It was a nail-biting finish and extremely happy with the way we won. Our coach has maintained that we can score 200 from any position. Tonight was another example that we will never give up as a team. The wicket was quite good to bat and I was just trying to execute my plans. When the target is 200, you cannot have silent overs. Me and Nitish had a nice partnership and that set the tone. We lost wickets then but thankfully Lord Rinku saved the day. He is a world-class bowler. We still felt we could win the game, though, and that we could chase anything. This teaches us a lesson that we should not give up until the last ball. It will be a great morale-boost for us. Winning is something we want to create a habit of. The first game, we were a little unlucky. I am really not surprised that we have scored 200 in these last two games because of the role clarity that has been given to us. I have not been in great form but tonight, I just wanted to go out there and execute my plan of playing late. When the bounce is good, you tend to hang back and use the pace. Their bowlers were quick so I tried to use their pace and it worked to my advantage.

Rashid Khan, Gujarat Titans captain: A tough game for us, especially as a captain. That is what T20 is all about, it is about entertainment. Same things happened with us last year when we were on the winning side. A good game of cricket and hopefully the fans would have liked it. (Message in the final over) It was more about bowling the ball that he was comfortable with. Rinku played some unbelievable shots. He tried his best deliveries but it did not work. Credit goes to the batter the way he finished. (On his hat-trick) Just keep it simple. Hit the right area consistently. If you miss your lengths, you saw what happened. As a bowler, I am always trying my best to hit the right areas. (On the score and if he is happy with how they played) We got what we wanted. We wanted 190-plus and we got more than 200. We had enough runs to defend but in T20s, sometimes, 250 is not enough to defend. Lots of things for us to learn and we have to take positives out of this game and come back stronger. Chin up, keep smiling and it was a bad day for us as a bowling unit. Next game, we try our best to come back stronger. (On the new Impact Player rule) It is good, something new happening in the format. It makes you mature and I feel it is very good for the game of cricket.

7:22pm Phew, let me catch my breath. That game ebbed, flowed and it seemed that Gujarat would win it, until....Rinku had other ideas. He had 28 to get off the final five balls and hit five massive sixes, spread across the ground and with the sort of conviction expected from a seasoned international cricketer. That it came after a Rashid hat-trick, which threatened to tilt the game on its head, only makes it even more special, especially if you are a KKR fun.

Gujarat would be gutted with how the last few balls panned out. Dayal bowled three full tosses, two drag-downs and was punished. It has taken the sheen off what was otherwise another brilliant Joseph display, and an equally special Vijay Shankar batting performance but tonight belongs to Rinku Singh and KKR.

7.21 pm Welcome to those of you just joining us from the conclusion of one of the most extraordinary finishes in IPL history. KKR needed 28 off 5 balls to win and Rinku Singh smashed five consecutive sixes to beat the defending champion Gujarat Titans. That came after a Rashid Khan hat-trick.

Anish: "Rinku Singh show was amazing in first match." It's gonna be hard to match what he did in the night match here, but these two teams will try.

Punjab Kings XI: 1 Shikhar Dhawan (capt.), 2 Prabhsimran Singh (wk), 3 Matthew Short, 4 Sam Curran, 5 Jitesh Sharma, 6 Shahrukh Khan, 7 Harpreet Brar, 8 Rahul Chahar, 9 Nathan Ellis, 10 Mohit Rathee, 11 Arshdeep Singh.

7.02 pm The news from the middle is that Sunrisers have won the toss and chosen to bowl first. Heinrich Klaassen and Mayank Markande come in as two changes for Sunrisers, though my autocorrect tried very very hard to morph him into a marinade. For Punjab Kings, Matt Short comes in for Bhanuka Rajapaksa.

Shanks: "Mayank Marinade ... autocorrect on overdrive again, or merely dinnertime?" The former, sadly.

You can follow the ball-by-ball commentary for the match in Hindi and in Tamil too.

6.30 pm Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of the second match of today's 2023 Indian Premier League doubleheader as Sunrisers Hyderabad host Punjab Kings. I'm Peter Della Penna to take you through today's action. And for those of you celebrating it, a very Happy Easter!

Sunrisers come into this match struggling in the early part of their 2023 campaign having lost their first two matches. Meanwhile, Punjab Kings have won two from two. Will both teams continue their early season form? Or can Sunrisers break their losing skid? Sidharth Monga lays everything out in his match preview.

Separately, in the video preview for today's match, Tom Moody is keeping the faith in Harry Brook despite a sluggish start to his IPL career.
