9.21 pm What an extraordinary 10th wicket partnership. Rathee was out there for five overs but only faced two deliveries. Shikhar shepherded him expertly. They were in danger of being bowled out for under 100 but have clawed to 143. Can they chase it down? Or will Punjab defend it? Stay tuned for the reply.

For those asking, this is the second highest percentage of runs scored in a completed IPL innings that went 20 overs or ended with a team all out. Shikhar's 69.2% of his team's runs is second only to... Brendon McCullum in the first match in IPL history, blazing 158 out of KKR's total of 222 (71.2%). There's also this gem from stats man Sampath Bandarupalli: "Shikhar Dhawan scored 94.55 % of runs during the 10th wicket stand with Mohit Rathee (52 out of 55). It is the highest contribution in an 50-plus stand in IPL."

Punjab Kings captain Shikhar Dhawan: [Takes the orange cap to cheers from the crowd] I'm glad that the Hyderabad crowd remembers me. It's one of the best I've played. It's good because I played to the end and from the other ends wickets are falling. We made a respectable total and now we can fight for that."

Kiran D.S.: "Shikhar Dhawan's innings reminded me of Ben Stokes's heroics in the epic 2019 Headingley Test. Mohit Rathee did a Jack Leach."

Pranav: "This Shikar's innings will be remembered for decades"

Meanwhile, ace Indian wrestler Vinesh Phogat could have been at the Asian Wrestling Championships in Kazakhstan today. She could have been training in Poland. Instead, she's at the SAI centre in Sonepat where, apart from training with Bajrang Punia, she's put her career on the line for the biggest fight of her life: taking on the Wrestling Federation of India.

postText:
10.59 pm Well how about that. It's not every day that an IPL match ends in under three and a half hours these days, let alone four. Shikhar Dhawan's very special 99 not out winds up in vain. Markande takes four wickets in the field to set up a low total before Tripathi finishes it off.

Punjab Kings captain Shikhar Dhawan: "As a batting unit, we lost too many wickets back to back and couldn't put up a big total on the ground and because of that we lost the game. 175-180 would have been a reasonable score. The wicket looked quite good but it was seaming and swinging. There's lots of learning as a team for us and we're gonna go and analyze where we can get better and come back strong. I'm enjoying the captaincy and leading the side from the front. We've got a great bunch of boys, really enjoying the tournament and taking it day by day."

Sunrisers captain Aiden Markram: "I believe we have a great fan base and they proved it tonight. It was a bit of a rough start but good to get a win in front of them tonight. Not too much panic because it was just the initial phase. We keep encouraging guys to back their options and give them the freedom to do so. [Leaving out Adil Rashid and playing Mayank Markande] It's not a nice move to make but I'm super happy for Mayank tonight. He bowled incredibly well. He got his chance and certainly took it. A lot of hype about him and rightly so. Hopefully it's the start of a great competition for him. [Tripathi's innings and partnership] We all know his ability and he showed it once again tonight. He's always a couple of balls away from doing something special. That's all we keep telling him, is to express himself because he's got all the shots. He got a feel of the wicket and he made it count for us and was there at the end. Hats off to him, it was a great knock. It's very easy [for me] to do it when you've got a guy like Rahul at the other end. It's a great franchise to be a part of. It's the first win for us and hopefully we can take some momentum going forward."

Shikhar Dhawan named Player of the Match in a losing effort ahead of Rahul Tripathi. Hmmm.... "I didn't expect that I'd reach there at the end of the game but I was playing according to the situation, still keeping positive and I hope you were happy with my strike rate... Of course it was disappointing [seeing wickets keep falling] but the way we thought the wicket was going to play, it was playing differently. It was seaming and sometimes keeping low. But that's a learning process for my batting unit and that's fine. When the water is still, you can see through it. Better to be still and see the game. I'm very very grateful for 99 because I never thought I'd reach there so I'm very happy."

That's it for today's coverage. Come back tomorrow for some more IPL action. Enjoy the rest of your Easter Sunday, wherever you are following around the world. I'm Peter Della Penna. Take care!

preText:
Unadkat has the new ball. Kohli on strike. A slip in place.

7.30pm Out come Kohli and du Plessis to get things going. What sounds like deafening cheers take over Chinnaswamy, while the LSG fielders spread out.

Hari: "Just like Arsenal Fans, RCB fans are very very optimistic about their trophy" --- If only it wasn't for a firing Firmino...

LSG: 1 KL Rahul (capt), 2 Kyle Mayers, 3 Deepak Hooda, 4 Marcus Stoinis, 5 Krunal Pandya, 6 Nicholas Pooran (wk), 7 Jaydev Unadkat, 8 Amit Mishra, 9 Avesh Khan, 10 Mark Wood, 11 Ravi Bishnoi. The subs are: Badoni, Swapnil, Gowtham, Mankad and Sams

RCB: 1 Virat Kohli, 2 Faf du Plessis (capt), 3 Mahipal Lomror, 4 Glenn Maxwell, 5 Shahbaz Ahmed, 6 Dinesh Karthik (wk), 7 Anuj Rawat, 8 David Willey, 9 Wayne Parnell, 10 Harshal Patel, 11 Mohammed Siraj. The subs are: Karn, Prabhudessai, Deep, Bracewell and Sonu Yadav

7pm Time for the toss at the vibrant Chinnaswamy... LSG win the toss and bowl. Rahul - of course, him - believes history prefers chasing at the ground. "For me, it's still home," he says. He wants LSG to keep their calm, and announces a few changes. Wood is back, though. Du Plessis was "50-50 on what to do", and has brought in Parnell.

Ritesh: "@Himanshu, you mean we will have Kannada commmentary next year… wow." --- Now that's the spirit... of cricket optimism

Sai: "Himanshu, when are we starting commentary in Kannada?" --- Maybe once RCB win the IPL?

You can also track the game with our ball-by-ball commentary in Hindi and in Tamil.

6.50pm Just 14 matches into the season, the trend of quicker runs - especially in the powerplay - was noted by Matt Roller in his analysis piece. He says it has been a wham-bang season so far. And with the Impact Player rule and flat pitches at the start of the season, batters are attacking more than ever, and it's showing in the numbers.

6.40pm LSG's pace spearhead Mark Wood had missed their last game due to flu, but ESPNcricinfo's expert Ravi Shastri thinks Wood should be handful in Bangalore; at the same time, he thinks RCB are more suited to their home ground. But how do RCB fix their death bowling? Tom Moody and Deep Dasgupta help provide solutions.

We aren't sure about Wanindu Hasaranga's availability yet, and Ashish Pant, our eyes at the ground, says he hasn't spotted him yet. His side RCB need to bounce back after a drubbing back in Kolkata, even as LSG look to build on some momentum of their own. Alagappan Muthu's preview says as much, with today's visiting captain - yeah - being none other than local boy KL Rahul.

6.30pm Kohli, du Plessis and Maxwell on one side. Wood (hopefully), Unadkat and Krunal Pandya on the other. Willey and co with the ball. Rahul - eh, it sounds familiar - and his men with the bat. There are individual battles waiting within the contest between teams as a whole. Welcome to match 15 of the season, as the Chinnaswamy in Bangalore warms up for some action.

9.19pm An innings of three parts: 56 in the first six overs - which was the powerplay - and that was followed by 48 in the next seven. And if you haven't calculated already, RCB smashed 108 off the final seven overs. Du Plessis was on 33 off 31 balls at one stage; he finished on 79* from 46. Maxwell crashed 59 off 29 deliveries, as balls flew all around the small boundaries at the Chinnaswamy. Big score to chase for LSG eventually, with Abhimanyu to bring the second innings to you.

So yes, it's been an uninspiring start to the tournament for these two teams. Delhi have played three, lost three, in increasingly emphatic fashions, while Mumbai are P2 L2, and doing a good impression of the team that finished rock-bottom in 2022. postText:
11.21pm Nortje and Mustafizur put on a death-bowling masterclass, but MI's Impact Player Tim David has taken them home off the last ball. MI drag themselves off the bottom of the standings with their first win this season. "You look at the last three IPL games, amazing," David Warner says. "Wrong end of it today, but the guys were fantastic. Two balls were wrong and that's the game. We did well to bring it back in. Nortje is world-class and that's what we expect from the big fella. Mustafiz too. Timmy David was on the wrong side of it, so I tried to keep it [the throw] at stump-height. I think from the last three games, we've some positives but we shouldn't lose wickets in clumps. Axar should bat in the top four; he got us to a par total."

Rohit, MI captain and Player of the Match: Obviously, winning the game is the most important thing and it's a great feeling to cross the line. We've been working really, really hard and we had camps in Mumbai a couple of weeks before the tournament. To get the result feels really good and we're going to cherish this. We recently played a Test match here and this pitch didn't look different to that and looked dry. So, I thought it was important to get the slower bowlers into the game quickly. We thought 173 was chaseable, and everyone put their hand up. When I went to bat, I wanted to make full use of the powerplay because as the game went on, I thought it would be tough with the couple of quality spinners they had. We tried to create a partnership and good to see Tilak bat with that intent as well. We always knew it would be tough for the new batter to come and bat. Like you said, we got a lot of young guys and it's all about giving them confidence and trust in their ability. We want to have a healthy atmosphere and we don't want to make drastic changes based on results.

Green: Took the helmet off and thankfully it [the two] came off. The only conversation we had was to be busy and thankfully a few came off. There was pressure, but it's so much fun. Getting ten an over - that's why you're here. I knew when the ball came to Tim's end...he's a big boy and can dive.

Phew, that was another tense finish. Thanks for your company and comments. Until next time, this is Deivarayan Muthu signing off on the behalf of Andrew Miller and Thilak Ram. Goodbye and good night.

7pm The whistles are loud and clear as MS Dhoni walks out for the toss alongside Sanju Samson. Dhoni has won the toss and CSK will bowl first.

"It will be slightly on the slower side," Dhoni says. "There could be dew around. Feels good [to lead for 200th time]. The crowd was fantastic. The new stadium is like playing in Switzerland. We have seen cricket change. Feels good to have survived for so long and it's a format we have to keep evolving. Important to get rid of mistakes in the later stages. A few changes - Santner and Pretorius make way for Moeen and Theekshana."

"We would have liked to bat first," says Samson. "Important to keep up the momentum. Always a pleasure to come to Chepauk and play against CSK and Mahi bhai. A few changes with the impact rule - Boult misses out because of a niggle."

6:50pm Trent Boult was seen giving a jolly pep talk in the RR huddle. He's been on song with his first-over wickets and has been bowling extremely well. Another youngster who's really grabbed his opportunities is Dhruv Jurel, who was the wicketkeeper in India's win in the Under-19 Men's World Cup last year. Ashish and Nikhil Sharma explore his story and Jurel's determination to succeed comes through.

6:45pm In the video preview, former India head coach Ravi Shastri believes that CSK will hold the edge over RR at home. He also wasn't happy with India's fast bowlers breaking down repeatedly and aired his views about the same.

Meanwhile, Deivarayan Muthu is soaking in the atmosphere at Chepauk and says: Hello, another humid evening at Chepauk. Thousands of fans wearing Dhoni's No.7 yellow jersey as usual, but there's also a bit of support for Rajasthan Royals, largely because of the presence of R Ashwin, the original son of the soil. Then, there's his captain Sanju Samson who had received the kind of reception that is usually reserved for Dhoni last September at Chepauk. RR also have M Ashwin who had started his IPL career by bowling big-turning wrong'uns to Mike Hussey and Dhoni at the CSK nets. Both the Ashwins are give it a good rip at training now. They had also bowled together at the nets two days out of the game. The black-soil pitch that was rolled out for the ODI series decider between India and Australia is likely to be used again today.

6:40pm Right then! Chepauk may be CSK's home-ground fortress and the men in yellow have a good spin attack to make use of the conditions. But in R Ashwin and Yuzvendra Chahal and more spin options in Adam Zampa and M Ashwin, Sreshth Shah wonders in his preview if Rajasthan Royals could match Super Kings spin for spin.

6:35pm Dhoni is the first player to lead a single team in the IPL for 200 games. There was a small presentation a short while ago with N Srinivasan, his wife Chitra Srinivasan and TNCA head Rupa Gurunath presenting Dhoni with a memento.

Tonight, the Chepauk, will yet again have a festive atmosphere as their favourite son Dhoni will walk out as CSK's captain for the 200th time. preText:
7.27pm All set then. Out come the two Kings openers, Shikhar Dhawan and Prabhsmiran Singh. Hardik Pandya leads his troops out as well. Rashid Khan greets Shikar Dhawan with a handshake. Mohammad Shami to start off with the new ball from over the stumps. Prabhsimran on strike. Two slips waiting for him.

Prashant: "One problem with the Impact player rule is that the batting all-rounds are not getting to bowl. They are playing as pure batsman and their bowling is not being tested."

Rohit: "One's got to feel bad for Yash Dayal. The Rinku Singh show in the last game was a freaky occurrence. To be dropped from the team in the next game doesn't give the young lad much confidence. "

7.20pm Just ten minutes out from the start of the game. Expect some swing early on but with the kind of depth Titans have in their batting unit, Kings should target in excess of 180, here.

Kagiso Rabada is speaking to the host broadcaster: [What's changed] Pretty much the same things, I am trying to improve in certain areas, but otherwise the same old. For me, I expect to bowl at any stage of the game. It all depends on what the coach and captain want of me, and I will just do my best at whatever stage. We have got a few players in form - Shikhar, Prabhsimran as well and we've got the likes of Curran, Nathan Ellis has been doing. Livingstone is just waiting to play, Arshdeep Singh. [On the team] It has shown in the way we have started. We lost the game, but are looking to bounce back.

BeardGuy: "One of the biggest disappointments this IPL has been the complete absence of up-and-coming Indian allrounders. I hope Rahul Tewatia, Vijay Shankar, and Rishi Dhawan shine with both bat and ball this match!"

Playing XI

Punjab Kings: Prabhsimran Singh, Shikhar Dhawan (capt), Matthew Short, Bhanuka Rajapaksa, Jitesh Sharma (wk), Sam Curran, Shahrukh Khan, Harpreet Brar, Kagiso Rabada, Rishi Dhawan, Arshdeep Singh

Subs: Atharva Taide, Rahul Chahar, Sikandar Raza, Gurnoor Brar, Harpreet Bhatia

Gujarat Titans: Wriddhiman Saha (wk), Shubman Gill, Sai Sudharsan, Hardik Pandya (capt), David Miller, Rahul Tewatia, Rashid Khan, Alzarri Joseph, Mohammed Shami, Mohit Sharma, Joshua Little

Subs: Vijay Shankar, Shivam Mavi, Jayant Yadav, Abhinav Manohar, Srikar Bharat

Toss: Shikhar Dhawan has the coin. Hardik Pandya calls correctly and Gujarat Titans will bowl first. Pandya does not remember the changes. Dhawan says they have two changes. Kagiso Rabada comes in for Nathan Ellis, Bhanuka Rajapaksa comes in for Sikandar Raza.

Hardik Pandya: [Last match vs KKR] It was one a in a million game. We can take that kind of a game with a smile, it is all good. We played fantastic cricket last game. These things happen. We could have done a few things better, but fresh game, we will not go back to those.

Shikhar Dhawan: We were looking to bowl first. It is good pitch, there is not a lot of dew available, so we will look to put up a big score. We have a good team. It was a off day [last match vs SRH], we have been playing good cricket.

Time for toss

6.58pm Live visuals on the television show that Mohit Sharma has been presented with his Titans cap. He last played in the IPL in 2020 for Delhi Capitals.

6.55pm Not long before the toss. Will Yash Dayal retain his place? Any debutants for Titans? Will Rabada make his way back? Who does Liam Livingstone replace? We'll have to wait for a bit to find out. What do you guys think, any changes in either teams expected?

Pitch report: "It's an absolute beauty, not for the bowlers, but for the batters," says Murali Kartik. 74 metres and 67 metres, the boundary dimensions square of the wicket, 74 metres straight on one side. "Quite a good covering of grass, says Chris Morris. In my opinion, I will like to bowl first, and see what should be there to chase." 168, the par score, here. Anyone who wins the toss will want to bowl first.

Samar: "GT really needs to find a way to get Dasun Shanaka in the 11. He could be the difference maker both with Bat and ball. Not to mention, he holds fort in field too"

Vips: "How about a Punjab win today. This will spice up the points table really well. Expect nothing short of a last over (maybe even a last ball) finish today."

6.45pm The first bit of news is that Liam Livingstone is back and training at the nets for Kings. If he plays, this will be his first formal cricket match since he jarred his knee on Test debut in Pakistan in December. He should take Matt Short's place in the XI. Kagiso Rabada might also get a look in, but Nathan Ellis has done fairly well so far. Hardik Pandya, who was unwell and missed the last match, should be available for this encounter. All this and a lot more in Sidharth Monga's preview.

6.40pm Both teams are coming off losses into this game. While Titans lost to Kolkata Knight Riders, yep that Rinku Singh game, while Kings went down to Sunrisers Hyderabad despite a Shikhar Dhawan masterclass. There's not much to separate between the two teams so far in the points table too, and a win will be crucial.

6.30pm Hello, everyone and welcome to the ball-by-ball commentary of Match No.18 of IPL 2023. I am Ashish Pant and I will soon be joined by Abhimanyu Bose in the comms seat. We have Gujarat Titans taking on Punjab Kings in Mohali. After four days of photo finishes one after the other, what do these two teams have in store for us today?

text: Back of a length again on middle stump, he flogs it away to deep midwicket.

On-pace length ball just outside off, was 133.kph outside off. He plays it with an open face to point.

Poor lines from Mohit and Rajapaksa gets an easy four. Slower bouncer, around 118 kph, but the line was down leg. And the batter just helps it past the keeper. With short fine leg up, that was only going one way.
On a length just outside off, he punches it hard to cover and sets off for a quick run only to be sent back and wisely so.
postText: Rajkumar Lingav: "@Nick - There is also these budding young talents in Sai Sudharshan (Batsman), Sai Kishore (Bowler) and S Bharath (Keeper). "

text: And is welcomed with a slam back over his head. Back of length ball on middle, Jitesh stands tall and crashes it straight over the bowler's head.
preText: Shami back

text: Another back of a length ball on middle stump, he swipes it to the deep backward square leg fielder. Jitesh wanted a second, but is sent back again
Banged in short around shoulder-high into the body of Rajapaksa. He fends it awkwardly towards square leg.
Fortuitous but Jitesh will take it gleefully! On a length into the batter, goes for an expansive drive, instead gets a thick inside-edge just past the stumps.

text: Edged, is it? Saha appeals but does not get a lot of support. Pandya has taken a review in the nick of time. They are already a review down. Back of a length ball just on off that tails away from Jitesh just a touch. He pushes at it and the ball goes past his outside edge. Oh, hello. UltraEdge confirms there was a smidge of an edge on that. What a top review from Saha, who was the only appealing. The on-field umpire has to change his decision, and Kings are four down.
Good length ball outside off, he slaps it to deep cover
preText: Sam Curran comes in now. Mohit is over the wicket.

text: Short and wide and Rajapaksa cuts it hard but straight to deep cover.
Ooh, goes past the outside edge again. Length ball just outside off, just shaping from the batter, who pokes at it and misses.
Good length ball outside off, he punches it to extra cover

shortText: Rashid Khan to Rajapaksa, 1 leg bye
text: Flatter legbreak on middle and leg as Rajapaksa goes back, looking to flog it away. Misses and is rapped on the pads with the batter in front. A loud appeal ensues, but the umpire says no. The only thing is whether the ball was pitching in line. Hardik takes the review. The ball-tracker shows that was pitching outside leg.
preText:
Rashid back

shortText: Rashid Khan to Rajapaksa, no run

Length outside off, he pushes it to mid-off
Good length ball outside off, he cuts it to hard but straight to deep cover
Dances down the track to the length ball on leg, but can only scythe it to the right of mid-off.

On a length now on middle and leg, he can only bunt it back to the bowler

preText: Joseph for his last over

text: Fuller on the pads of Curran who flicks it to wide long on and they take two. Rajapaksa had to put in a dive but think he was safe
Fuller down leg, Curran is well inside the line looking to hoick it away, and misses. Oh, that is called a wide. Joseph is not impressed with that call.

Very similar to the second ball of the over, but this time, the umpire does not call it a wide. Why was the earlier ball called a wide, and this isn't? Curran opts for the review. The third umpire says, if Curran was in his normal stance, the ball would have struck his pads. The decision stands.
Low full toss on leg stump, he backs away and mistimes to mid-off.
Fuller but down the leg, called a wide this time.

text: End of a difficult innings for Rajapaksa! Knee-high full toss on middle stump, Rajapaksa chips it straight to deep midwicket. Easy catch for Gill running in. The batter never got going and a strike rate of 76.92 was just not good enough on the day.
Banged in short into the body of Shahrukh, who is upto the task and pulls him over deep midwicket with aplomb. What a shot first ball!

text: Angles the full-length ball into the pads of Curran, who gets a thick inside-edge onto his pads towards short third.

shortText: Mohammed Shami to Shahrukh Khan, 1 run
text: Hit hard and on the bounce to Little at mid-off. Length outside off, was in his slot, but does not get under it enough. Hits it flat and hard.

Fuller on middle stump, he backs away again and drags it to deep midwicket

shortText: Mohammed Shami to Shahrukh Khan, SIX

postText: Mustafa Moudi : "Same old story for PBKS - They begin the tournament on high posing as serious Contenders and then suddenly goes on free fall after 4-5 match failing to even make it in the Top 4 !!"

text: And, now Curran falls! Mohit gets his second wicket of the night. He goes into the pitch with the off-cutter shoulder high with the line outside off. Curran has to wait for it, and while he gets a good chunk on it, there is no pace. The ball goes straight to deep midwicket where Gill takes a simple catch.

preText: Little to bowl the final over

text: Oh, Brar goes straight and all the way! Right in his arc, on off. He clears his front leg and sends it soaring straight over the bowler's head.
On a length on leg stump, he drags it to deep backward square leg. They take a run.

11.45pm Gujarat Titans have joined Rajasthan Royals and Lucknow Super Giants at six points from four games with the win today. Gujarat Titans again showed that they can ace a chase. From Sunday onwards, we have had last-ball thrillers every day. Today, it went to the penultimate delivery. Join us tomorrow for when Kolkata Knight Riders take on Sunrisers Hyderabad. For now, on behalf of Ashish Pant, Venkat Raghav and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo, this is me, Abhimanyu, signing off. Goodnight, and get rested before the next thriller!

11.35pm Time for the presentation ceremony

Mohit Sharma is the POTM: "I didn't think much but I have played at Mohali for three years. I thought that it could play on the slower side. I thought I could use some variations. I was fortunate that Hardik was there so I could discuss with him whenever I wanted to try something. You just have to go back and do the same thing. You go to train and keep giving your best. [On bowling in middle overs] I was prepared from before about my role. I knew that I would most probably have to bowl after the tenth over. Credit goes to the coach and the environment created here that everyone's role is very clear."

Gujarat Titans captain, Hardik Pandya: "To be very honest, i would not appreciate the game to go this close from the situation we were in. There was definitely a lot for us to learn from this game. That's the beauty of sports, it's never over till it's over. So we will go back to the drawing board. I think we can take a couple more risks in the middle overs. The wicket was good but because of the hardness of the soil and wicket, the ball was getting dried up. It was a belter when the new ball was playing. I was not surprised, when Mohit and Alzarri came. They bowled terrific. And credit to Mohit. To come join us as a net bowler and then wait for his chance, knowing his time will come and today it came. It will be a tough pill to swallow, taking it this close. Not a big fan of taking the game to the last over."

11.23pmGujarat Titans were seemingly cruising for a large part of the chase. With seven needed off the last over, it looked like a simple conclusion, largely thanks to Shubman Gill's composed 67. But Sam Curran had other ideas. However, in the end, it was "the iceman" Rahul Tewatia who got the job done.

Shubman Gill: "The wicket got tougher towards the end. It was difficult to score boundaries at will. It was important for us to run hard and get those boundaries. I feel I should have finished the match but I feel Rahul Tewatia and Kings XI is a love-story. In these types of games there is definitely pressure on both teams. But it's important to keep getting those singles and not have dot balls. Just after their innings got over, we knew that it would be easier to score runs with the hard ball. It got slower with the old ball. So we needed to get off to a good start in the powerplay. We lost a bit of momentum when Hardik bhai got out. It wasn't a big score but it was important to rotate the strike and not have dot balls. It's amazing. He [Mohit Sharma] was looking good in the nets, especially with the old ball. He has got a good yorker and he is very accurate. I think it was a great Gujarat Titans debut for him."

PBKS skipper, Shikhar Dhawan: Yeah I agree that we did not quite put as many runs on the board. If you see the number of dot balls, whenever they play 56 dot balls, they end up losing the game. So we need to rectify that. Whenever a team lose early wickets, they go on the back foot but we need to work on that. Our batting unit needed to give more of a cushion to the bowling unit. He came for practice yesterday but he pulled his muscle so he may be fit in another 3-4 days."

3.28 pm The players are striding out to the middle. Virat Kohli takes strike. Faf du Plessis is at the non-striker's end. Anrich Nortje has the new ball.

Sam: "What's up with Perth producing these super tall allrounders big hitters like Mitch Marsh, Cam Green, even Aaron Hardie... 3.01 pm The news from the middle is that Delhi has won the toss and will bowl first. As reported in the ESPNcricinfo preview, Wanindu Hasaranga comes straight into the XI for RCB and David Willey is the man to make way. As for Delhi, Mitchell Marsh comes back into the XI for Rovman Powell.

RCB XI: 1 Faf du Plessis (capt), 2 Virat Kohli, 3 Mahipal Lomror, 4 Glenn Maxwell, 5 Shahbaz Ahmed, 6 Dinesh Karthik (wk), 7 Wanindu Hasaranga, 8 Harshal Patel, 9 Wayne Parnell, 10 Mohammed Siraj, 11 Vijaykumar Vyshak.

Subs: Suyash Prabhudessai, David Willey, Akash Deep, Karn Sharma, Anuj Rawat.

Delhi Capitals XI: 1 David Warner (capt), 2 Mitchell Marsh, 3 Yash Dhull, 4 Manish Pandey, 5 Axar Patel, 6 Lalit Yadav, 7 Aman Khan, 8 Abishek Porel (wk), 9 Kuldeep Yadav, 10 Anrich Nortje, 11 Mustafizur Rahman

Subs: Prithvi Shaw, Mukesh Kumar, Pravin Dubey, Sarfaraz Khan, Chetan Sakariya

Meanwhile, Hemant Brar is inside the Chinnaswamy and is chiming in for the first time: "Hello from the venue. It's a warm day in Bengaluru. Could become cloudy in the evening but no forecast of rain. The players, meanwhile, are warming up. Harshal Patel is bowling yorkers on the side pitch, Karn Sharma and Wanindu Hasaranga rolling their arms as well. In the Capitals camp, Ricky Ponting is having a long chat with Shane Watson."

Tom Moody says in today's T20 Time Out video preview that Harshal Patel needs to step up for RCB to get back to their winning ways.

Samir Dave: "I think the time is ripe enough for Mitchell Marsh to prove his mettle as a frontline allrounder ! DC shld do a SRH n let Marsh open the innings- small ground and short boundaries will only help ! With his steady bowling- he has potential to be the next Shane Watson !"

2.30 pm Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of the first half of today's doubleheader in the 2023 Indian Premier League as Royal Challengers Bangalore host Delhi Capitals. I'm Peter Della Penna on hand to steer the commentary ship.

Both teams have been sailing through rough waters in the first two weeks of this year's tournament, with only one win in seven matches between them as they languish at the bottom of the table. But both sides have reinforcements arriving for today's encounter with Wanindu Hasaranga now available for RCB following the conclusion of commitments for Sri Lanka and Mitchell Marsh now in Delhi's camp after taking a few matches off for his wedding. Find out about all that and more in today's match preview by Deivarayan Muthu.

5.09 pm See-saw innings for RCB. Kohli got them off to a brilliant start, but then the sequence of three wickets in three balls in the middle stunted their momentum badly and the curious decision to send in Rawat ahead of both Hasaranga and Parnell meant plenty of dot balls were chewed up with the two overseas never getting to face a ball. Will it cost RCB and allow Delhi to get their first victory of the 2023 season? Stay tuned for the start of the chase.

Delhi bowler Kuldeep Yadav: "The wicket was pretty much on the slower side so I was just trying to hit the right length. I bowled a couple of overs to Virat bhai, checking his initial movement. [On the wicket of Maxwell] He was going really well and I thought I can be the man to change the game from here. I believe in myself and we got him out and then next ball DK got out and we were back in the game. I'm just focusing on bowling in the right areas. We have a lot of games to go and I think I can probably break the 20 [wickets] mark. 175 is a good total. For spinners, it's not coming onto the bat. Once the spinners come on, we need to keep rotating the strike and that's the important thing."

postText:
7.10 pm Much of the drama of that chase was sucked out in the first four overs and once Axar got out, the final overs just meandered along with Pandey's half-century a silver lining for Delhi. The fielding by Delhi was poor in the first innings, missing several chances. By comparison, RCB were switched on from the very first over with Rawat's runout of Shaw a great catalyst for a tremendous team-wide fielding effort.

Delhi captain David Warner: "I said at the toss that we had to do both disciplines very well and unfortunately we did it again tonight where we lost too many early wickets. We didn't build partnerships chasing that total. It should have been an easy task but unfortunately we didn't come up trumps. We lose three wickets in the Powerplay and runouts are non-negotiable in this format and that sometimes can cost you the game. Siraj had his tail up and bowled extremely well. You can't take credit away from the way they came out and started as well. The positives were great with the bowling and fielding were exceptional. Our attitude and energy were amazing. But yet again it was just our batting. We're going to have to try to work out how we're going to take on the Powerplay and not lose early wickets, especially in the first two or three overs. That's going to hurt you in a lot of games. We have to have a hard look at ourselves and come back strong with five days off. Things aren't working at the moment but teams have come back from 0-5 so hopefully we can be that second team."

RCB bowler Vijaykumar Vyshak after his three wickets on IPL debut: "I've been waiting for this opportunity for a very long time. I've been working hard so I think it's been paying off. Faf came and told me that the wicket was holding a bit so I backed my strength and bowled my slower ones a little more and I think that helped for me. I've been working on it for two years so I think it's finally paid off. I wasn't ready to bowl the knuckle ball but Faf came and told me again, 'You can probably go for a slower one' so I thought I'll do that and I got a wicket. It's very important because the management has told me to go express yourself so I think I did that and I'm very pleased with the performance. [Prior to being added to the official squad] I was in as a net bowler so I was just helping the boys."

RCB captain Faf du Plessis: "We unfortunately have had to defend a few games in a row now at the Chinnaswamy and it's not always easy so I'm very proud of the bowlers tonight. It's difficult because it's the first day game of the season and also with the new rule now with the extra batter, you always feel like you need to get more. So even at halfway stage, 175 in a day game usually feels like a really good score but it's just that unknown factor with the extra batter but it proved to be the right score. The way we bowled in that first six overs, not only today but so far in all the games, Siraj is bowling beautifully. In a game where it's a bit slower the wicket, generally the first six overs is the most important with the bat. You want to try to play positive and get ahead of the rate but the way we bowled was just unbelievable. So huge credit to our seamers in the first six."

Player of the match is Virat Kohli for his first innings half-century and his three catches. "[On the first catch skier over cover] It was a bit of a tricky one when it went up in the air. I first of all made sure that no one is close to me so I had space to judge the ball. It was quite difficult but the other two were quite easy. I was quite disappointed that I got out to a full toss. I'd been playing really well and after I got to 50, I was targeting 30-35 runs in the next 10 balls. That's usually how I play and that would've helped us get past 200. I mentioned to the guys in the change room that it felt like 175 was enough on this pitch. It felt like it slowed down."

Matthew Short, PBKS batter: It was nice to get a few runs away but at the end of the day, we needed one of the batters to go on and make a fifty-plus score, similar to what Shubman Gill showed later in the evening. Hopefully if I get a start like that, I can make it out. The last few months has been huge for me. I feel I have the confidence to show that skill-set in this competition. Punjab Kings XI: Atharva Taide, Harpreet Bhatia, Matthew Short, Sikandar Raza, Jitesh Sharma (wk), Shahrukh Khan, Sam Curran (c), Harpreet Brar, Kagiso Rabada, Rahul Chahar, Arshdeep Singh

Substitutes: Prabhsimran Singh, Nathan Ellis, Mohit Rathee, Rishi Dhawan

7pm It's time for the toss. Curran calls tails, and it comes down as tails. Punjab Kings will bowl first. He says Dhawan is a huge loss but he hopes the youngsters can stand up. He adds that the pitch looks a little strange. Rahul quips he is happy doing anything, and that it is just about enjoying their cricket. Assessing the conditions and then adapting will be the key, like always.

Let's see what the conditions have in store for us. The pitch is to one side of the square, meaning that the dimensions are skewed. Matthew Hayden says the pitch looks tired, although it is a fresh strip. Patchy grass throughout, and if the pacers bowl into those areas, they could extract some assistance. Pommie Mbangwa hopes that there are more runs in this track than the other day.

Big news coming in. Shikhar Dhawan has picked up a shoulder niggle, with Sam Curran leading PBKS tonight. LSG bowler Yudhvir Singh, meanwhile, has been handed his cap and looks set to make his debut tonight.

LSG have batted first only once so far this season, while PBKS have batted first in each of their games so far. The last time a game was held in Lucknow, LSG applied the spin-squeeze to restrict SRH 121-8 before chasing down that total in 16 overs. What will the captain winning the toss want to do tonight?

While we await the toss, do hop over to our coverage of the RCB-DC game, where RCB are very much in control against the Capitals.

LSG have been one of the teams to beat so far, having won thrice already (in four attempts). Two of those have come on their home patch, which is where they will face PBKS tonight. Most of their batting components have functioned well too, with Kyle Mayers, Marcus Stoinis and Nicholas Pooran among the runs at different stages in this campaign. There might be a bit of concern around the middling returns of Deepak Hooda and captain KL Rahul. Nothing, thus, would please LSG more than this pair getting among the runs tonight.

PBKS, meanwhile, have stuttered after a strong start to the season. Batting has been a bit of a concern. Shikhar Dhawan has done the bulk of the heavy lifting but none of the others have really been consistent.

Their bowling seems slightly better, both on paper and in terms of how they have fared. Sam Curran's inclusion has added variety, although they would want Kagiso Rabada to hit his straps soon, having struggled against the Gujarat Titans.

Plenty to look forward to, as always. PBKS have won once on the road, while LSG are yet to lose at home. So, expect another thrilling contest, with neither wanting to give the other an inch.

11:55pm Right. That will be that from us for tonight. Hope you enjoyed our coverage as much as we enjoyed bringing it to you. The action in the IPL, especially on weekends, comes thick and fast. MI take on KKR in the afternoon game before GT and RR clash later in the evening. Do join us for those games too. Until next time, this is me (Shashwat) signing off on behalf of Thilak and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo! Goodbye, goodnight and take care!

Sikandar Raza, Player of the Match: (On the feeling) It feels great, to be honest. When I got out, there were a few demons. Credit to Shahrukh for the way he finished. If we had not won, I might not have felt so good. (On the pressure) It is one of the biggest stages and now that you are here, you want to do well. I had average games (prior to tonight) so that was the emotion I was carrying as well but it was important to channelise it. Jitesh's wicket was very crucial. We all know how he bats. If he stayed for 6-8 balls, he would have finished the game by himself. Then Shahrukh came out and hit the first ball for six, and I felt really confident that he can finish off the game.

Sam Curran, Punjab Kings captain: Amazing win and this franchise seems to love a close game. The boys chipped in; it was not a perfect game but good to win. The guys bowled really well; the spinners bowled nicely. The way we bowled towards the end was good. Dew came in but the wicket was still offering a bit. Raza played nicely in the middle, and the way Shahrukh came in and finished. The word around the dressing room is that he has worked very hard and the coaching staff have been clear with his role. Fingers crossed he can keep continuing. Different dimensions, so, each game, you have to come up with different plans. The rhythm is good. We used 6-7 bowlers, we have so many options and that is good to have.

Shahrukh Khan: As I told you after the first innings, it was important to play smartly in the middle. The way that Raza and everyone played, it allowed me to go out and finish off the job. (On first-ball six off Wood) I was late to come in. Just when Jitesh got out, the time-out happened. I just wanted to keep my mind clear. I think my practice is paying off. If I go too cheeky, I don't think it will work too much. So, I try to play straight and happy that it paid off. When Harpreet was batting, I told him to go for the big hit off the last ball. Unfortunately, he got out to Wood but it is important that I was on strike (for the final over) and finished it off for my team.

KL Rahul, Lucknow Super Giants captain: I think we were about 10 runs short towards the end. The dew came in and it seemed to help the batters a little bit more. We did not execute well with the ball. When you are playing on a new ground and a new pitch, you cannot rely on the previous games. We take it as it comes, assess it on the go and not really set ourselves a target. If a couple of batters get in, play good knocks, we can get to 180-190. Unfortunately, today, few of the batters hit good shots but got caught just on the boundary line. On another day, we would have got those 10-15 runs extra that would have made the difference.

(On his catch) The game was on the line and I try to give everything when I am on the field. Each player has a different role to play and that is why it is called a team game. We have 7-8 batters in our team and few can clear any boundary. Some are not as powerful but have skill. It is about each player playing their part and role and that is what makes a team exciting, and that is what we need to do. We do have power hitters down the order in Pooran and Stoinis. Mayers up top takes the aggressive route and a few of us have to assess the conditions and stick to what works for them. Just about giving them the confidence to do what they are comfortable with.

11:30pm Wow, what a game that turned out to be. For large stretches of this innings, it did not look like it would come down to the final over but it did, largely thanks to Bishnoi's brilliance. That, though, also highlights how Rahul and LSG missed a trick by not introducing him earlier. While the ploy might have been to delay his arrival and use him at the death as much as possible, they allowed the game to drift, especially when Raza and Bhatia were at the crease together. LSG would also be ruing the way they batted, and the runs they left out in the middle. Rahul scored 74 but after this defeat, the murmurs around his strike rate will only get louder.

As for the Kings, they would be thrilled with how they held their nerve. Just a few days ago, they failed to win in the final over, so, from that perspective alone, this is an improvement. Shahrukh also came to the party, with Raza also notching up his maiden IPL fifty. They were excellent with the ball too towards the end, and a combination of those factors means that they are now level on points with LSG.

3.28pm Arjun Tendulkar grabs the new ball. The Tendulkars are to become the first father-son pair to play the IPL. The emcee at the stadium announces his name and the crowd gives out a big roar. Rohit Sharma gave him his cap. He looks quietly confident, more than anything itching to deliver the first ball. We have a count down from ten to one.... and play on.

Mohd Irshad : "Arjun is a good kid, working hard...did good for Goa....come a bit handy with bat...debut ranji hundred like his father did. Wishing him.best."

3.26pm A little bit on Duan Jansen: he is twin brother of Marco. He is a left-arm seamer. In 2022, he was with St Kitts & Nevis Patriots in the 6ixty tournament and CPL. During the 6ixty, he finished as one of the leading bowlers and helped his team win it.

In all, there were three changes for Mumbai, even though SKY said one at the toss. Rohit, Arshad and Behrendorff out; David, Arjun and Jansen in. KKR have kept things simple - no change, which means, Venky Iyer starts instead of Suyash Sharma. Lot of Mumbaikars in the KKR set up too - Chandrakant Pandit and Abhishek Nayar, to start. So who starts as favourites? Mumbai have a 22-9 record against KKR.

Afeef: "Based on recent form, KKR start as favourites. They've won the last 3 encounters between these two teams, and they're doing better in this season than MI."

3.17pm Oh hello everyone. There's so much to unpack. Rohit's stomach bug keeps him out of the start, but he's in the impact sub list, so he could stay off the field while the sun is out and maybe even come to bat later. Suryakumar given the 'headache' of captaincy while his own form suffers. Maybe this captaincy thing shall help him. And then there's the debut of Arjun Tendulkar. Sachin's going to sit in the dugout too!

2.52pm There will be two Mumbai Indians captains turning up at toss on Sunday afternoon. It is understood that Harmanpreet Kaur will accompany Rohit Sharma to the centre as part of the franchise's initiative to support young girls.

The initiative, called Education and Sports for All and run by the franchise in association with Reliance Foundation, will also have the Wankhede Stadium filled with over 19,000 young girls. In a media release issued by Mumbai, the franchise said these girls are from 36 NGOs in the city. No tickets have been put on sale for the public otherwise.

Mumbai Indians will also be wearing the jersey of their title-winning WPL side today.

2.45pm Cameron Green and Tim David helped Mumbai Indians seal victory against Delhi Capitals, as they chased down five runs off a brilliant final over bowled by Anrich Nortje. As you wait for the game to begin, you can read Roller's piece on the two of them and how they have settled into flexible roles at Mumbai Indians.

2.40pm Jofra Archer is having a bowl out there, but it's some left-arm medium with a short run-up.

The good news for KKR fans: Dre Russ is in the house and he is shadow batting!

2.35pm Nagraj Gollapudi is at the ground and he says Arjun Tendulkar may be ready to play today. He has marked his run-up. Duan Jansen could debut as well, with Jofra Archer continuing to miss out. Arjun Tendulkar, Duan Jansen and Riley Meredith could make up Mumbai Indians' seam attack today, with Cam Green offering support.

While KKR have put in some astonishing performances this season, the top order -- specifically an opening partner for Rahmanullah Gurbaz -- has been a question for them. While Ian Bishop feels they don't need to tinker with the combination of Gurbaz and Jagadeesan, Amol Muzumdar said it may be time to bring in Jason Roy in our video preview.

2.30pm It's Kolkata Knight Riders taking on Mumbai Indians at the Wankhede Stadium in today's first IPL game. Last week, when KKR played the afternoon game, Rinku Singh delivered a thriller for the ages. But the Wankhede is not a happy hunting ground for the visitors, who have only beaten Mumbai Indians there once -- in 2012. You can read up about that, and more, in Nagraj Gollapudi's preview. 7.50pm That's all the action from the Wankhede today, but that's not all the cricket from today. Gujarat Titans are taking on Rajasthan Royals in a replay of last year's final. This is Abhimanyu, signing off on behalf of Sreshth, Thilak and everyone else here at ESPNcricinfo.

Venkatesh Iyer is the POTM, for his 51-ball 104: "Would have been happier if we would have finished on the winning note but nonetheless, pleased with my effort. That's the role given to me by the management and it's my job to repay them. Obviously it was a very beautiful wicket to bat on. Once you score those 30-40 runs, it gets easy to score. Really happy to get a hundred. Their new ball bowlers are both swing bowlers and once you allow them to settle down, it gets difficult. So I just didn't want to let them settle. Once the swing goes away, it gets easier to play them. Once you're out there doing something for the team, you forget all the pain. The wicket was really nice and I was enjoying myself out there. In hindsight I think we did score 15-20 runs less, and the way MI were going, they could have scored it in another over but yeah, we were a little short."

Mumbai Indians captain on the day, Suryakumar Yadav comes out to speak: "We had a chat in the dugout that we had to carry the momentum from the last game and the boys put on a show. I would have loved to finish the game but nevertheless, I was very happy with the way the team played. In the afternoon we thought the wicket was a little dry, but the way the guys batted it settled down in the evening. At the Wankhede in day games, 160-170 is a good score but Kishan got us off to a great start. I took my time in the first five-seven balls and thought if I could get my eye in I could get a score. We know that if the top order gives a good start, what kind of firepower we have lower down the order. It was a legendary spell [Piyush Chawla]. He put his hand up under pressure."

7.40pm It's time for the presentation ceremony

Sumeet: "On a complete tangent.. ZAK even today looks so fit and does not look a day older than the 2011 World Cup winning ZAK! "

7.30pm The Mumbai Indians side take a lap of the stadium, which is all blue right now. There are loud cheers all around. Sachin Tendulkar ended his career with a lap of honour and Arjun Tendulkar begins his with one, notes Hemant Brar!

Nitish Rana: "I think we were 15-20 runs short. Credit to PC bhai (Piyush Chawla) for the way he bowled. I feel quite bad for Venky. You play so well, score a century in a day game in Mumbai and you end up on the losing side. I feel bad for him. If our best bowlers are going for runs, there's not much to say. The way Ishan played against Narine. I think we could have bowled better in the powerplay. I definitely want my bowling unit to deliver more. One or two matches is fine, but it's been five games now. People can have off days, but on back-to-back games, it hurts as an unit. But we will talk about it and hopefully we can bounce back."

7.21pm Mumbai Indians have bounced back in style with two wins in two games. Venkatesh Iyer's belligerent century seems a long while back now. He never got the support he needed from his team-mates today and Mumbai Indians have chased down the target in style. Ishan Kishan and Rohit Sharma pretty much killed the game in the powerplay and Suryakumar Yadav returning to form is an added bonus for them.

9.10 pm Gujarat had a lengthy lull in the middle of their innings where plenty of singles were being collected but no boundaries. Will that cost them? postText:
11.09 pm From being dead and buried in the Powerplay after sensational twin new-ball bursts from Shami and Hardik, to being just as dead and buried at the halfway stage. They were 66 for 4 after 12 overs needing 112 runs to win from 48 balls with a 2.01% chance of winning according to the ESPNcricinfo win probability calculation... and somehow Rajasthan get there with four balls to spare! What an extraordinary comeback by Royals. They avenge their loss in the 2022 IPL Final.

Hetmyer could have been caught at deep third man by Shami in the 16th over on 22, but a horrible misjudgment resulted in the ball landing just over the rope for six. The fielding by comparison that Rajasthan produced in the first innings made a huge difference in the end, in particular Boult's improbable return catch after Samson collided with Hetmyer, and Buttler's alert runout off the deflection by Zampa.

Gujarat Titans captain Hardik Pandya: "That's the beauty about this game. The game is never over. That was the message to the boys as well. The game is never over until it's over. So I think this is one more less for us. [Asked why he opted to bring in Noor as the Impact Sub instead of Josh Little] He's someone who is difficult to pick as well. He actually bowled well. I don't want to be harsh on him. He got us a big breakthrough which we wanted but I think the other bowlers did not execute. It's a very long tournament. Obviously all these losses remind you at the end of the tournament reminds you if you are not on the other side but it's still a very long tournament. A lot of matches left. We still need to play a lot of good cricket even if we had won today. I felt we were short some runs at the innings break. They bowled some good overs but we should have gone harder to put the game [out of reach] and get a 200 total. When I was watching outside, I did feel we were maybe 10 runs short."

Rajasthan Royals batter Devdutt Padikkal: "It got a little tense. When these matches go down to the wire, it's always a bit tense. But I felt everyone had the belief that we had Ashwin out there who could finish it off. We knew that we had to try to keep the scoreboard ticking at some point. We couldn't just try to take it deep. We had to get boundaries from time to time. It was moving around quite a bit the first 3-4 overs so we had to be circumspect but at the same time when the ball was in our areas, we had to go for it. Thankfully we connected with a few which was really important in the end. [On Hetmyer] It's unbelievable how consistent he is doing what he does toward the end of the innings. Every game he comes in and gives us what we need at the end. So we are really grateful to have such a talented asset and hopefully he can continue to win us games. He's always the one leading the celebrations so it's going to be the same tonight."

Rajasthan Royals captain Sanju Samson: "When you play some quality opponents on a quality wicket in a quality stadium like this, you expect a great match. I'm very happy to be on the winning side. I think it was very important to rotate the bowlers. They were going hard at our spinners. After the timeout, they were playing some quality cricket shots and we needed to respect that but I'm very proud of our team for restricting them to a 170-odd score. With the start we had while batting, it was very important to know how good a wicket this was. With the quality of bowling they had in the Powerplay, we had to respect them. But we knew we could play some shots later on. We had a good matchup with Zampa on David Miller and almost got him but still it turned out well for us. [On Hetmyer] I don't think he likes easy situations. We don't mind putting him in these situations."

Shimron Hetmyer named Player of the Match for his 56 not out off 26 balls to seal a Royals win. "I just really wanted to win against these guys because they beat us three times last year so it was a bit of revenge really. I just practice it really. It helps to practice with that mindset that you're a couple of wicket down and you need 100 runs with eight overs left. You just try to program your mind that way and so far it's working. I was pretty happy to be honest to be facing [a spinner for the final over]. I was just focused on getting a double off the first ball and then see what happens after that."

That'll do it for ESPNcricinfo's live coverage from today's IPL doubleheader. Come back tomorrow for some more action. Until then, take care!

preText:
7.30pm Well here we go. Rohit sharma and Ishan Kishan come out to open. Orange flags everywhere. Bhuvneshwar Kumar has the new ball.

Sid: "Let's see how Markande play against his ex-team.. after being together with MI for so long time, he was under-utilised by MI so far .."

7.15pm "Very strange selection by SRH.. Umran Malik not in starting XI when they're bowling first. Could've easily kept Mayank/ Tripathi/ Brook out for that extra bowling option. " ArunK, I tend to agree with you, but I think they might be looking at getting in another batter in the second innings.

7.10pm The big news is that SRH have left out Umran Malik. And MI are going in with just three overseas players. Possible that Riley Meredith comes in in the second innings. Arjun Tendulkar gets a second game.

7pm SRH have won the toss and will field. Aiden Markram says the wicket looks slightly dry, and it should get better later on in the night. Rohit Sharma is back as MI captain. A huge cheer from his former home ground. What a killjoy. The Jansen twins won't be going against each other. Jason Behrendorff, who was unwell last game, is back in place of Duan. Here are the XIs

MI 1 Rohit Sharma (capt.), 2 Ishan Kishan (wk), 3 Suryakumar Yadav, 4 Tilak Varma, 5 Cameron Green, 6 Nehal Wadhera, 7 Tim David, 8 Hrithik Shokeen, 9 Piyush Chawla, 10 Arjun Tendulkar, 11 Jason Behrendoff

SRH1 Mayank Agarwal, 2 Harry Brook, 3 Rahul Tripathi, 4 Aiden Markram (capt.), 5 Abhishek Sharma, 6 Heinrich Klaasen (wk), 7 Washington Sundar, 8 Marco Jansen, 9 Mayank Markande, 10 Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 11 T Natarajan

6.55pm One side slightly bigger than the other at the Uppal Stadium. The pitch, says Ian Bishop, is flat with the grass cut very low. It could help spin but if there is dew it should nicely skid on. Toss in five.

Venkat: "Focus is on Tilak today... he is playing in his home ground and playing against home team."

Rahim Chagani: "SRH seem like a pretty settled team but I'd love to see Glenn Phillips unleashed in the batting line-up, instead of always playing as a specialist fielder. Unfortunately, the only player to drop would probably be Harry Brook, who played a blinder on his way to a hundred last week. Guess Glenn will have to bide his time for a bit longer. "

6.30pm It's day 20, and match 25 of the IPL 2023. It's Sunrisers Hyderabad hosting Mumbai Indians. Two teams that have just begun to find their bearings but one them must lose tonight. The other goes to three wins in a row. It is also Jansen twins going up against each other for only the second time in professional cricket. Also eyes on Jofra Archer. Unlikely to play is what we hear but you never know. And what of Arjun Tendulkar? 2-0-17-0 in the powerplay at the Wankhede is not a bad debut. Does he get a second game? We will soon find out at the toss in half an hour.

You can also follow the ball-by-ball commentary for this match in Hindi or in Tamil.

7:28pm The umpires make their way out to the middle, followed by the players. Mayers and Rahul will open the batting for LSG, as expected. Boult with the new ball for RR and he will bowl from around the wicket to the LSG skipper. No slips in place.

7:18pm The one big takeaway from the XIs is that Wood is not part of the LSG side tor tonight. Naveen-ul-Haq can bowl in different phases and at the death, although replacing Wood or recreating his impact might not be easy. LSG have gone in with seven batters in their bat-first XI but might bring in Gowtham towards the end if required, or a specialist bowler if they bat well and don't need any more batting resources in the first innings.

Rajasthan Royals XI: Jos Buttler, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sanju Samson (c & wk), Riyan Parag, Dhruv Jurel, Shimron Hetmyer, R Ashwin, Jason Holder, Trent Boult, Sandeep Sharma, Yuzvendra Chahal

Substitutes: Devdutt Padikkal, M Ashwin, Joe Root, Donovan Ferreira, Navdeep Saini

Lucknow Super Giants XI: KL Rahul (c), Kyle Mayers, Deepak Hooda, Krunal Pandya, Nicholas Pooran (wk), Marcus Stoinis, Ayush Badoni, Yudhvir Singh, Ravi Bishnoi, Avesh Khan, Naveen-ul-Haq

Substitutes: Jaydev Unadkat, Daniel Sams, K Gowtham, Prerak Mankad, Amit Mishra

7pm It's time for the toss. Rahul and Samson are out in the middle. Samson gives it a flick, and it lands in Samson's favour. RR will bowl first. He says that the surface looks good. One change for RR - Jason Holder comes in place of Adam Zampa. Rahul says he would have bowled first too. He adds that LSG are quite settled with their combination, and says that they try to keep the right-left combination going with the bat as much as possible. No Quinton de Kock again for LSG, although Rahul does say he feels bad for continually omitting him.

Shrikant: "Today I shall be looking forward to performances of Zampa, Chahal, Bishnoi, and possibly Amit Mishra. Obviously, I am a big fan of wrist spinners. "

Let's see what the conditions have in store for us. The pitch is not dead in the centre, meaning that one square boundary is 62-metres long and the other is 68 metres. The straight boundaries, meanwhile, are in excess of 70 metres. There is a bit of a grass covering but there are bare patches too, and Nick Knight expects the ball to skid and the surface to be a little two-paced. He does not expect spin to play a massive role, though. Sanjay Manjrekar chimes in, saying that the captain winning the toss would want to bowl first. In fact, that is what captains did on all seven occasions in IPL 2019.

Not many teams have been inclined to play three specialist spinners in their XI. RR, though, have been an anomaly in that sense, and as Sidharth Monga explains, that is well worth the risk.

As we build up to the game, do hop over to S Sudarshanan's preview, where he chronicles what we might have in store tonight, and how these two teams are similar, yet so different.

6:20pm Match 26 of IPL 2023. Rajasthan Royals versus the Lucknow Super Giants. The team perched at the top of the points table against the side placed a rung below. Sanju Samson, who has earned rave reviews for his belligerent brand of batting up against KL Rahul, whose batting approach has, like previous years, already evoked plenty of debate. A side that is yet to play at their home ground in Jaipur against a team that has scored more than 200 in both of its away games.

There is plenty else to look forward to as well. Both franchises have tried to pack their line-up with as many power hitters. LSG seem slightly better-equipped on that front, for Deepak Hooda, Kyle Mayers, Marcus Stoinis and Nicholas Pooran are all capable of single-handedly winning games of cricket. RR are not very far behind, though, with the likes of Jos Buttler, Shimron Hetmyer, Yashasvi Jaiswal and of course, captain Samson in top form.

With the ball, RR have been brave enough to unleash Adam Zampa, R Ashwin and Yuzvendra Chahal in tandem. LSG have a spin troika of their own in K Gowtham, Krunal Pandya and Ravi Bishnoi (and possibly Amit Mishra), although Rahul's usage of them did leave a bit to be desired against PBKS.

All things considered, this game promises to be as fascinating as any. That this is the first time Jaipur will be hosting an IPL fixture since before COVID-19 became a thing, only adds another layer of intrigue. And for every little detail that transpires today, we have got you covered!

R Ashwin: If we would have been a little smarter, we could have kept them down by 10 more runs. You can't get away here like some other grounds. You need to play good cricketing shots here and you get value for that. If we get off to a good start, back good, cricketing shots, we should be able to get this done. We need to bide our time. Not one of those pitches where you can come in and tee off.

9:12pm An exceptional bowling display by RR and they have kept this strong LSG batting unit down to 154. LSG did not lose a wicket in the powerplay but only managed 37. That set the tone the rest of the innings and barring a few spurts, where runs came quickly, they struggled. Their utilisation of Pooran and Stoinis also left a bit to be desired and in the end, it felt that they had too much to do.

Credit, though, must be given to RR and the way they bowled. Most of their bowlers did not give the batters width and that worked on a pitch that was not very easy for stroke-play. They will have to bat well but RR will back themselves to get the job done tonight. Do join us in a bit for the run-chase!

postText:
11:47pm Right. That will be that from us for tonight. But the action in the IPL comes thick and fast. We have a double-header tomorrow, with PBKS hosting RCB in the afternoon and DC clashing with KKR in the evening. Do join us for those games but until next time, this is me (Shashwat) signing off on behalf of Chandan, Ranjith and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo! Goodbye, goodnight and take care!

Marcus Stoinis, Player of the Match: (On his bowling) It was nice to get involved with the ball. There were not exact plans to get them out, it was about using the conditions and using my smarts as a bowler. (On his partnership with Pooran towards the end) That was what we identified. It was a tough wicket. It was about not setting your standards too high and understanding that we needed to put on a good total. You will have to ask the skipper (smiles) but I am good health-wise (to bowl regularly).

KL Rahul, Lucknow Super Giants captain: (On his right elbow) I got hit by a throw by one of my teammates, so I am maybe doing something wrong as a captain (chuckles). At the 10-over mark, the message we sent out was that maybe 165 is a good total, so, let us try to get to 160. Did not have to set ourselves very high. They are a quality team, they have good bowlers. We fell 10 runs short maybe but we made it up with the ball in the end. There was no dew and that was fair on both teams. (On how they arrived at a par score) We came in yesterday and we were thinking 180 is a par score. Knowing the batters they have, the mindset was to get 15 runs extra. When Boult bowled the first over, me and Kyle had a chat and we said that the ball was not coming on. We assessed it quite well but if there were a couple more partnerships in the middle, we could have gotten more. (Turning point) That Samson run out and two wickets falling back-to-back lets you to come back into the game. RR's top three-four are really strong and our plan was to get them out early, and it came via a run-out today.

Sanju Samson, Rajasthan Royals captain: (On how it feels to lose such a game) Obviously not great but we need to take the lessons and move on from here. With the batting line-up we have, that was a chaseable score. They bowled well, used the conditions well but I still believe it was a chaseable score. I was expecting something like this (the pitch), a bit of low bounce and I think we got something like that. We need to play smart cricket and we were going really well till about over 9-10. Then it was about getting one big over in the middle phase. They bowled well and when we tried to go hard, we lost wickets. (On learnings) Irrespective of whether you win or lose, you take lessons from the game. We did a good job restricting them to that score but learnings from there as well.

Kyle Mayers: It was a good victory. Any win away from home is good. (On his form) I think I have been batting well, from international cricket and into this tournament. (On the pitch) It was not best for stroke-play and I told myself early to not look for sixes and look for more boundaries. It was a difficult surface for any new batter to come in and start hitting. I thought we were in a situation where I needed to bat more balls on a difficult surface. I felt it (strike rate) was good, I tried to play the situation well, pick my match-ups and tried to capitalise. (On the pitch being two-paced) I think it was just low. It was not two-paced as much, it was more up-and-down bounce. Variable bounce was the hardest thing. It was about trying to hit the ball as straight as possible and access the off side.

Shaheer: "68 needed from 51 deliveries with 10 wickets in hand and they have defended it successfully. Incredible from LSG."

11:20pm Wow, that game ebbed, flowed, twisted, turned and ultimately ended in LSG's favour. At the half-way stage, it felt that they did not have enough runs on the board. As it turned out, they did. That was largely down to how well they bowled, and how brilliantly they used the conditions and the dimensions.

RR, after a strong powerplay, could not cash in against the spinners and with Buttler not being at his fluent best, they handed over the initiative to LSG. Samson's run out did not help either and while Padikkal and Parag tried to make a dash towards the end, their intent and execution left a bit to be desired, especially as the run-rate kept climbing post Hetmyer's dismissal in the 16th over.

preText:
3:27pm The umpires make their way out to the middle, followed by the players. du Plessis and Kohli will open the batting, and they will face Arshdeep first up. This could be a very intriguing battle. One slip in place for Kohli.

3:25pm The big talking point is, of course, Kohli captaining RCB for the first time since relinquishing captaincy after the 2021 season. Raza being left out is another, considering he was POTM in the last game he played. Ellis replacing Rabada is also interesting and perhaps indicates PBKS are expecting this pitch to aid his changes of pace.

Shashank: "I am also asking the question a million RCB fans will be asking - Why is VK captaining despite FDP being in the 11?" -- If RCB were to field first, du Plessis would have come into the XI as an Impact Player. Now that they are batting first, he is a part of their starting XI. du Plessis picked up a niggle in the CSK game and has not been deemed fit enough to field, hence, Kohli is standing in as skipper.

Liam Livingstone, Punjab Kings all-rounder: Seems a long while ago. Nice to be back on the ground and not in the gym. (On being away from the game) Given me time to reflect on the last couple of years and really excited to play again. It has been difficult, there have been days that have been really difficult. Days like this (today) make it worthwhile. Fingers crossed that I can get up and running again. We have been playing some good cricket, trying to take the game on, entertain the crowd - that is a big thing for us. RCB are a great team but the boys are really excited. The environment has been brilliant and everyone is looking forward to it today. (On the crowds) I guess that is our job. If the stadiums are full, we are doing our job.

Punjab Kings XI: Atharva Taide, Harpreet Bhatia, Matthew Short, Liam Livingstone, Jitesh Sharma (wk), Shahrukh Khan, Sam Curran (c), Harpreet Brar, Nathan Ellis, Rahul Chahar, Arshdeep Singh

Substitutes: Prabhsimran Singh, Sikandar Raza, Mohit Rathee, Rishi Dhawan, Shivam Singh

Royal Challengers Bangalore XI: Faf du Plessis, Virat Kohli (c), Mahipal Lomror, Glenn Maxwell, Shahbaz Ahmed, Dinesh Karthik (wk), Suyash Prabhudessai, Wayne Parnell, Wanindu Hasaranga, Harshal Patel, Mohammed Siraj

Substitutes: Vijaykumar Vyshak, David Willey, Akash Deep, Karn Sharma, Anuj Rawat

3pm It's time for the toss. The big news is that Kohli is captaining RCB today. Curran, meanwhile, will again be stepping in for the injured Shikhar Dhawan. Curran gives the coin a flick, Kohli calls heads, and it comes down as tails. PBKS will bowl first.

Curran says that they bowled well in the last game and are confident of doing so again today. Adds that Dhawan is getting closer to a return and hopes to have him back in the side soon. Liam Livingstone and Nathan Ellis come in, with Kagiso Rabada being one of the omissions. Kohli says that Faf du Plessis will not field today but will be used as an Impact Player, with Vijaykumar Vyshak coming into the XI when they field. .

2:53pm Not long left now before the toss. If Livingstone is fit, who does he replace? Raza was the Player of the Match in PBKS' last game, and Short has looked good at 3. Curran and Rabada, you'd assume, are pretty un-droppable because of what they bring to the table. RCB might have lesser selection headaches, although they might look at replacing Parnell with Willey.

Thomas: "Hoping to see Willey in place of Parnell today - RCB need the better batter and Willey has been consistently good with the ball so far"

Let's see what the conditions have in store for us. Daren Ganga reckons there could be a bit of weather (or rain) around. There was a bit of overnight rain, although the sun is shining as things stand. The pitch is bang in the middle of the square, meaning that the square boundaries are equidistant. Rohan Gavaskar says the pitch has not been watered because of the overnight rain. While he reckons it is a dry surface, he does not expect it to cause batters problems and expects the runs to flow.

Afeef: "I can't wait any longer to see Livingstone in action!"

While we await the toss, do jump into Matt Roller's preview, where he chronicles the contrasting trajectories these two teams have enjoyed in recent IPL seasons, while also illustrating how today's fixture is one neither team would really want to lose.

2:30pm Match 27 of IPL 2023, and it pits the Punjab Kings against the Royal Challengers Bangalore. Both teams, on paper, have superstars in their ranks but have had a stop-start campaign so far. PBKS have won thrice (in five attempts), while RCB have lost thrice (again, in five games).

Both teams, rather similarly, have been over-dependent on a few individuals with the bat. Shikhar Dhawan, in the early part of the season, almost single-handedly kept PBKS afloat. He missed their last game, though, and is a major doubt for today. The Kings, thus, might have to find a way to score runs without their regular skipper, especially if they bat first.

RCB, on the other hand, slumped to an eight-run defeat against the Chennai Super Kings, despite Faf du Plessis and Glenn Maxwell producing astonishing knocks. Virat Kohli fell early in that chase but irrespective of that, their batting unit seems too reliant on this aforementioned troika.

In fact, that is what this contest could boil down to. Both sides' shortcomings have already surfaced this season. PBKS, you could argue, have masked those better than RCB so far. To win today, though, both outfits must aim for something similar.

It is not quite the top-of-the-table clash we had yesterday, but this fixture does provide PBKS an opportunity to go level with the Lucknow Super Giants and the Rajasthan Royals, while offering RCB a chance to emerge out of the mid-table logjam they are currently a part of.

postText:
5:07pm That was a strange innings by RCB. They raced out of the traps in the powerplay and went at close to 10 runs per over. Thereafter, they slowed down drastically, despite having two set batters at the crease. Kohli, in particular, huffed and puffed in the middle overs. While trying to up the ante, he perished to Brar and was soon followed by Maxwell. Du Plessis did get a couple of boundaries away but looked exhausted by the time he was dismissed by Ellis. Karthik, too, could not provide RCB with the finishing kick they craved.

While RCB's batting plans left a little to be desired, PBKS must be applauded for how they used the conditions. They brought out their changes of pace and largely refrained from bowling in the slot. The pitch did help their cutters to grip, and they now have a target that they will be confident of chasing down, despite the surface showing signs of tiring. Do join us in a bit for the second innings!

postText:
7:27pm Right. That will be that from us for this game. The Delhi Capitals, though, are lining up to play the Kolkata Knight Riders later in the evening, and make sure you join us for that match as well. Until next time, this is me (Shashwat) signing off on behalf of Ranjith, Thilak and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo! Goodbye and take care!

Mohammed Siraj, Player of the Match: (On Taide's wicket) The first ball was a little short. Then, I tried to bowl a little fuller because I was getting shape. If I pick wickets in the powerplay, the opposition is put under pressure. The lockdown was very important for me. I was quite down before that because I used to be expensive earlier. I focussed on my gym training, on my bowling and I wanted to do well. Even in the ODIs, my rhythm was good, my confidence was high and I have brought that into this season of the IPL. I am a good fielder; I just make a few mistakes once in a while (smiles). I always try to keep improving on every aspect so that I can remain a part of the team.

Virat Kohli, Royal Challengers Bangalore captain: This (win) does not make us an invincible team or the league position before today did not make us a bad team. The table cannot define your mood, when you have just played five or six games. Maintain our processes and stay in the moment. In the first half, the conditions changed drastically. Faf batted outstandingly well. We thought of extending our partnership for as long as possible so that it could give us an extra 20 runs. After overs 7-8, as soon as the ball was getting bashed into the square, the ball really started getting scuffed up. We changed our strategy then to bat deeper. Had we stayed in, we could have given a crack at 190-200. We felt 175 was a good score on this pitch. I told them that was more than enough. All we had to do was be confident and hold the ball in hand looking to get wickets. The way you win games in T20 cricket is by taking wickets. At the half-way stage, the idea was to take the game to the opposition in the first six overs. We broke the game open right there and our fielding was brilliant as well.

Sam Curran, Punjab Kings captain: (On the score) I thought we bowled really well as a group. The way Faf and Virat played was good. I did not think they got away from us too much. In the end, we just did not bat well enough. They bowled pretty well as well but we lost wickets. The conditions were quite strange as well. we thought it would rain at one stage, with all the lightning and thunder. (On the pitch) It was a really good wicket with good-sized boundaries, you want a fair contest between bat and ball. Just a couple of things with the bat that we might regret but we move on to Saturday. The games come thick and fast, so it is about learning from this.

Wanindu Hasaranga: When we were batting first, I saw the wicket gripping so I tried to bowl my wicket-taking options every time. (On the run out) That was unbelievable. RCB is always a good franchise and I am enjoying very much.

7:03pm The scoreboard might say that RCB have won this game by 24 runs but it was full of twists and turns. Siraj breathed fire in the powerplay and accounted for Livingstone and Taide, with Short falling to Hasaranga. Prabhsimran, though, continued on his merry way, putting the bowlers under pressure whenever he could. That ploy to keep attacking, however, ultimately backfired as PBKS simply did not have enough wickets in hand towards the end. Jitesh tried his best to keep his side afloat but could not get them past the finish line.

While PBKS were a little reckless with their stroke-play, RCB must be lauded for how they bowled. Their bowling changes worked, and it started right in the powerplay when Kohli brought Hasaranga on. Siraj was used as a partnership-breaker and they held their nerve just when it mattered at the end.
