8.30pm Evening all, Warner's got his Capitals in a huddle, Phil Salt among them too. And out comes Salt's England team-mate Jason Roy to open the KKR innings, alongside Litton Das, making his IPL debut too. Ishant Sharma will take the new ball, in his first outing of the season. All change!

8.28pm The first ball is barely two minutes away, and here comes Miller again to get things going in Delhi. No rain, only play...

Delhi Capitals: 1 David Warner (capt), 2 Mitchell Marsh, 3 Manish Pandey, 4 Phil Salt (wk), 5 Lalit Yadav, 6 Aman Khan, 7 Axar Patel, 8 Kuldeep Yadav, 9 Anrich Nortje, 10 Ishant Sharma, 11 Mukesh Kumar. The five subs are: Shaw, Dhull, Sarfaraz, Sakariya and Ripal Patel

Zayan: "Mixed feelings for a Bangladeshi fan... Mustafizur dropped but Litton making his debut..."

8.15pm Finally, the coin is flipped. DC decide to bowl. Warner says that with the weather around, he wanted to bowl first. Ishant and Salt are in, and Porel and Mustafizur are out. Rana announces four changes... and predictably, remembers hardly any of them.

John Carter: "We would need different balls on Mars though" --- Red ball on the red planet? No matter it's T20; it's Mars after all

8.11pm So the match starts at 8.30pm, and no overs have been lost. The toss will be at 8.15pm. Stay tuned.

Nitish: "@Hari... IPL will collaborate with Elon Musk to shift it to Mars if anything happens on Earth" --- Very well... with stadiums there covered by powerful electricity-emitting roofs, and what not

8.02pm Strangely enough, the players are checking out the pitch, while the coaching staff is busy chatting around, even under respectable rain. And just as I type that, they all rush back; and the covers are back too. Now the inspection has been pushed to 8.15pm.

Hari: "The way these climatic changes are happening, I m wondering if we will have an IPL in 2050 at all." --- I'm sure they'll find a way out to make IPL happen through rain, storm and hail very soon

Sabyasachi Ghos: "Send some rain here in Kolkata and get the match started." --- Why not? The kalbaisakhi has descended, after all

Drip, dripper, drippest... the rain has has picked up in Delhi, as I enter the action. Hello everyone! Three large covers are firmly rolled over, even as some of the players keep practising one one side of the ground. Next inspection at 8pm. And, and... the covers are now being removed, as rain has stopped.

7.45pm Well, the inspection is due, but to judge by the rather large raindrops sploshing on the covers, it's all a bit redundant for now. Here's Himanshu to take up the drip-by-drip commentary.

Bhargav Mitra: "Delhi Kolkata always had a history of getting affected by rain, The first washed out match in the 2008 IPL was the Kolkata leg match of Delhi Kolkata. Also Unmukt Chand's debut duck match against Brett Lee was affected by rain. "

7.34pm There will be an inspection at 7.45pm, in just over ten minutes' time. Let's see what's what then.

7.22pm As if Delhi Capitals haven't had a rough enough time of it in this campaign, they've suffered a spate of bat thefts too

... yes, yes, insert your own jokes. But let's hope their luck turns soon.

Venkat: "If this match gets called off, it's a blessing for DC as they would opened their account in the points table."

Deva: "Is chasing no longer a good option. Last 4 games were won by visiting teams who were asked to bat first.. Worried for DC.. Fingers crossed.. Wish this gets posted.. Btw, Happy Eid al Fitr Mubarak to all cricinfo lovers !!!!"

7.08pm So, Bangalore have held firm against Punjab, which makes things very tasty in the upper echelons of the IPL table. If KKR win tonight, we could have six teams on six points in the middle of the standings. Delhi, if they weren't already, will soon be feeling pretty lonely at the foot there.

6.51pm I sense we are in for a delay, as the covers are still on for the moment. But sit tight... indeed, the delay is now official. The pitch and run-up are under covers, but the players are practising on the edges of the square.

Ayeed: "Time for KKR to give Liton Das a go?…said every ardent Bangladesh fan"

Vinod Rajpal: "Hey Andrew, u watching RCB vs Punjab Kings? Its getting tenae over there…. I am smelling the 1st Super Over of this season ! " Indeed I am... 30 off 18 with wickets running out. Drama!

6.45pm We're about 15 minutes away from the toss, although there has been some rain around today, so fingers crossed that there's no delay. It does seem to have eased off, I'm hearing. But hopefully our spies at the Feroz can be more enlightening.

Meanwhile, over in Mohali, things are hotting up for Punjab Kings in their run-chase against RCB.

SandyKam: "Dark clouds loom over the stadium as it's drizzling. I'm here all the way from Houston Texas, hope I get to see a game. "

Akhil: "I'm 15 kms from the stadium and looks like it can rain any moment now."

6.30pm Good evening and welcome to Delhi for Match 28 of the 2023 IPL. And the question on everyone's lips is ... can Delhi Capitals break their duck before their mathematical hopes are over? Five losses in five outings as we near the tournament's halfway mark doesn't augur well. But a win tonight, and they will be just two points adrift of their visitors, Kolkata Knight Riders, who are themselves looking vulnerable after back-to-back losses. And yet, if KKR can get back to winning ways (and let's face it, it's not out of the question), then they in turn will be just two points off the top of the table. It's all up for grabs tonight!

How much DC would have liked to win with five overs remaining! Though it was a pitch where the ball stopped and gripped, the hosts made it difficult for themselves by almost getting into a shell in the last five overs. Anyway, they are off the mark at last, and will hope they can carry this confidence. Until next time, it is goodnight and goodbye from Delhi for today!

Ishant Sharma is the Player of the Match for 2 for 19: "I was just waiting for my chance. That's all I was thinking. Every single day the areas [of bowling] change... we talk about the plans. There's no lucky charm in the team. We want to win every single game from here."

David Warner on their first win: "Great to get the two points. It's awesome; we are really proud of the bowling unit. We asked for wickets in the powerplay, and they did that. Again we lost wickets in a cluster. We can have those upfront conversations. We played an okay game."

Time for the presentations

Sourav Ganguly, DC'S Director of Cricket: "I was thinking it was like my first Test: happy to get off the mark! We have bowled well this season. These are good pitches and fast outfields, but the problem is the batting. We need to go back and look at ourselves as to how we can do better. Nortje has been outstanding. Good to see Ishant and Mukesh. I wouldn't say it is an inexperienced line-up... Many of them have been around for a long time. They also know it's time to put up a better batting performance."

Nitish Rana reflects on the close loss: "We were 15-20 runs short, and we knew the wicket wasn't easy. I should have batted longer, and at that time, my wicket was crucial. Credit to the bowlers, if they can even fight with this total. The plan was just to delay [their win]. Credit to DC too for their batting in the powerplay. We need to play well as a team... I'm sure we are playing well if we can fight even with such a low score."

Rahul: "Missed stumpings and fielding errors cannot happen when defending a low total..."

12.20am They get the points, but DC will ask themselves why and how they took it that far. At one stage, they needed 24 to win from 30 balls, with six wickets in hand; that went down to seven required from the last over. The KKR spinners turned the screw - even Nitish Rana and Anukul Roy contributed - but missed stumpings and fumbles in the field cost them in the end. Anyway, apart from the two points, Warner returning to his attacking best will encourage DC. Remember, they are still well and truly in the race. Stick around for the presentations.

Thanks for your company. Look forward to seeing ya'll very soon.

The entire Sunrisers team seems to have occupied space around MS Dhoni as they listen to his pearls of wisdom. Makes for a great picture.

And here he is for the post-match chat. MS Dhoni: All said and done, it's the last phase of my career, however long I play [On the roar and crowd support]. After two years, the fans have had the opportunity to come here and watch, feels good to be here. Crowd has given us a lot of love and affection. Not getting enough chances to bat, but no complaints. I was hesitant to bat second because I had that feeling there won't be a lot of dew. When there are chances dew, you have to bat second. Spinners once they came in, bowled a very good length. Fast bowlers once they came back, especially Pathirana, bowled superbly."

After all the serious questions are out of the way, Dhoni says he has a quibble. And that's because they didn't give him the 'catch of the match award.'

Ravindra Jadeja should be the player of the match for his three-for now that Conway has already given us a flash interview. Yes, it is Jadeja! "The moment I come here and see the wicket, it's always a happy feeling," he beams. "Also, the boundary on one side is a lot bigger."

10.49pm CSK's march continues, but they remain third on the points table, behind on NRR to Royals and LSG. It's also their second win on the bounce, their fourth overall. They didn't even give SRH a whiff in their chase of a smallish score thanks to Devon Conway whose dream season continues. He now has three successive half-centuries at the top of the order.

Aiden Markram: Never nice to lose, disappointed. Let ourselves dow with the bat. Lacked partnerships of substance. It wasn't a 130-odd wicket, more closer to 160. Tough to get momentum if you don't have partnerships. They bowled well in the middle overs, didn't give us much to score of. We knew their spinners will play a big role, it was more about each person having his own plan to counter that. The guys had their plans but we couldn't get it right tonight ultimately. We need some wins now, have to see how we can get better with the bat. Proud how the bowlers stuck it out and took the game deep. Gonna take 1-2 guys to put their hands up, hopefully we can get it right the next game.

Devon Conway after his third-straight half-century: Nice to be there in the end and get the win. Plan for us is simple. Every game, doesn't change too much. Play good cricket shows in the power play and put the bowlers under pressure. We try and look to repeat that regardless of what the score is. We probably got the best of the conditions, probably didn't hold as much as it did in the first innings. Pitch we experienced in Bangalore was a lot better. We knew we didn't have to be too reckless here.

7.40pm That's that then. In the words of KL Rahul, "We don't know what happened." I am sure the teams will figure it out. It is not the end for them. LSG still in the top half of the table but they have played one extra match. Thanks for joining us. See you tomorrow.

7.36pm Mohit Sharma is the PotM. He says, and this is not verbatim: Nothing special, it is all normal. Consistency and experience is there, but it is all process. That's the speciality of this team: whether you do well or do badly, you go back and follow the same process. We never lost the belief. Hardik kept telling us from ball one that we are winning the match. Just keep doing your job. That belief was always there, that is special. I was only focusing on executing my plan. I tried to be clear in my head. Whether I am bowling the slower bouncer or the yorker, the batter shouldn't be able to predict.

7.32pm Hardik Pandya says, and this is not verbatim: After the two games we lost, this seems like god is telling us I am not always going to take from you, I will give to you too. The way the environment changed when we got wickets, the belief we had, was wonderful to watch. In a tournament like this, one loss can break you, but such a win can do the opposite. At best, we could have got 10 more. That's how the wicket was. During the strategic timeout, we spoke about the set batter batting longer because the new batter was going to find it difficult. When there was 30 required off 30, I felt they were ahead. We started sniffing something when it came down to 27 off 4 overs. A run a ball off 10 overs is different, but when it comes down to 24 off 24, you know a mistake can cost you the game. That's when the game changes. The amount of cricket Mo has played, I didn't need to tell him anything. The calmness, planning and execution he showed, it was tremendous. At the same time, Shami showed his experience. Mohit and Shami were tremendous. Special mention to Jayant as well, playing after such a long time. Obviously Noor, that guy has some talent.

7.25pm In the end, KL Rahul took it deep and laid it all on the on -pace over from Mohammed Shami. He missed two leg-side balls there. They back themselves to hit those for sixes all the time. It wasn't to be. But the question is: should the set batter take it all on himself or should he try to finish it quickly and if he gets out early, the new batter gets time to get his eye in?

7.20pm KL Rahul is at a loss for words. He says, and this is not verbatim: I don't know how it has happened. It happened too fast. I can't put a finger on where we let the game slip, which was in our pocket. We were quite brilliant with the ball and in the field. 135 is probably par or 10 under par. We used the conditions well. We started pretty well with the bat too. I still can't say what happened. At the end of the day it is just a game, we still have four wins in seven, but this is going to sting for a while. We were well ahead in the game, I wasn't trying to bat really deep, I was still trying to take the bowlers on that I fancy. They bowled three good overs between Noor and Jayant. Probably should have taken a couple more chances. Not an easy wicket for new batters to come in. Set batters need to finish the game. We missed some boundary opportunities in the end. We should have got it done.

7.13pm Wow. Conditions are king. It all looked sealed and done. When the last boundary was hit, LSG needed 39 off 45 with nine wickets in hand. GT even dropped two catches. Still the defensive bowling on a slow pitch was superb. KL Rahul kept putting off the risks until the 19th over when he got pace on the ball. Wickets fell on the other end because the strategy seemed to be for others to go after the bowling. In the end, Mohit Sharma and Mohammed Shami bowled superbly in the last three. Forty-five balls without a boundary. Heartbreak, desperate heartbreak for KL Rahul. Ecstasy for GT

postText:
We've had different styles of entertainment on the Saturday double header. The first saw a winding, nervy turnaround win for the defending champions Gujarat Titans against Lucknow Super Giants and a high-scoring game here saw 25 sixes hit. Hope you enjoyed it all. You can check out Hemant's report here. Lots of content gushing in from the IPL on ESPNcricinfo, check it out. Double header coming up tomorrow as well, join us then. Goodbye for now from me, Ekanth, and our scorers Chandan Duorah and Ranjith P.

KipEetSimpul: "Batting 1st on belters may be a better strategy for teams with strong batting line-ups and weaker bowling squads...the CSKvRCB and PKvMI games are the latest examples "

Sam Curran, PBKS Captain is the POTM: Special win. Amazing ground, played many games with different sides. Great to get the win. Don't think I should be getting the award, with the way our pacers finished the match, Arshdeep and Nathan were incredible and the spinners bowled well. When I went in to bat, I knew I had to give myself a chance. In the previous games, I've looked to go big a little too early, reflected on that. But we got a long line-up and we saw Jitesh went bang-bang and we know he's got that. He's a massive player and we just have to take our responsibility as players come back from injuries. (On captaincy) Two from three, I think we can go back to Shikhar. Great experience, the coaches and the local guys are helping me through. Bayliss, Haddin and Co have created a good, relaxed environment. We've won a few early games which helps.

Afeef: "Not often that Livingstone hits a big six and gets upstaged thrice in the same match by others!"

Mustafa Moudi : "After that 31 Expensive Over, Yash Dayal was dropped and has not chances of return. Can this happed to Arjun Tendulkar ??" Could be, hard not to feel for Arjun as was the case with Dayal. But very much a possibility.

Arshdeep Singh: Feels good whenever I take wickets, the win makes the feeling better. Before IPL, I changed my run-up and it helped me with avoiding no-balls. The rhythm is nice and I'm enjoying my cricket right now. (Mindset) Calmness comes naturally, my heart rate doesn't even go up to 120 (laughs)

Rohit Sharma, MI Captain: We had some errors in the field but not gonna look too much into that. Will tell the boys to keep our heads high, we've won and lost three. Lots of time left in the tournament, we need to stay in the game and competition. Quite happy with Green and SKY's batting, they kept us in the game till the end. Credit to Arshdeep for his bowling, not our day today but we gave a good fight.

Today's match was in the action/thriller genre. There was no messing about. Kings had an innings of two contrasting halves with the bat. In the chase, it was a tug of war. Lest we forget, Arshdeep got a wicket with the new ball. But after Kishan was dismissed, Green and Rohit combined to put on a 76-run stand. They took 50 balls but after Livingstone removed Rohit, Green and SKY put on 75 off just 36. The slower balls worked better than the pace-on ones but the fours and sixes weren't few or far between. Curran, Chahar, Ellis and Livingstone all went over 10 but Arshdeep's death bowling won it for the visitors.

11:22pm: Arshdeep Singh is getting hugs from everywhere and boy does he deserve them. Mumbai were in the contest, they were even ahead at some points. Rohit, Green, SKY and David kept the momentum going but Arshdeep's magic: 11 for 3 in his last two overs, helped Kings clinch the six fest.

RR 1 Jos Buttler, 2 Yashasvi Jaiswal, 3 Sanju Samson (capt. & wk), 4 Devdutt Padikkal, 5 Shimron Hetmyer, 6 Dhruv Jurel, 7 R Ashwin, 8 Jason Holder, 9 Trent Boult, 10 Sandeep Sharma, 11 Yuzvendra Chahal

3pm Sanju Samson has won the toss, and RR have decided to bowl first. "Looking at their side and our side, we will like to bowl first," he says. He says the same bowling XI as the last match. Virat Kohli says he would have wanted to bat first anyway. He says it is quite dry, will slow down, and he is pointing to spike marks on the pitch already. Kohli says the only change is David Willey for Wayne Parnell is the only change in their team.

2.55pm The pitch for this match is the centre strip. So no bigger or smaller boundary. Aaron Finch reports it is a "really dry" surface too. So, as I said, please don't expect 200s here. And also expect the side winning the toss to bat first. We might see Adam Zampa come in today. Also I can report that Virat Kohli is going out for the toss, which means Faf du Plessis is not going to field. Looks like David Willey is going to replace Wayne Parnell in the RCB XI.

2.50pm Ten minutes to the toss. Can RCB address their batting line-up outside of du Plessis, Kohli and Maxwell? Which Indian batter to RR pick for their middle order? Parag or Jurel?Neal: "RCB are the competition's sleeping giant without an IPL title. Making a move on the leaders tonight and who knows where it might lead. "

2.40pm It is an afternoon game, the annual green fixture for RCB. Their kits this afternoon are green and made from recycled stadium waste. Gratitude is due to Sri Lanka for showing the way: they have been using recycled waste for their kits for a while now. I wonder if Faf du Plessis will wear a green cap to the toss or his Aramco Orange Cap. Speaking of, Mohammed Siraj is in the running for the Aramco Purple Cap.

Ekanth Prakash is our man at the ground. He describes the scenes thus: "Hot day at the Chinnaswamy and the crowd are making their way in. 7.02 The news from the middle is that Delhi has won the toss and chosen to bat first.

6.30 pm Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of today's encounter in the 2023 Indian Premier League as Sunrisers Hyderabad host Delhi Capitals. I'm Peter Della Penna to take you through today's action.

Both sides are trying to dig their way out of the cellar on the 2023 IPL points table. postText:
11.16 pm This was a dogfight for sure. But Delhi somehow outscrap Sunrisers on Hyderabad's home turf to leave with their second win in a row. Meanwhile, Sunrisers have now lost three straight.

Sunrisers Hyderabad captain Aiden Markram: "Not good with the bat again, not enough intent. We looked a team that was not excited to win a game of cricket unfortunately. We'll have to go back to look how we can chase better, be more free as a team and as a unit and hopefully that can help us going forward. It's difficult. You can say all the right things but ultimately guys need to buy into it. We want to play a certain brand of cricket and if we get it wrong doing that then we'll sleep a lot better at night. But unfortunately tonight, just lacked a bit of intent. We've got really good players and really good batters and unfortunately I think we're just letting ourselves down through lack of intent. Guys need to work out what brings out the best in them and makes them the most free to play. [On the bowlers] Incredibly proud of them and executed great game plans, kept it pretty simple and used the conditions pretty well tonight. It's a pity we couldn't get the job done for them. Our bowlers didn't deserve to be on the losing side like this tonight."

Delhi Capitals bowler Anrich Nortje: "Obviously really happy to get the win. Still not the ideal performance, probably a few runs short. Bowling, I thought the spinners bowled really well and one or two of the seamers as well at stages, and then at the end, unbelievable finish. What an over [by Mukesh]. The [batters from the first innings] said there was some inconsistency on a good length so try straight lines and hit the wicket and see if we can get some inconsistency with some cutters here and there. [On bowling at the death] Just try to keep it as simple as possible. Just focus on the target and go. [On facing Klaasen] I'm not gonna lie, the plan wasn't to bowl half-volleys. But it's definitely a good challenge. [On Mukesh's last over] He was very clear. Kudos to him. He did an unbelievable job. He really focused well in that last over, took his time and executed. So it was so good to see and really inspiring."

Delhi Capitals captain David Warner: "I love it here. It's an amazing crowd. I haven't been here for a long time. Thankfully my hair can only go white from here, it can't go gray. This game throws up some challenges. Mukesh there under pressure was absolutely amazing and our two spinners were great. You don't want them to get used to bowlers in back-to-back bowlers so if I can maneuver them around in the middle overs it can work. [On Ishant] Credit to him. He's worked very hard to get back into the IPL and to bowl as well as he did was exceptional. To win tonight, hopefully we can make it three in a row. We've got another against Sunrisers next."

Axar Patel named Player of the Match for his 34 off 34 and two wickets in the chase.

That's it for today's live coverage. Come back tomorrow for some more live IPL coverage. Until then, take care!

7.28pm The umpires have walked out, the openers jog out with their shadow batting, and Mumbai are in a huddle. Saha and Gill opening, as usual, and they don't have a fifty stand this IPL yet. In fact, their average is the second worst so far, only behind Shaw and Warner. Tendulkar to open the bowling again, Mumbai backing him like they should. No slip, short third in the circle and Saha on strike. Let's get this rolling...

7.20pm Thanks Abhimanyu. Lots to look forward to in the first innings: when do Mumbai bring on Chawla? (their best bowler this season), how do they sort their death bowling problems after the last game, what total is safe on this high-scoring ground if there's little or no dew?

7.15pm Time to welcome Vishal to the hot seat as he takes you through the first innings!

7.07pm Here are the teams:

Gujarat Titans XI: Wriddhiman Saha (wk), Shubman Gill, Hardik Pandya (capt), Abhinav Manohar, Vijay Shankar, David Miller, Rahul Tewatia, Rashid Khan, Mohammed Shami, Noor Ahmad, Mohit Sharma

Substitutes: Josh Little, Dasun Shanaka, R Sai Kishore, KS Bharat, Shivam Mavi

Mumbai Indians XI: Rohit Sharma (capt), Ishan Kishan (wk), Cameron Green, Suryakumar Yadav, Tim David, Nehal Wadhera, Riley Meredith, Arjun Tendulkar, Kumar Kartikeya, Piyush Chawla, Jason Behrendorff

Substitutes: Ramandeep Singh, Tilak Varma, Shams Mulani, Vishnu Vinod, Sandeep Warrier

Hardik Pandya says that Josh Little is back in. He doesn't remember who for!

7pm Toss time! Rohit Sharma calls it right and Mumbai Indians will bowl first. Says he wants to make the most of the conditions as they are expecting some moisture. Two changes for Mumbai Indians: Jofra Archer is not well so Riley Meredith is replacing him. Kumar Kartikeya replaces Hrithik Shokeen.

Srinivas PT: "Hardik Pandya not in the WTC test squad due to availability or injury or pure selection decision?" He has expressed that due to his fitness and workload, he is happy to play the white-ball formats right now, although he hasn't entirely ruled out a return to Test cricket.

Abhishek: "I remember watching 2011 India vs Aus quarterfinal in office with my manager then. Not worth it :)"

Manu Ajmani: "Don't they have to submit the playing XI along with the substitute before the toss or is it just this IPL that you can hand out caps based on if a team is batting or bowling?" In this season of the IPL, the rule has been introduced that teams can name their XI after the toss, depending on what they are doing.

Pitch report: Matthew Hayden from the ground says it is unusually humid in Gujarat. He suggests the bounce will be traditional, but the ball may grip for the spinners and the middle overs may be tough for the batters. Little chance for dew, so batting first may be a good way to go.

NethraReya: "Under 40 mins to start, manager sitting facing me at work, the moment he looksaway, I will escape home to watch this classic!!" Fingers crossed for you. Until then, you know where you can get all the action! (HERE, that is)

Patel: "Ava De~Bring it on!" I suppose this is a more authoritative answer than mine.

Samrat Ahuja: "Any cap being handed over today in any camp??" Does not look like it. Although, sometimes caps are handed out after the toss this season, as teams are picked on the basis of whether they are batting first or bowling.

6.48pm While Hardik Pandya gave the team talk to the Gujarat Titans huddle, it's Jason Behrendorff animatedly addressing the Mumbai Indians huddle from the middle.

Monjul: "Titan catch phrase 'ava de', what does it mean and how it is related to cricket?" It basically means "let them come"!

Karthik: "Shane Warne also won the tile in his first season in charge." This is true, although that was the first season for everyone!

Aditya: "Mumbai are the only side in the IPL that the Gujarat Titans have never beaten!" Indeed. The two teams faced off just once last season, with Mumbai Indians winning by a narrow margin of five runs.

Mustafa Moudi : "Fun Fact: Yash Dayal and Arjun Tendulkar, the only 2 bowlers to concede 31 Runs in an over this season belongs to these 2 sides !!"

In the points table, Gujarat Titans are currently fourth and a win will see them go level on points with toppers Chennai Super Kings. Mumbai Indians, meanwhile will look to be one of the six teams with eight points after seven games played with a win today.

Arjun Tendulkar, in his short IPL career so far, has seen the highs of getting his first wicket and then found out how difficult life is at this level as he was taken for 31 runs against Punjab Kings. But Tom Moody feels Mumbai Indians should back him to do the job at the death. Shaun Tait, meanwhile, says that Jofra Archer could take just one game to "light it up" and be back to his very best after an indifferent start to his Mumbai Indians career. All this and more in our video preview.

6.35pm This game will be another chance for the young Tilak Varma to shine. According to former India coach Ravi Shastri, he is banging the Indian team's door down with his performances over this season and the last one.

You can also track the game with our ball-by-ball commentary in Hindi and in Tamil.

6.30pm It's Match 35 of IPL 2023 and it is defending champions Gujarat Titans up against the team that has won the title five times, Mumbai Indians. Mumbai Indians went on a three-game winning streak before their defeat against Punjab Kings, while Gujarat Titans recorded an unlikely win in their last match against Lucknow Super Giants. Rohit Sharma is up against Hardik Pandya, the only two Indian captains to win the title in their first season in charge. You can read about that and a lot more in Srinidhi Ramanujam's preview. I am Abhimanyu Bose and I will be joined soon by Vishal Dikshit as we bring you all the action from Ahmedabad today.

postText:
9.16pm What a batting show from Titans on their home ground! They were just 50 for 1 in the powerplay and initial it looked like even 170-180 would be good here with some swing around, and the way Chawla was keeping the scoring down. But the way Manohar and Miller blasted those seven sixes together in a rapid stand after the platform laid by Gill's fifty, Mumbai had no answers in the end. They leaked 70 runs in the death (17-20) today - the most so far this IPL - that too after conceding 65 in the last game against Punjab Kings. Lots of questions to answer for their bowling, but for now they'll want to hunt this down with their batting firepower. Abhimanyu will take you through the chase.

Abhinav Manohar: I went in when a few wickets fell so Ashu pa (Nehra) told me to carry on for three and we knew we could make up for the runs in the end because we have the firepower and it paid off. There was an effort to get more runs in the middle over, and Hardik also said if we can go after their main bowler like Piyush Chawla…First six overs will be important with the ball moving, I'm sure our bowlers will do it.

ROY: "Very sad to see Arjun been kept under the wraps for death bowling. If you have to become a complete bowler, you will go for runs but one day you will achieve your mark."

AK: "Not sure for what they were protecting Tendulkar Jr for? He was good in the first two overs and they knew Meredith and Behrendorff were leaking runs. "

Adarsh: "MI's gamble on two injury-prone stars failed badly. 8 overs of Bumrah Archer in every game, and things would have been totally different."

Arun Prakash: "Tewatia's impact to GT cannot be measured just by looking at scorecard. That 5 ball 20 is as good as Gill's 50"

Bharat Anne: "This Innings is a crispy spring breeze after yesterday's airless match"

postText:
11.45pm So there you have it. Gujarat Titans go level on points with table-toppers Chennai Super Kings, but are still below them on net run rate. Mumbai Indians stay seventh after back-to-back defeats. You can read Vishal's report for all the details of what went down in Ahmedabad tonight. There's more IPL action tomorrow of course, with RCB taking on KKR. For now, it's me, Abhimanyu, signing off on behalf of Vishal, Chandan and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo.

Abhinav Manohar is the Player of the Match: "I think I am lucky to be in this franchise. In the net sessions we are given the freedom to bat as much as we want. I think I have been gifted to time the ball well and I've been doing it from a young age and to do it at this level it feels special, it feels like a dream. In this game I couldn't go from ball one due to the situation but it was good to get my eye in and play my game."

The winning captain, Hardik Pandya: "That has always been my motto. In captaincy I take the call in the moment rather than pre-planned. Captaincy is something where I just always bounce my instinct. Me and Ashu Pa have a very similar mindset and 99% of the times we back our calls and they are similar calls. Today bowling Rashid and Noor we knew we can take off pace against batters like Green and David who like pace on the ball. [On Manohar] It's pure hard work, the amount of balls he hits in the nets and credits to the support staff as well. Last year we spoke to him and this year so far he has been hitting it the best in the team. We are very happy and looking forward to more innings like that"

11.33pm Time for the presentation ceremony

Harshit: "True MoM should be Shami. He bowled open spell so well that Mumbai could never take off. " He probably won't get it, and one of the batters will, but I do think that his opening spell was a breathtaking one. Ishan Kishan could barely get bat on ball! Very unlucky not to finish with a wicket today.

Atul Ghai : "Do you use voice to text software to transcribe the interviews?" Nah, we have to hear the voice and type the text!

Rubie: "Most runs conceded in the last four overs this season? What about,Punjab sixing 96 runs in the last 5 overs earlier?" In the last five overs of a game, that is indeed the highest this season.

Mayank Sawhney: "Junior Tendulkar has outscored Senior Tendulkar in his First IPL Appearance with the Bat. Sachin had scored 12 in his First IPL Match for MI against CSK in 2008 and Arjun made 13 today :) "

Rashid Khan: It's just few things. To be consistent with line and length. Good to get a few wickets but just working on a few things. A few areas where I don't want to bowl but it's going there. The first few overs, to keep them a little bit quiet... In this wicket if you are hitting the right area it makes it hard for the batsmen. It's great to have him in the side and have this bowling partnership with him. He just wants to learn and he is just working so hard. Last year he was bowling hard in the nets and just keeps asking questions. Even when I am in the gym he would come to me and ask. That's how much he wants to get better and perform and now he is delivering so I am so happy. That's great news for GT and also for Afghanistan."

MI captain, Rohit Sharma: "It's a little disappointing. We pretty much had control of the game till the last few overs when we went for too many runs. It's just about execution. We need to execute what's right, who are the batsmen, those kind of things. But in the end we didn't do that and gave too many runs. You've got to look at every team has very different strengths. We have a strong batting lineup to achieve the target. Today our batting couldn't get going. There's a lot of dew as well so if we had batted well then maybe we would have chased it. But we didn't start well and you don't do that when you are chasing 200-plus."

11.20pm After an incredible batting display, Gujarat Titans backed it up with a classy show with ball in hand. Shami and Hardik stifled Mumbai Indians right from the start, with Hardik scalping his opposite number. Rashid Khan and Noor Ahmad then ran through the middle order, picking up five wickets between them. After that, it was all just merely a formality, even as Nehal Wadhera played an enterprising knock and Piyush Chawla hit a few boundaries. Earlier on, Shubman Gill set up Titans' innings after they were put in to bat. Abhinav Manohar, David Miller and Rahul Tewatia then amped it up at the death as MI conceded 70 runs in the last four -- the most by any team in IPL 2023.

6.55pm One boundary is smaller than the other but does it really matter at Chinnaswamy? Kevin Pietersen says the pitch is quite dry. He says it won't hurt for batters to give themselves three-four balls before they go six hunting.

Mustafa Moudi: "A side highly dependent on Openers Vs a side which is still unsure about their ideal opening pair. Really interesting clash !!"

6.50pm Himanshu Agrawal has important updates from the ground: "Wayne Parnell bowling at full pace on one of the practice pitches. Could be a sign of him playing, with the toss barely ten minutes away. Kohli walking out for the toss. Has a sheet in his hand."

6.45pm We hear Shardul Thakur, who turned the last match around for KKR against RCB, might still not be available for selection although he is at the stadium.

6.40pm KKR won the first match between these two teams this IPL thanks to a freak fifty by Shardul Thakur. It remains one of their only two wins. And it is them who have a lot of questions around their combination. We will soon find out what it is at the toss.

Himanshu Agrawal is at the Chinnaswamy Stadium, and has his eye trained on Andre Russell. He says: "David Willey and Shahbaz Ahmed practice on one side, even as Russell heads out to have a look at the centre pitch. KKR really need runs from him, so maybe assessing the pitch can help."

A touching moment in the end as CV Varun so emotionally spoke about missing the birth of his son. AC Prathiban that he spoke about has played just two first-class matches and one List A game. He played in the TNPL for Trichy Warriors. He has worked on Varun's bowling a lot. That interview is what we end this coverage with. Do join us tomorrow. Cheers.

11.35pm CV Varun is the Player of the Match. He says, and this is not verbatim: That's how the game of cricket is. Last match I went for 49, today I get this award. My focus is on my accuracy, not to add variations. I have been working a lot. I would like to thank AC Prathiban and Abhishek Nayar. I would like to dedicate this to my newborn son and my wife. I will see him after the IPL.

11.30pm Nitish Rana says, and this is a translation from Hindi: Last three-four matches, I have been saying if we start performing as a collective, we will get the results. We have enough character in the dressing room for not giving up the belief despite being where we were in the table. Today we wanted to put up a total and hope for spin to come in. We thought it was dry and it would turn. As such it didn't quite turn but our bowlers turned up. Suyash has always been the first to out his hand up and say I will do it for you. We hope to keep repeating what we did today.

11.20pm Andre Russell says, and this is not verbatim: We really needed that victory. We have been under the pump. We know once we get a good total - and anything above 200 was a good total - we can impart pressure. Once I get the ball, I try to do my best. I try to contribute in whatever way. Still confident with the bat. Got a very good yorker tonight from Siraj. Part of the game. We just got to take it day by day. Recovery is very important for me. The older I get the smarter I get with my body.

11.15pm Virat Kohli says, and this is not verbatim: To be honest we handed over the game to them. We deserved to lose. We weren't professional enough. We bowled well but fielding was not up to standard. This was a freebie handed over to them. In the field, we dropped two chances, that cost us 25-30 runs. When batting, we set us ourselves up very well, but then four-five soft dismissals. Not wicket-taking balls but we hit straight to the fielders. Even while chasing, after losing wickets, one partnership brought us back in the game. We were one partnership short. We need to stay switched on, and not give away soft plays.

11.11pm With that, KKR end their losing run of four matches pretty convincingly. They wanted to bat first, they expected the pitch to slow down, and despite a slowdown in the middle overs, they got to 200 through Roy and Rana. RCB got off to flier, but the spinners pulled them back. For a brief while, there seemed to be someone from outside the big three doing the job, but once Mahipal Lormor fell, a slide began.

Shabeer Komath: "@hemanth, is it mandatory to substitute an overseas player with another one ?" --- Not mandatory, but if you have an overseas players who happens to be an excellent fielder - such as Glenn Phillips for SRH - you would want him to come in as your substitute fielder.

Tom Smith: "Kuldip Yadav is one of the impact subs for RR not Kuldeep Sen as you put in your commentary, Please fix this." --- Thanks for pointing out, this has been fixed.

Azweer : "I just have a doubt. You just can swap only one Impact player in the XI know? Then why do we need a pool of subs?" --- To have different options. If you are batting first and suffer a collapse, you can bring in an extra batter. Else, you strengthen your bowling in the second innings.

Akshath: "Why why why...??? Why do we have an overseas player as a substitute when the playing 11 already has 4 overseas players..!!!" --- To come in as a fielding substitute if one of the four overseas players go off the field for whatever reason.

Navneet : "Why RR hadn't given Joe Root a chance? Is he injured?" --- Don't think he is injured. The question is: whom does he replace?

Sundar: "Oh! Mistake by Royals. CSK is better at chasing because of the inexperience in their bowling (even though their rookies have done reasonably well). Advantage CSK."

For CSK, expect Rayudu to come in as Impact Player when they bat, for one of the bowlers. Royals could bring in Kuldip Yadav KM Asif, or even M Ashwin, depending on how the pitch plays.

7.00pm Rajasthan Royals have won the toss and opted to bat first. "It looks like a really good wicket to bat on," their captain Sanju Samson reasons. "We will take the learnings from the last game but each and every game, opponent, and conditions are different. We would have liked to see more pink here than yellow (laughs). Boulty misses out with a niggle, and Adam Zampa comes in."

"We would have bowled first," says CSK captain MS Dhoni. "This pitch here has decent amount of pace but the bounce is on the lower side so bowlers need to adapt soon. At the end of the day, you need characters, we are trying to build characters, trying to convince them to focus on process. The result doesn't matter. We are playing the same side."

Nagraj Gollapudi is at the venue. He says: "CSK seem to be sticking to the same three seamers and probably XI. Stokes still has his left kneed in a brace although he has been bowling in the side nets with the rest. None of the RR bowlers have yet measured a run-up so not sure if they are likely to make a change."

Pitch report: It's a black-soil pitch with a decent grass covering. The game is being played on the centre pitch, which means there is not longer or shorter side; both square boundaries are 66 metres. Down the ground it's 78 metres. So expect the bowlers to bowl on the fuller side.

9.10pm What a chaotic finish it has been. But in the end, Royals have become the first IPL team to post 200 at this venue. Jaiswal and Buttler once again gave them a flying start. CSK seemed to have staged a comeback in the middle phase but the last five overs produced 63 runs - many of them came when the batters weren't in control. postText:
11.25pm Royals go back into the group of three at the top of the table with 10 points each. They have the best net run rate of that trio: 0.939. With this win, they've also made it 4 out of 4 while batting first. Hope you've enjoyed our coverage tonight. Look forward to your company for the remainder of the season.

Sanju Samson: "This is a win the team and dugout really wanted. The way youngsters Jaiswal, Devdutt, Jurel batted was outstanding, the mindset of attack, attack and attack is something we will keep promoting in the dressing room. Credit goes to the team management and support staff [for working with players like Jaiswal] who work very hard at the academy. Lot of work has gone behind his success. Proud of the way he's playing."

Yashasvi Jaiswal is the Player of the Match for his IPL best, a 43-ball 77.

Akhil: "CSK batters never could guess who is going to ball next over. That's how much good Sanju handled his bowlers today"

MS Dhoni: (pardon the odd paraphrase) They scored quite a bit above par. We gave away too many in the first six. At the same time, wicket was great to bat on. Bowlers bowled well in the middle overs but a lot of edges went for boundaries, at least 5-6 went for them and that had made an impact. They had par-plus and we couldn't get a good start in the power play with the bat. I felt Pathirana's bowling was good, he didn't bowl badly. I think the scorecard doesn't reflect how well he bowled. Yashasvi batted really well, was important to go after the bowlers and it was important to take calculated risks. We had to assess what a good length is, as captain you tell them but initially we have away a few boundaries and after that you're always playing catch up. In the end of the innings, Jurel batted well but I think it's the first six where it got away from us. This is a very special venue, my first ODI hundred in Vizag gave me 10 games but the 183 I made here gave me another one year. It was great to be back here.

Rajkumar: "As a CSK fan, Hope Dhoni is preserving himself for a playoff surprise."

11.10pm CSK were never in this. Not even when Dube got going along with Moeen to inject some late momentum. The start was slow, and the pressure of having to force the pace got to every batter that came along. Conway had an off day, Gaikwad blew hot and cold, Rayudu was out for a two-ball duck and Rahane was consumed by the pressure of going after every ball. Not all's lost though. CSK are still in a fairly good position at third despite this loss. The margin of victory could've been a lot bigger than the eventual result.

4:13pm Russell, on his 35th birthday and in his 100th game for KKR, rings the iconic bell at the Eden Gardens to signify the start of play. Gurbaz and Jagadeesan will open the batting for the hosts. Shami with the new ball for the Titans. Here we go!

sabin: "How does Sai Sudarshan doesn't get a look in the team?" -- Sudharsan has not done much wrong but with Hardik content to play the anchor role, and Abhinav Manohar impressing as a middle-order hitter, GT have gone in without Sudharsan.

ARGON: "Big big blow for KKR with Jason Roy not playing....he was the main reason for quick starts in the powerplay..." -- One man's absence is another man's opportunity. KKR would hope Gurbaz can play a similar kind of role in the powerplay today.

3:52pm Play will start at 4:15pm IST. No overs have been lost.

3:44pm The ground staff has seemingly told the umpires that they can get the ground ready for play by 4:15pm IST. If play starts at that time, we will not lose any overs.

3:30pm Looks like we might have a bit of a delayed start. The pitch and the square is uncovered but there are still some areas where the covers are on. It is not raining at this moment and it might not be long before we get underway. Stay tuned!

You can also track the game with our ball-by-ball commentary in Hindi and in Tamil.

3:17pm Looks like we have some good news. The sun is peeping its way through the clouds and the covers are now being removed.

3:10pm Uh-oh, looks like the rain has arrived. Sreshth Shah, who is at the venue, says that the entire ground is under covers now.

Kolkata Knight Riders XI: Rahmanullah Gurbaz (wk), N Jagadeesan, Venkatesh Iyer, Nitish Rana (c), Rinku Singh, Andre Russell, Sunil Narine, David Wiese, Shardul Thakur, Harshit Rana, Varun Chakravarthy

Substitutes: Suyash Sharma, Mandeep Singh, Anukul Roy, Tim Southee, Kulwant Khejroliya

Gujarat Titans XI: Wriddhiman Saha (wk), Hardik Pandya (c), David Miller, Abhinav Manohar, Vijay Shankar, Rahul Tewatia, Rashid Khan, Mohammed Shami, Mohit Sharma, Josh Little, Noor Ahmad

Substitutes: Shubman Gill, KS Bharat, Sai Sudharsan, Shivam Mavi, Jayant Yadav

3pm It's time for the toss. Nitish Rana gives it a flick. Hardik Pandya calls heads and it comes down as heads. GT will bowl first. Hardik says the decision is because of the weather around and that he would have batted first had the sun been out. Same XI for GT. Rana says he would have batted first anyway, even with the possibility of rain. Harshit Rana comes in for Umesh Yadav, who tweaked his hamstring in the last game. Jason Roy also misses out because of a back niggle, with Rahmanullah Gurbaz replacing him.

GT's last day game was against the Lucknow Super Giants, where they opted to bat first and were ultimately vindicated. Two out of KKR's three wins have also come when they have batted first, with the only exception being the reverse fixture in Ahmedabad.

Afeef: "Looking forward to a special performance from Andre Russell on his 35th birthday " -- KKR could do with one of those Russell performances today.

Let's see what the conditions have in store for us. Pitch No.6 is going to be used today, and Matthew Hayden says the pitch is superb. He wonders, though, whether this track could turn, with the number of world-class spinners on display and this being a day game. There is a bit of abrasiveness and Daren Ganga feels if the pacers change their pace and bowl into the track, they could contain the batters.

As we build up to the toss, here is Alagappan Muthu's preview, where he charts down what we could have in store and how both teams, having played enough games this season, might approach this game with a greater idea of their strengths and weaknesses.

2:30pm It is match 39 and we are back at the Eden Gardens, where the Kolkata Knight Riders have won only once this season. They will, however, take heart from the fact that they're facing the Gujarat Titans today, one of only two teams they have beaten this campaign.

The last time these two sides met, Rinku Singh produced a last-over heist for the ages, smashing Yash Dayal for five consecutive sixes and sealing the deal for KKR. Both outfits have traversed slightly contrasting trajectories since, with KKR winning just once and GT consolidating their spot in the top four.

KKR, because of their win against RCB a few days ago, might not have entered last-chance saloon yet, although the margin for error for them remains minimal. As for Gujarat, they have an opportunity to climb back to the top of the table and fire another warning shot that they are just as dangerous as they were in their debut title-winning season.

postText:
6:04pm Phew, that was a very eventful innings. Gurbaz called the shots in the powerplay and ensured that KKR raced out of the traps, even as they lost a couple of wickets. There was a brief lull thereafter but just like in the powerplay, Gurbaz kept finding the fence whenever KKR needed him to. His sumptuous knock offset Iyer and Rinku's struggles and set the platform for Russell and Wiese - both of whom cleared the fence towards the end and got KKR up to 179.

GT will not be very displeased with this bowling effort, considering six-hitting is not very tough at this venue. Rashid, though, came in for a bit of tap but Little was exceptional, giving away only 25 runs and picking up two wickets. Noor also continued his recent upward trajectory and those performances have meant that GT now have a total they will back themselves to hunt down. Do join us in a bit for the run-chase!

Andre Russell: Feeling good, thanks again for the birthday wishes. I think, looking at the scoreboard, I am not really happy. We have good bowlers and we can fight with this total. (On the pitch) It looks like a 190-200 wicket so we are 20 runs short. We have only ourselves to blame for that. But I am backing our bowlers, including myself. (On his 100th game for KKR) It means a lot. I can't explain it in words. The love I get in Kolkata is just amazing and it is tremendous to represent this franchise. It is like a family.

8:06pm Right. That will be that from us for this game. The action in the IPL, though, does come quite thick and fast. Do hop over to the DC-SRH game, where Abhishek Sharma has given SRH the start they were after. Until next time, this is me (Shashwat) signing off on behalf of Chandan, Vairavan and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo! Goodbye and take care!

Josh Little, Player of the Match: I just spoke to Hardik before the game and we talked about keeping it as simple as possible - hitting the hard lengths, and happy that I could do it today. The first game of the season was always going to be nerves. I have settled in nicely now. (On his plan on this pitch) It was just about smashing back of a length and letting the ball do the talking.

Hardik Pandya, Gujarat Titans captain: (On Noor and Little) They got us back in the game and they kept us in the hunt. The way Gurbaz batted - he was hitting good balls with some conviction and clarity. The way they (Noor and Little) bowled was great. I would have taken 180 on that wicket any given day. In a group, we know that to win the game, irrespective of the situation, we have to play good cricket. that humbleness is helping us win games of cricket. They are respecting the situation, we want to face it and it is just about playing good cricket and being smart. (On Vijay Shankar) He is a fitter Vijay Shankar, more confident and the amount of hard work he has put in is terrific. His hits changed the game and moving forward, we can expect more of the same. I always felt that good people get to good places and he is certainly one of those.

Nitish Rana, Kolkata Knight Riders captain: (On the score) I think we were 20-25 runs short. If we keep dropping catches against big teams, I do not think the result will be any different. No one apart from Gurbaz and Russell got going. There were not enough partnerships and had we had a partnership of 40-50 runs, the score could have been more. We kept them quiet in the middle overs but against such teams, if you do not take your chances, you will end up on the losing side. If we do well in all three departments, only then will we have a chance. Unless we do that, the result will not be in our favour. I feel the small moments are more important than the big moments. If you do these small things well, like taking catches and fielding well, there are more chances of victory.

7:51pm Well, the Gujarat Titans did it at a canter towards the end. But just before Miller and Shankar joined hands, KKR seemed in the contest, with their spinners keeping things tight in the middle overs. As the game moved into the final phase, though, Miller and Shankar took it up a notch and KKR just could not respond. They also dropped Miller at a crucial juncture and that eventually came back to haunt them.

As for GT, this win catapults them to the top of the table. They have aced another run-chase and the way they have been hunting down totals, they look on course to make the playoffs for the second time running. In an ideal world, they would have wanted one of Gill or Hardik to have batted deeper but they would not mind that, especially with their middle order firing on all cylinders.

postText:
11.10 pm So both sides win the away match in the head to head encounters just a few days apart. Delhi win in Hyderabad, Sunrisers return the favor taking the result in Delhi. The Capitals now sit alone in last place on four points. Sunrisers meanwhile have clawed up to be joint seventh place with KKR and Mumbai on six points. All three of them are four points behind the four-team logjam at the top of the table.

Delhi Capitals captain David Warner: "Losing by nine runs, it actually was a pretty nice wicket. Getting in and out of our overs, we were a fraction off tonight. I think Mitch Marsh bowled fantastic through the middle overs and was our best bowler, but coming up nine runs short is pretty disappointing. They took the pace off quite a lot. At the end of the day when you get two guys off to a good start, it's important that we try to capitalize on that and one of them go on to score a big one. If we were able to do that, it sort of takes it out. But when you lose wickets in the middle and there's no partnerships unfolding, it makes it pretty difficult. [On Axar Patel's batting position] He's in good touch and good form, but for us it's about we got off to a good start and him at the back end... we knew it would be vital with their spinners spinning into left-handers and we only had me and Axar [as lefties]. We had two guys going at that point and holding Axar back at the back end, it can be difficult but they're the challenges that present us when we're actually in the moment and maybe we can think about that, sending him earlier. We just have to build momentum through the middle with the bat. We need one or two players to get 80+ scores and win games for us. We've been losing too many wickets throughout the middle and that's where we're suffering a little bit. Our senior players have to take responsibility. One of us has to get a big total and then it takes care of itself from there."

Sunrisers wk Heinrich Klassen: "It's about time I do something at the IPL so I'm very pleased about it. I think it was a good team effort and we finally freed ourselves up as a batting unit. I'm glad that the batters played with a little bit more freedom in the middle and at the start of the innings and hopefully it's a good sign of things to come. We've got the players to do it up front and need to free them up a little bit and like tonight they showed that they can do it. We've got a great wicket back home and hopefully we can take this form and this result back home. You have to fit in where the team wants you. You can't be one-dimensional so I'm happy to play where the team needs me. The wicket was holding a little more and had turn in it so we encouraged [our spinners] to try to spin the ball as much as they can and slow it up against the big hitters to make it difficult on this wicket. [On Abhishek Sharma's bowling] He's been bowling well in the nets so we just keep encouraging him to try to turn the ball and not do all this fancy stuff out of his hand. Just try to spin the ball as much as he can."

Sunrisers captain Aiden Markram: "It was a great team effort. It's good to see the guys put in great efforts in the buildup to this game and good to see a nice fresh approach from the batters and some good character and good skills at the end by the bowlers too. I don't mind getting things wrong on a cricket field as long as they approach things in the right way to try to be the best versions of ourselves. You have to take your hats off to the players to get them to buy in so quickly. Klaasy has been in great form. Abhishek did the hard work for us up front playing some great shots but we still needed someone to finish it off. I thought the partnership with Klaasen and Samad was really good. Klaasy just plays one way really and it's good to see him do that on this stage. It was basically a case of a couple of good overs and a wicket would get us back in the game. It took something special like the catch from Mayank to get us back in the game. The bowlers showed a lot of character. We've got to take it one game at a time for us but also appreciate we need to get wins under our belt. Hopefully we can play another good game of cricket in our next game."

Mitchell Marsh has been named Player of the Match in a losing effort with his half-century and four wickets: He beats out Abhishek Sharma who also scored a half-century and took a wicket. "It's a disappointing loss for us. Nice to have that partnership with Salty but unfortunately couldn't get us over the line. We knew that the Powerplay was going to be really big and it was important to get off to a good start because the wicket slowed up a bit. I think we gave 20 too many and they were too good. [Duing the partnership with Salt] If the ball was in our area, just keep trying to find the boundary. Unfortunately we lost a couple of wickets and that can happen when you chase totals because you feel like you need to keep going but ultimately we were outplayed. I still think there's a lot of positives coming out of today. We've lost some close ones. There's a reason why the IPL is the best tournament in the world. It's bloody hard to win games. Close games can define your season. Unfortunately we've been on the wrong end of a few. But our spirits are high. There's still a long way to go in this tournament. We need to start winning but I hold a lot of belief in this group."

That's it for today's live coverage. Come back tomorrow for another IPL doubleheader. Until then, take care!

Arshdeep Singh has the new ball. Third and fine leg are back. Arshdeep around the wicket immediately. Here we go.

3.28pm The PBKS fielders come out onto the field. Devon Conway and Ruturaj Gaikwad are the CSK openers.

Punjab Kings Team S Dhawan*, A Taide, LS Livingstone, Sikandar Raza, SM Curran, JM Sharma†, M Shahrukh Khan, Harpreet Brar, K Rabada, RD Chahar, Arshdeep Singh

3pm It looks like a dry pitch, the sun is out, and CSK have decided to bat first. MSD says that heat is a big factor in the afternoon games. Apparently CSK were a little late to the stadium. Dhoni says it's good: it keeps them from overthinking. CSK are unchanged. Shikhar Dhawan says PBKS would have batted first too because of the dry pitch. Harpreet Brar being back is part of the "one-odd" change they have made.

2.50pm Manthan Jain: "Read that Mike Hesson interview on Cricinfo he told that when you replace a captain with a vast legacy and success and if he is still playing you can't appoint an inexperienced captain as he might get under massive pressure that's why they chose faf csk missed a trick here last year by appointing jaddu he might be a decent captain but with MSD still playing and his legacy he was under immense pressure so either they need to chose a very experienced guy or make jaddu captain after MSD retirement."

2.40pm Shivam Dube was supposed to be a one-dimensional hitter when RCB let him go. Now he has emerged as spin monsterer for CSK. Among Indians with at least 500 runs in the tournament, only one has hit more sixes than fours and that's Dube, writes Deivarayan Muthu.

2.30pm Match 41, IPL 2023. It's the two Kings, Chennai Super Kings against Punjab Kings, in the sultry Chennai. A thunderstorm might be around but I doubt if it will disturb the match. Any dip in temperature will no doubt be welcome.

It's almost crunch time. CSK are two points behind the table leaders, and don't want to fall too far behind. PBKS are bang in the middle of the table, and want to rise up. We will know it all in 30 minutes.

You can also track the game with our ball-by-ball commentary in Hindi and in Tamil.

On that note, we take your leave. The other match is already 15 minutes in. Thanks for joining us. Bye

7.45pm The Player of the Match is Devon Conway. He says, and this is not verbatim: We felt it was a little bit slow when you hit the wicket. We thought 200 was a very competitive total so a little bit disappointed that we lost this one. I try not to over-complicate things. I try to keep things as simple as possible. I try and work as closely as I can with Mike Hussey. Along with the other players. We have got a lot of experience in our camp. Just try to work with them. In the middle as well.

7.40pm Shikhar Dhawan says, and this is not verbatim: It feels very very special beating Chennai in Chennai. I am very happy with the way we played. It shows great character of our side to bounce back from that loss, and leaving it behind. All credit goes to the team and the support staff. I was very happy at the way the bowlers bowled. At first when I saw, I thought the wicket was dry but it had good bounce. As a captain, I wanted Liam to play more overs. And Jitesh too. The good sign is that all the boys are performing.

7.35pm So even Dhoni has gone back to that Jadeja innings of 10 balls where he tried to hit only one boundary. Without actually taking names, though. Conway was brilliant, the PBKS spinners were not great, but their fast bowlers closed out well with slower balls. Then in the chase, the batters kept doing enough against pace so as to not have toe be desperate against the slower bowlers. Pathirana was excellent in overs 18 and 20, but not enough to win it for CSK.

7.32pm Sikandar Raza says, and this is not verbatim: Coming from the Zimbabwe culture, we put more emphasis on winning rather than individual performances. I don't know what the discussion was before the last ball. Just am lot of arms waving in the dugout. That over when Livi took charge was the momentum shift. Jitesh has been striking so well all all IPL. The way he batted today was great. I was trying to get bat on ball and run as hard as I can.

7.30pm MS Dhoni says, and this is not verbatim: We lost it in a couple of overs in the middle. You need to be aware what you need to bowl and be clear because the batters will be going for it. Also towards the end of our innings, could we have got 10 more? Because our bowling needs exposure, and we should be doing better with the bat. The pitch had turn, there was some turn when it hit the seam. The slower balls gripped. I think 200 was par but we bowled two bad overs. Pathirana bowled well but other than that, we need to see if the plans were wrong or the execution was bad.

7.25pm What a thriller we have had. CSK will be upset they couldn't defend 200 on a pitch that gripped. PBKS were excellent with the bat. The intent shown by them was great. I still go back to Jadeja's innings, who just kept looking for gaps and not big hits.

postText:
Jaiswal ended on the wrong side but ended as the deserved POTM recipient. Brilliant win for the hosts. SKY, Archer, David coming into form augurs well for them. That's it for now, two high-scoring thrillers ending with the chasing team winning. Thanks for tuning in, hope you enjoyed our coverage. I'm Ekanth on comms, Chandan Duorah and Thilak Rama were our scorers and it's goodbye from all of us.

Yashasvi Jaiswal, POTM: When I completed my century, I didn't know whether the ball went to the boundary. So I thanked God for everything. That was the highlight. Days like this definitely can happen. I want to focus on the process and work hard, and have the belief. I have been positive and am maintaining a good, fit lifestyle which is helping. The straight drive is my straight drive.

Rohit Sharma, MI captain: Was pleasing to see how we chased down the target. Last game too, we came close and we back ourselves to chase them down. So it was pleasing. Polly's shoes are big to fill, but Tim has got a lot of ability and power. At the back end that helps and is good to have. The changes in the side are difficult, but sometimes you have to play the conditions and make calls based on compositions, so the players need to be prepared for that. Jofra's had a massive injury, with bowlers we knew they need match practice. But his pace was a big positive and we thought SKY's innings like that was around the corner. (On Jaiswal) I watched him last year, he's taken it to the next level. I asked him 'where did you get the power from'. He said he's been going to the gym, that's good for him, India and RR.

Hari: "Time to remove the win prediction feature from Cricinfo?" Lol, nah, the fact that it went wrong illustrates how unlikely the result was.

Gorango: "Holder bowled 5 full tosses in a row. Maybe not the right death bowler."

Namit: "First Venky and now Jaiswal! It's official, MI is good in spoiling Centuries!!!"

Rohan: "The forecaster was stating RR was winning it till the 39th over, and yet MI won. This shows that Timmy is way beyond science and mathematics! :D"

Mustafa Moudi : "Fun Fact: A total of 827 Runs scored today in 4 innings with each innings total being higher than previous. What a Sunday !!"

Tim David: Amazing feeling. For our confidence, seeing how the boys went about it was awesome. It felt like every bowler had to be targeted but the conditions were batting-friendly. I wanted to play an innings like this for a while. In the final over, I tried to get in front and close the angle down, play good shots. It was good to bat at the end. Every time someone missed the yorker, you felt like you missed out as a batter.

Sanju Samson, RR captain: At the timeout, we were thinking that with the way SKY was going, we were thinking of fighting it out and we were almost there but Tim David did something special. (On the dew) It was kinda wet, not that wet, we were expecting it but had the experience to deal with it. The way we've been playing, with the last nine games ending with us winning or coming close, illustrates the high standards at which we've been playing. Jaiswal ended up on the wrong side but very happy for him personally.

On a belter with dew assisting the batters, MI lost Rohit early. It looked to me like it hit the off bail but slow-motion replays online suggest that might not have been straightforward. Sorry to the commentors who said so, I didn't see it at the time. Then Kishan couldn't get going but Green kept trying and made 44. It was when SKY took off that MI's chances rose. Ashwin was economical and took key wickets but his spell ended early. His spinning partner, Chahal, wasn't as effective. Boult and Sandeep bowled good death overs, but Holder's off-day cost the visitors big time. He was caught in a Tim David hurricane that swept over Wankhede.

11:50pm: David is Goliath! Jaiswal's 124 ends in vain. MI go up to 7th position and RR fall to 3rd in the points table. Hard to encapsulate the strokeplay, the power and brilliance with the bat. Ashwin's bowling shines out as well. But in the end, it was SKY and David's brilliance had the final say.

Varun: "while Holder did a Ben Stokes , David did a Brathwaite!"

Charlie99: "Someone had to say it - Remember the name!!"

preText:
7:27pm The umpires have made their way out to the middle, followed by the players. du Plessis and Kohli will open the batting for RCB. And straightaway, we will have spin. Krunal to take the new ball.

You can also track the game with our ball-by-ball commentary in Hindi and in Tamil.

7:19pm Hazlewood returning to the side is a massive boost for RCB and adds more firepower to their bowling attack, especially during the powerplay. That phase could be crucial in the second innings, considering Rahul has not quite been at his best this season. RCB, though, need to put up enough runs on the board first.

Lucknow Super Giants XI: KL Rahul (c), Kyle Mayers, Deepak Hooda, Marcus Stoinis, Krunal Pandya, Nicholas Pooran (wk), K Gowtham, Naveen-ul-Haq, Ravi Bishnoi, Amit Mishra, Yash Thakur

Substitutes: Ayush Badoni, Daniel Sams, Quinton de Kock, Prerak Mankad, Avesh Khan

Royal Challengers Bangalore XI: Faf du Plessis (c), Virat Kohli, Anuj Rawat, Glenn Maxwell, Mahipal Lomror, Dinesh Karthik (wk), Suyash Prabhudessai, Wanindu Hasaranga, Karn Sharma, Josh Hazlewood, Mohammed Siraj

Substitutes: Harshal Patel, Sonu Yadav, Vijaykumar Vyshak, Michael Bracewell, Shahbaz Ahmed

7pm It's time for the toss and the first big news from the middle is that Faf du Plessis is back captaining RCB today. He calls heads and it comes down as heads. RCB will bat first. du Plessis says that it might slow down later in the game and that it looks good to bat on right now. Josh Hazlewood comes in for David Willey, and Anuj Rawat replaces Shahbaz Ahmed. Rahul reckons that the pitch will be consistent throughout the game. One change for LSG - Avesh Khan is out, K Gowtham is in.

Hawk: "Would wish for Kedar Jadhav to make his return straightaway. RCB have been overly reliant on their top 3 and DK just hasn't stepped up this season."

As we build up to the toss, do jump into Shashank's preview, where he details what could be on the cards tonight.

Let's see what the conditions have in store for us. The pitch is not at the centre of the square meaning that the dimensions are slightly skewed - 72m to one side and 63m to the other. It is a black soil surface again. Low bounce could be a factor and might impact six-hitting. Rohan Gavaskar, though, reckons this is more than a 145-run track.

The last time these teams met, the game descended into utter pandemonium at the end. Avesh Khan throwing his helmet into the turf might have been the defining image but there was plenty that preceded it, including a failed Harshal Patel attempt at running out the non-striker while backing up, a whirlwind Nicholas Pooran fifty and a trademark display by RCB's famed batting trio.

The pitch may or may not be similar to the one dished out that day, but with the star cast more or less the same, we could have another cracker on our hands tonight.

6:20pm Match 43, and we are back in Lucknow, where LSG have a decent if not intimidating record, having won twice this season in four attempts. That said, they do come into this game having lost two of their most recent fixtures at home and against an RCB side that is showing signs of clicking into gear, KL Rahul's men could have their work cut out.

This game also begins a run of five straight away matches for RCB, which does not culminate until May 18, when they take on SRH in Hyderabad. The Chinnaswamy track has so far put their bowling attack to the sword. So, from that perspective, they might not really mind being on the road.

Both teams also have questions surrounding their batting units, although those quandaries are vastly different in nature. RCB have been too dependent on Faf du Plessis, Glenn Maxwell and Virat Kohli, with their middle order yet to fire.

LSG's runs have been spread out a touch more but the debate around KL Rahul's strike rate refuses to go away. The last time he batted in Lucknow, he was at the crease when the last over began, yet, could not take his side past the finish line. Today, thus, is the perfect opportunity for the LSG skipper to vanquish those ghosts, especially against a side he has historically been successful against.

postText:
9:40pm RCB began their innings well and did not lose any wickets in the powerplay. As the innings progressed, though, they kept losing wickets and momentum. LSG's spinners tied them down and the visitors were just not able to break the shackles often enough. du Plessis tried to anchor the innings but fell just as the death overs dawned. Karthik got a couple of boundaries away but could not stay at the wicket till the end either. This wicket is definitely challenging, although RCB would have ideally wanted a few more runs on the board to defend. LSG, despite having botched a similar run-chase in a day game a few days ago at this venue, would be confident of hunting this down and going level with GT at the top of the points table.

Faf du Plessis: Pretty slow wicket with not a lot of bounce - we were thinking 135 was about a par score. If we get one or two wickets in the powerplay, it could be a tough chase. Playing finger-spin was really tough, that stopped a lot. I felt there was not a lot of bounce for the leg-spinner. Boundary-scoring is hard. We have got some good spinners in our line-up, if we get a few early wickets, it will be tough in the middle.

postText:
12:01am Phew, that brings us to the end of tonight's coverage. It was filled with drama throughout and once the contest ended, tempers threatened to spill over too. But as far as the cricket is concerned, it was a massive win for RCB, and one that has taken them level on points with CSK, RR and of course, LSG. Hope you enjoyed our coverage as much as we enjoyed bringing it to you. Until next time, this is me (Shashwat) signing off on behalf of Raghav, Thilak and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo. Goodbye, goodnight and take care!

Faf du Plessis, the Royal Challengers Bangalore captain is also the Player of the Match: (On the surface) Complete opposites (comparing it to Bengaluru). To have a fifty partnership in the first six overs was a match-winning partnership in the end. (Decision to bat first) Batting first was important. They had four spinners but it looked like right through, playing spin was hard work. It is a little bit easier for a captain, at the Chinnaswamy, it feels like the ball is going everywhere (smiles). I would have liked 135. In my mind, that was a really good score and we were going towards that score. Once again, if you come in on this pitch, it is really tough to score. Said to the boys that if we get two or three early wickets, it would be hard for them. I am super happy for Karn. One of those guys who does the hard work all the time but does not get the recognition. Playing at Chinnaswamy is tough for a leg-spinner. Unbelievable from him tonight. We have missed Hazlewood's experience. Someone like him brings so much calmness and composure. Nice way to ease him into the competition.

Krunal Pandya, Lucknow Super Giants stand-in captain: We did pretty well in the first half restricting them. It was a great team effort. Really happy with how we have bowled this tournament. 126, at the start of the game, we would have taken. But we just could not execute our plans. (On Rahul's injury) It is a sad thing. He pulled his hip flexor, I guess. I do not know how bad it is. The medical team will assess it.

Josh Hazlewood: (On how it felt returning after long) It has been a long while. Excited more than nervous. It is great to be back here, in front of some good fans. The bowlers really turned up and finished off really well at the end. The wicket was quite slow. The spinners played a huge part for both teams. A few more (runs) would have been nice (smiles). It was super loud for both teams. A few of our guys are quite passionate so it gets the crowd up.

11:38pm Wow, that was some game. At the half-way stage, it felt that RCB were just a little short. But as it turned out, they came home with room to spare. Siraj and Hazlewood set the tone in the powerplay, with Maxwell also picking up the crucial wicket of Krunal. LSG then tried to counter-attack but that ploy fell flat on its face, with Pooran and Stoinis getting out while trying to clear the fence. The run-outs did not help either and RCB were professional enough to seal the deal towards the end. This win, by the way, has taken RCB level on points with LSG, who might be left ruing what was a very presentable opportunity.
