postText:
11:30pm Right. That will be that from us for tonight. Prabhsimran set up the game for PBKS with a sizzling hundred before their spinners finally came to the party, picking up six wickets between themselves. This 31-run win means that PBKS now have a better NRR than RCB, and that could still come into play this season. Speaking of RCB, do join us tomorrow as they clash with the Rajasthan Royals in the afternoon game. Until next time, this is me (Shashwat) signing off on behalf of Vairavan and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo. Goodbye, goodnight and take care!

Prabhsimran Singh, Player of the Match: I was not thinking a lot. Just when the wickets fell early, I wanted to bat deeper. (Confidence of domestic form) I have been with the team for a long time and I have learnt a lot from my seniors. I was just trying to grab my opportunity. The wicket was a little difficult because it was turning. I was thinking to build a partnership with Sam and then wanted to target the bowlers. Very important knock for me, I was waiting for this for a long time. Whenever I talk to the seniors, they tell me to make it big. (On his celebration) That is my celebration in domestic cricket also. You could say I was conversing with the almighty and probably also with the team management.

Shikhar Dhawan, Punjab Kings captain: I was thinking where the game was going (after the powerplay). The way we brought the game back was amazing. Credit goes to the spinners and then the fast bowlers for closing it out. It was an amazing knock (by Prabhsimran). I rate this knock quite high, playing that sort of a knock with that high strike-rate and the shots he has played against the turn as well - it was amazing. Because of that innings, we could reach that big total. (On Harpreet Brar) I have confidence in him and I asked him to bowl more at the stumps. The way he stood up and took those wickets, especially getting those left-handers out, it was very big. (On seeing the youngsters perform and if it reminds him of his younger days) I am still young (laughs). I don't feel that I am feeling old, when I am with them, I behave like them only. I like how the boys have taken responsibility. I am very happy with the way they are growing. (On what lies ahead in the IPL) This win gives us a lot of confidence. We know that we have to win both matches. We have to stay calm and focussed because staying calm and being focussed works for us.

David Warner, Delhi Capitals captain: (On how much it turned) It was about restricting them to a decent total. They got a little bit more than what I thought. Prabhsimran batted well. A few dropped chances cost us a few runs. After the way we started and then losing six for 30, you are not going to win many games. You have to play with pride, belief in yourself and play with freedom. Another disappointing effort with the bat after the start we had. (On the number of changes DC have had this season) I think we found the right combination but we keep losing 4-5 wickets in the middle and that is something you cannot do at this level.

Harpreet Brar: (On how he enjoyed the surface) Obviously I enjoyed it. In the first over, I conceded 13 runs and I was a little nervous. But watching the first innings, I knew I could make a comeback. I was thinking about bowling dot balls and putting the new batters under pressure. (On changes he made after the first over) In the first over, because the wicket was slow, it was easy for batters to go on the back foot. Later, I tried to change that and tried to bring them forward. Whenever you play on a slow wicket, the powerplay is very crucial. It went very well for them but we (me and Rahul Chahar) bowled well in a partnership. He kept applying the pressure, and I got wickets because of that.

11:06pm That second innings was very similar to the first, with one team dominating the powerplay, only to be pegged back in the middle overs. PBKS, though, had a much greater impact in that phase than DC did in the first innings. While Salt and Warner were at the crease, this looked a routine run-chase. But once that stand was broken, DC fell like a pack of cards.

Aman and Dubey tried stitching together a partnership but by then, the horse had probably bolted. In the end, it was a comfortable victory for PBKS, who now move to 12 points and are still well and truly alive in this playoff race. As for the Capitals, well, they are officially out of the reckoning now, and this game perhaps summed up their campaign, for they were good in patches but could not seize the moments that really mattered.

preText:
3:27pm Not far away from the start of play now. RR are in a huddle as the RCB openers du Plessis and Kohli stride out to the middle. Sandeep with the new ball for RR. Here we go!

Rahul Vijay: "If Boult is fit, why would have been he left out? Especially when be has a good record against Kohli?" -- Think that might be a tactical call, with this being a day game and the pitch looking quite dry. It might also mean spin plays a more prevalent role during the powerplay, especially against Kohli.

3:10pm It's understood that both Hazlewood and Hasaranga have niggles, hence RCB's changes among their overseas players. Samson confirmed at the toss that everyone was fit to play, so it seems like Boult has just been left out.

Rajasthan Royals XI: Jos Buttler, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sanju Samson (c & wk), Joe Root, Dhruv Jurel, Shimron Hetmyer, R Ashwin, Adam Zampa, Sandeep Sharma, KM Asif, Yuzvendra Chahal

Substitutes: Devdutt Padikkal, Riyan Parag, Kuldip Yadav, Donovan Ferreira, Navdeep Saini

Royal Challengers Bangalore XI: Faf du Plessis (c), Virat Kohli, Anuj Rawat, Glenn Maxwell, Mahipal Lomror, Dinesh Karthik (wk), Michael Bracewell, Wayne Parnell, Karn Sharma, Harshal Patel, Mohammed Siraj

Substitutes: Vijaykumar Vyshak, Finn Allen, Shahbaz Ahmed, Himanshu Sharma, Suyash Prabhudessai

3pm It's time for the toss. du Plessis calls heads, and it comes down as heads. RCB will bat first. He says the heat has played a role in his decision and reckons the pitch is dry. Wayne Parnell comes in for Josh Hazlewood, with Michael Bracewell also replacing Wanindu Hasaranga. Samson says he would have batted first too. He reckons that they have maintained a relatively high standard of cricket throughout. Adam Zampa comes in for Trent Boult for RR.

Four of RCB's five wins this season have come when batting first. Three of those have been in afternoon games. So, they might be tempted to bat first if they win the toss. Of course, that is contingent to them breaking Samson's run of eight tosses won.

Let's see what the conditions have in store for us. The pitch being used today is bang in the centre, meaning that both square boundaries are equidistant. This strip was last used for the RR-CSK game, where RR scored more than 200. With this being a day game, there could be a bit of help on offer for the spinners. Both RCB and RR have won four games each batting first, and Simon Katich reckons both teams might want to bat first again today.

Neal: "Hope Joe Root scores his first IPL runs tonight. He was finally picked for Rajasthan's last two games but never got to bat due to Jaiswal's heroics! "

The last time these sides met, RCB, riding on fifties by Faf du Plessis and Glenn Maxwell (who else), posted 189 - a total that they ultimately defended, winning by seven runs. That was an afternoon game too, although expect Jaipur to be much hotter than Bengaluru was in April.

2:30pm Match 60 and we have a proper four-pointer on our hands. Rajasthan Royals have 12 points in as many games, Royal Challengers Bangalore have 10 in 11 matches. A win for either side, thus, would tilt the scales considerably in their favour. A loss and they might be left praying for other results to go their way.

RR, after they were on the wrong side of a last-ball heist against Sunrisers Hyderabad, got back to winning ways on Thursday, with Yashasvi Jaiswal powering them to a resounding victory against the Kolkata Knight Riders. Sanju Samson also stroked his way into form, and RR would hope that that pair, alongside Jos Buttler, can hit their straps against RCB too.

Speaking of RCB, well, they have now lost twice in succession after that high-voltage win against the Lucknow Super Giants. On both occasions, they put up 180-plus totals on the board, only to find out that they were comfortably short both times.

At the start of their campaign, they quite enjoyed defending totals, especially in day games and away fixtures. Now that their campaign is seemingly at a crossroad, they would want to rekindle some of that magic against RR. Not just because RCB have reached last-chance saloon, but also because a win would take RR's destiny out of their own hands.

postText:
5:07pm Wow, that was quite a finish at the end. Rawat ensuring that RCB got more than 170 with an 11-ball unbeaten 29. Earlier, du Plessis and Maxwell scored fifties, like they did in the reverse fixture and kept RCB going through the middle. Maxwell, in particular, was very impressive with the way he kept transferring the pressure onto the bowlers. RCB now have 171 on the board, which on a surface that has not been very conducive to stroke-play, is a very good score to have.

As for RR, they would not be pleased with how they ended the innings. Prior to that, though, they did well to trigger a mini-collapse just before the onset of the death overs. At that point, it seemed they would restrict RCB to a score under 160. It did not quite transpire that way but with the firepower they have, they will back themselves to get the job done. Do join us in a bit for the run-chase!

Mike Hesson: (On the score) I think it is slightly above-par. Everyone that batted thought something around 160 would be tough to chase. It (Rawat's cameo) will lift us. Good for Anuj as well, shuffled around a bit. We have always known he has the power, so good for him to do a job for us at the end.

postText:
6:47pm Right. That will be that from us for this game. The action in the IPL, though, comes thick and fast. In a little less than an hour, CSK will take on KKR, with KKR in a must-win situation. Until next time, this is me (Shashwat) signing off on behalf of Thilak, Vairavan and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo! Goobye and take care!

Wayne Parnell, Player of the Match: I think credit goes to our batters. That last over really brought momentum to our side. We understood what was needed and to execute the way we did was really pleasing. All of our batters had the same message - take the pace of it and hit the stumps. To win by a big margin is also crucial for us. (On going around the wicket to Samson) It was a similar surface to back in Paarl. I was trying to bowl at the stumps and make the batters go across the line. It is a long tournament, niggles occur, it is about being switched on every single day.

Faf du Plessis, Royal Challengers Bangalore captain: (On the game) It was really good. We needed it, in terms of the NRR. It was a really difficult pitch when we batted first. Even in the powerplay, the ball was keeping low and we felt that 160 would be a good score. Those hits towards the end pushed us to a very good score. We have not quite managed to do it (finish off strongly) well. If you get it, everyone's shoulders are out, you are ready, so it is really important. That (setting the intensity high) is a non-negotiable for us. Everyone celebrating with real passion, that is very nice to see. (On the remaining games) Hopefully we can set it up for that last game against GT at the Chinnaswamy. Today was really good for the team and I am sure everyone will be extremely motivated for the next two matches.

For all of you wondering, RCB, courtesy of this win, now boast a better NRR than RR. This is how the points table looks like, after Match 60.

Sanju Samson, Rajasthan Royals captain: (On the batting performance) We usually go hard in the powerplay but that did not quite happen today. It will take some time to assess our display. That is the nature of T20 cricket, you have to go hard in the powerplay, knowing that the wicket will slow down. Today, it did not work out. Credit has to go out to the RCB bowlers and their teammates. Their energy was great and they really wanted to win this game. (On the score) That could have gone to the wire, it could have been a tight match if we had a decent powerplay. I felt that was a par score on this wicket. (On the second half of the campaign) That is a great question actually. I was thinking about it and where it went wrong. Sorry, I do not have an answer for that. We all know the nature of the IPL. We know things can change in a couple of days. Funny, funny things happen at the end of the league stages. We have to be strong, be professional and think about the game we are playing in Dharamsala. You have to keep your hopes high and try your best. (On trying to bat out the innings) There are a lot of different ways to look at it (in hindsight). The people out there might have thought the game was still in their hands and I think you cannot blame them the way they batted. We have to take responsibility as a team.

Michael Bracewell: It was nice to get those two points. Very valuable in this competition. For me to come back, and contribute to the win was nice. (On the pressure of the big game) We have great support staff here and you feel very included even if you are not in the playing eleven. I was just trying to stay up to speed as much as I could. (On the Rawat cameo) That was a massive innings. It was a difficult innings to get going on, and it gave us all the momentum going into the second innings. The way our bowlers started was spectacular as well. Our top three did all the dirty work to build a foundation for Anuj to capitalize at the end. I try to not get too caught up with the highs and lows of the game and just take it ball-by-ball. Two more must-win games and we are trying to take it game by game. As a group, we thrive under this sort of pressure, of having to win and having the tournament on the line.

6:22pm Phew, it will take everyone, including me, RR and RCB some time to make sense of what has just unfolded. RCB got off to the perfect start, removing Jaiswal in the first over. Buttler and Samson followed soon after and once that happened, RR were always chasing the game. But despite that, the way they fell apart, losing five wickets in the powerplay and eventually crumbling to the third-lowest score ever in the IPL, was alarming. The defeat will hurt but the margin of victory means that their NRR has also taken a massive hit, and with just one game remaining, RR are now dependent on other results going their way.

As for RCB, well, everything that could have gone right for them went right. Siraj was superb in the powerplay, as was Parnell, who came in to replace Hazlewood. Their spinners then cleaned up the lower order and their NRR has now gone into the positive. With two games still to come, RCB have more than a chance of getting to 16 points and making it to the playoffs.

7.30pm Deep third is square. And there is a deep square leg. Here we go

7.28pm The settled opening pair of Devon Conway and Ruturaj Gaikwad walks out for CSK. Vaibhav Arora will take the new ball.

7.25pm Before we start, a word on the conditions. Both sides expect it to be slow underfoot. The pitch is towards one edge of the square. One square boundary is 61m, the other 70m.

7.10pm CSK XI: D Conway, R Gaikwad, A Rahane, M Ali, A Rayudu, S Dube, R Jadeja, MS Dhoni (c & wk), D Chahar, T Deshpande, M Theekshana

KKR XI: J Roy, R Gurbaz (wk), S Narine, N Rana (c), R Singh, A Russell, S Thakur, V Arora, H Rana, S Sharma, V Chakaravarthy

7.05pm CSK substitutes: Pathirana, Nshant Sindhu, Senapati, Rasheed, Akash

KKR substitutes: A Roy, Jagadeesan, Umesh, Iyer, Ferguson

7pm MS Dhoni has won the toss, and CSK will bat first. He says the pitches have changed over the duration of the IPL, and now Chennai is a bat-first surface. He says he is happy with how players have taken responsibility. "Perhaps fielding can improve 5-10%." CSK are unchanged.

Nitish Rana says he would have wanted to bat first himself because the pitch looks a little sticky. Rana reports one change: Vaibhav Arora in for Anukul Roy.

6.50pm Deivarayan Muthu is at Chepauk. He reports: "Shivam Dube, who hurt his finger against MI last weekend, was hitting Albie Morkel-style monster sixes at training the eve of the game and looks set to start again for CSK if they bat first. Meanwhile, Varun Chakravarthy had a little reunion with the CSK players. He had started his IPL career as a net bowler for CSK at Chepauk in 2018 even before he became a TNPL star. This will be his first IPL match against CSK in Chennai. This game is set to be played on pitch No. 3, which was used for CSK vs MI."

6.40pm What do KKR need to go their way for them to qualify? Firstly they need to win their remaining games. In the words of S Rajesh: "Their best case would be for Titans to win their last two, Royal Challengers to beat Royals and then lose their last two, Super Giants and Royals to lose their last two, and Punjab Kings to lose to Delhi Capitals in their return game on Wednesday. Then Titans, Super Kings and Mumbai Indians will qualify, leaving Knight Riders and Punjab Kings to fight for the fourth spot on 14 points. There isn't much to choose between their NRRs at the moment (-0.357 for KKR and -0.268 for Punjab Kings) which means Knight Riders will still have to win handsomely to lift their NRR."

Bharat: "Wow. What an IPL this has been. Still only 10 games left and 9 teams still theoretically in contention and only DC ruled out. Although RR, KKR and SrH now can't cross 14 points and need several other results NRR to go their way to qualify. So effectively 6 teams in the race."

6.30pm Match 61 of IPL 2023. We have had a bit of a blowout in the first match of the day. It is now about Chennai Super Kings hosting Kolkata Knight Riders. It is a must-win match for KKR, who have 10 points from 12 matches, but more importantly it is a big match for CSK to remain reasonably confident of a two-two finish. First things first, though: a win will ensure CSK progress into the playoffs.

And that ends our offerings for you tonight. This result gives Mumbai Indians hope of finishing in the top two if they can win their last two matches. CSK still not through, KKR still not out. The IPL remains wide open. Not much dew so far in Chennai but tonight it made a big difference. That might confuse teams with what to do in the playoffs. A big week coming up. For now, though, good night and good luck.

11.30pm Rinku Singh is the Player of the Match. He says, and this is not verbatim: We lost three wickets early, so we decided we will take this deep. I bat at 5, 6 in domestic cricket too so the experience helped me. I have worked hard, really hard, to get batting well, which is what gives me confidence.

11.27pm Nitish Rana says, and this is not verbatim: Chandu sir [Pandit, KKR coach] asked for a heavy roller, which I didn't want. I felt the heavy roller might break the pitch, but it settled the pitch completely. The ball didn't turn in the second innings. Credit to our spinners for how well they bowled. I always felt that if I or Rinku could hold one end up, we will chase this down. That's what happeened.

11.10pm MS Dhoni says, and this is not verbatim: The minute we bowled the first ball in the second innings, we knew we needed 180. But there was no way we could have got 180 on that pitch. The dew made a big difference in the second innings. We can't really blame any of our bowlers. Just that the conditions had a big impact on the game. Very happy with what Shivam has done, but important that he is not satisfied and keeps improving. Chahar swings the ball, he knows what fields to take, and he bowls accordingly.

11.08pm KKR have strolled this chase despite losing three wickets inn the powerplay. Rana and Rinku never looked under any pressure despite coming together at 3 for not much. Both of them scored sensible fifites to see them through. So CSK are not yet officially through, and KKR are not yet officially out.

I'm not the kind of person who dwells too much about my last innings. The focus is on what's need at the moment. The most satisfying moment was to hit Abhishek for a six because he is my childhood friend.

Hardik Pandya, GT Captain: Very proud of the boys. Two in two. Last year was different, we knew there'd be a lot of challenges this year. Boys have put their hands up in different situations. I think we've rightly earned the chance of making the playoffs. I spoke about where we stand and that there will be high expectations but we focus within the group. We tick a lot of good boxes, we made errors in our journeys but were very consistent. Even when we lose, we were in the game and made some mistakes. People were focusing on the right thing, that's why we're here. For me, bowlers are very close to my heart. I sometimes feel batters take a lot of credit. A couple of overs are always important. I'm a bowler's captain and will ensure they're well prepared and always get credit.

Mohammed Shami: I've been focusing on hitting the ball into the pitch, bowl to my strengths and on good lines. (On powerplay bowling) I've been trying to hit similar lines and make use of the new ball. That's always given me success. The wicket was the same as that in the last game. Mohit coming in has helped go well in the middle overs, given we have Rashid and Noor as well. (On what he's been eating) I'm in Gujarat, so will not get what I want (non-veg food), isn't it? (laughs)

Abhilash: "Every wicket today was a catch out just sparing that Noor's run out"

Third four-plus wickets haul today (Bhuvi Shami Mohit), the most in an IPL match. Only five T20 matches before had three or more 4-plus wicket hauls.

Stats from Sampath: Gujarat's 91 runs in their previous game vs MI were the most runs by a team after the fall of seventh wicket in an IPL game. Sunrisers bettered that scoring 95 runs today.

Mustafa Moudi : "Fun Fact: When these 2 sides faced each other for the first time in 2022, Rashid got dismissed on a Golden Duck with the Bat and conceded 28 Runs with the Ball. Same happeed tonight too !!"

Aiden Markram, SRH captain: Still believed at half-time that we were in with a chance but with four wickets in the powerplay, we went down. We have high-class bowlers and we thought the ball would swing for a while but it didn't. Gill did well. Credit to Bhuvi for bringing it back. Klaasen is a great player with class, power and a good cricketing brain. Unfortunately, the rest of the group did not support him. Lots of pride still left in the upcoming games. Maybe we'll give out a few opportunities and guys can finish well but sadly we haven't been good. Bhuvi showed us the way and Nattu was good as well.

11:23pm: A comfortable win for Titans. An expected cruise, Gill's slowdown while closing in on the hundred does not matter. Shami retained his new-ball magic. Mohit got a four-for. All is good in their camp. Sunrisers did well to go from 59 for 7 to 154 but that, led by Klaasen's solid fifty, is as good as it got for them. The game did drag on for close to four hours again but the game was on for only a few minutes as Sunrisers' batting crumbled.

7.00pm Rohit calls Tails and Tails it is. Mumbai Indians opt to bowl first. "We know what to expect from the pitch," Rohit says. "It looks like a good track but I don't know how it will play. So better to have total in front of it. This pitch will present a different challenge and we are up for it. Even the seamers have been quite effective here. So we have got four seamers and two spinners. You can take a lot of positives from past results but you have to play well on that day. We have made once change: an offie coming in for a left-arm spinner."

"We don't mind batting first," Krunal Pandya says. "We wanted to bat first only. We have a lot of changes. Naveen comes in, Mayers sits out. Hooda is in for Avesh. There's one more change, which I am forgetting. Everyone's fit."

Pitch report: One square boundary is 75 metres, the other just 61. Down the ground it's 78. The longest pocket is the deep extra cover from one end - 81 metres. It's a red-soil pitch, so ideally it should have more bounce and pace but Kevin Pietersen thinks otherwise. "It's going to be low and slow," he says. Deep Dasgupta adds there's hasn't been much dew, but it has been a bit unpredictable.

Vincy: "MI's batting has brought them to where they are in the points table today. For once I wish their bowlers come to the party. They won't find a better venue than Lucknow and a team in LSG who haven't had a great time at home."

6.45pm It will be a big Test for Suryakumar Yadav as well. Most of his runs this IPL have come at the Wankhede (342 at a strike rate of 206.02 as compared to 137 at 161.17 while playing away). Can he be just as destructive in away conditions. Abhimanyu Bose ponders.

6.40pm Mumbai Indians are flying from the high-scoring Wankhede to the dusty turner in Lucknow, Vishal Dikshit notes in his preview. It's a journey from the fastest scoring ground in the tournament to the slowest. So it will be interesting to see how the Mumbai batters counter the LSG spinners.

6.30pm Hello and welcome to match 63 of IPL 2023. It's Lucknow Super Giants taking on Mumbai Indians as the race for the playoffs heats up. Both teams are neck and neck, MI at No. 3 with 14 points and LSG at No. 4 with 13 points. Both have played 12 games each, and whoever wins tonight will take a big step towards the playoffs. 7pm Shikhar Dhawan has won the toss, and PBKS will bowl first. No brainer on a new pitch. Dhawan reports two changes: Atharva Taide in for Rishi Dhawan, and Kagiso Rabada in for Sikandar Raza.

David Warner says DC would have wanted to chase too because of the dew. Anrich Nortje and Prtivhi Shaw are back for DC. Mitch Marsh is out injured. Dubey makes way for Shaw.

6.55pm Bang in the middle of the square: 65m square boundaries, 75m down the ground. Fresh pitch. Really hard with some grass. The quicks are going to be in play, reckons Matthew Hayden. A good batting surface, he and Simon Doull conclude.

6.50pm A lot of the teams can't manage to get players that represent the city/state culturally. PBKS have taken the scenic route to get a Punjabi player: from Pakistan via Zimbabwe. Here he is conversation with Mohammad Isam.

I come from a Punjabi background and I can speak Urdu. A lot of the conversations in Zimbabwe are in English and Shona, which is the local language. I don't think I have spoken so much Punjabi in my life as I have done in the last six weeks. At least my Punjabi got polished a little bit.


Aditya: "If PBKS lose today, and RCB lose tomorrow, CSK and LSG qualify with 4 teams fighting for the fourth position right?"

Sanket : "PBKS should play Rabada here if he is fit in place of Nathan Ellis or even they can afford to drop Sam curran who has been average this season. Historically Dharmshala has very good bounce and carry so Rabada can be really handy on this kind of surface. "

Sanket : "Good thing for Punjab will be that as DC is no longer in the contention for the playoffs they might play a weaker and inexperienced side like experimenting with few Indian uncapped players."

6.40pm What a time then for the IPL to make it to a new venue for the first time this year. Dharamsala is no stranger to people of both the participating states who anyway tend to drive up during the summers. One of the most picturesque venues in the world, Dharamsala had to pull out of the Border Gavaskar Trophy because its outfield was not ready after it had been relaid. This will be the first test of the new outfield.

If you are seeing this on a mobile device and didn't know it already, ESPNcricinfo is better experienced on our apps. And we have recently rolled out an update for Android, which you can download or update here.

6.30pm Match 64, IPL 2023. We are nearing the end of the league stages, and we don't yet know more than one playoff team. Tonight we have one of the contenders, Punjab Kings, going up against the already eliminated Delhi Capitals. The equation for PBKS is simple. In the words of S Rajesh, here it goes:

Played 12, Points 12, NRR -0.268
Remaining: DC (h), RR (h)
Given their poor NRR, it is highly unlikely that Kings will take the fourth spot with 14 points. They will need to win their last two and finish on 16, and then probably hope that other results help them out, as RCB are on as many points with a significantly better run rate.
To start with, they need a big win against bottom-placed Delhi Capitals on Wednesday. That is a home game for Kings, but in Dharamsala, not Mohali.

postText:
That brings an end to tonight's presentation. That was interesting from David Warner and Rilee Rossouw on the pitches at Kotla. Pretty scathing that they could never trust the home pitches, and lost all home advantage. On a true pitch, the best of their batting came through, and the value of their bowlers shone through. Kuldeep and Nortje were sensational. On a slow pitch, you negate the quality of Kuldeep because many other spinners can do well there. All this analysis will go into the final analysis. PBKS are also almost out bar a mathematical miracle. We take your leave now. The action never stops. See you tomorrow.

11.40pm Rilee Rossouw is the Player of the match. He says, and this is not verbatim: It was long overdue. I am chuffed it did come, and with the win. It is a good wicket, which suits our game. It is just natural the batting on this wicket. Credit to Livi, he played an unbelievable knock.

11.38pm David Warner says: It was a bad performance in the field but we will take the win. We lost the toss but batter with fluidity. The wicket helped after the inconsistent pitches at home. You want consistency from your home venue. We haven't been able to work out what am good total there is.

11.25pm Dhawan spot on with the analysis of his bowlers. They didn't pitch it up when it was seaming around. Khaleel and Ishant did. That was the big difference between the two sides. And then Nortje sealing it with the 16th and the 19th. Just heavy lengths with that extra bounce in the pitch.

11.20pm Shikhar Dhawan says, and this is not vebratim: It was frustrating, but I don't think we bowled well in the first six overs. We should have taken some wickets the way the ball was moving around. You always hope. After that no-ball, we hoped because Livi was playing a great knock. Even my decision to bowl a spinner last over backfired. And before that the fast bowlers didn't pitch the ball up in the powerplay. That was the plan but we didn't execute. It is hurting us. Every powerplay we are giving 50-60 runs and not taking wickets. We knew the first two-three overs it would swing, and we knew we could take our time. The first over also went maiden, which doesn't often happen, but it did happen.

11.16pm A consolation win for DC as the other batters leave Liam Livingstone stranded. He had absolutely no support in conditions that this chase was very possible. PBKS now need some kind of wild miracle to make it through. A weird tactical change today: Taide in for Raza ro accommodate Rabada

postText:
RCB continue to keep their playoff hopes alive and well. S Rajesh's scenarios piece will be up soon. Check it out to know how this result has impacted the standings of all the teams in contention. Sidharth Monga's match report is up as well. Thanks for tagging along. Goodbye from me Ekanth and our scorers, Chandan Duorah and K Vairavan.

Virat Kohli, POTM: Quite special considering the magnitude of the game. We saw the ball was gripping in the middle. We wanted a solid start but did not expect to be 172 for no loss. That's how well Faf and I have played, he's been on a different level. I had a quiet couple of games and wasn't hitting as well in the game as I was in the nets. My intent from ball 1 was to go after the bowlers. There was a dip but I wanted to take it up in the right time. Happy that it all came together nicely. I never look at my numbers. I don't give myself enough credit sometimes for playing impact knocks. I take pride to play the situation. I don't play fancy shots. We have to play 12 months of the year, so you can't play fancy shots and throw your wicket away. I try to stay true to my technique and take pride which helps my team. (On why Faf and him work) I think it's the tattoos. Very similar to how AB and me batting together. There's a good sense of where we are and how to take the game forward. It's been a beautiful transition. Blessed and grateful for the support. I told Faf that it was like a home game, cheering for RCB and taking my name as well. I feel you can't create this. I'm myself on the field and think it resonates with the people. Great to see people happy when I perform.

Faf du Plessis, RCB Captain: Amazing chase. We felt it was a good wicket walking off and that 200 was the par score despite Klaasen's ton. Not too many balls that spun or stuck on the wicket so we wanted to play positively. We were clinical with the bat today and ball last game. Kohli and I complement each other well, hit different areas and are good mates on and off well which works for us. Taking the momentum home is key. Away conditions are tough. Chinnaswamy will be amazing for another must-win game for us.

Mohit: "RCB vs GT will be a lot harder... MI will go hard against SRH to get their NRR up! exciting weekend"

Nick: "What an IPL it has been..! No dead rubber till last match. All remaining matches are important ...!"

Thomas: "Really feel for Klassen - what could have been the day when the world took notice of him, he gets outshone by the Kohli-Faf show"

SRH players and staff take a lap across the ground with a banner reading 'THANK YOU HYDERABAD' and the crowd is cheering along.

Aiden Markram, SRH Captain: I thought we batted pretty well but did not maximise. Maybe we left a few runs out there, in the powerplay. Can't be on the winning side for Heinrich, who batted brilliantly today. The support was awesome not just for us but for RCB as well. Pity we couldn't give them a win. But thanks to them. (Mindset coming into the last game) We are still sportsmen and hate losing, wanted to go away with a smile but they were much better. Faf and Kohli killed the game. We still hung in there and weren't too far off at the end. (On his bowling options) We had a look at few guys which is good for the future. Probably one less option in the powerplay but the guys tried their best but execution let them down here and there with Faf and Kohli in full flow. Someone like Nitish was very impressive even if the figures don't reflect it. Klaasen hasn't had the easiest path, he wouldn't have dreamt of it. Great knock for him personally even though it didn't end with a win.

11:01pm: Kohli century leads a clinical performance as RCB retain control over their fate for now. He took charge with scintillating strokeplay, it looked like approaching a slowdown but hit his way past it. Some of the cover drives and the whips were sensational. There were a quiet couple of overs but generally included a boundary each over. Faf was the aggressor in the powerplay and survived being dismissed by an athletic catch by Dagar because the second bouncer for the over was deemed to be a no-ball. Kohli wasn't shying away from playing attacking shots at all stages. Sunrisers' bowling couldn't apply consistent pressure, they weren't allowed to, and end their season at home.

7.25pm We are nearly ready for the start. Out come the umpires, closely followed by the openers, Prabhsimran Singh and Shikhar Dhawan. Trent Boult, the main man for powerplay wickets, has the ball. Play!

7.15pm Fifteen minutes until the start. And with the chance to go first, Punjab are obliged to go hard. They have to win big to get the NRR boost they need to stay in contention, even in the event of RCB and MI losing. As for RR, they just need to get over the line, and get themselves in the mix.

7pm It's toss time... Rajasthan win the toss and bowl first. Part one of their survival bid falls into place then. R Ashwin is out of the reckoning with a back spasm, Punjab are unchanged.

Punjab Kings Shikhar Dhawan (capt), Prabhsimran Singh, Atharva Taide, Liam Livingstone, Jitesh Sharma (wk), Sam Curran, M Shahrukh Khan, Harpreet Brar, Rahul Chahar, Kagiso Rabada, Arshdeep Singh

6.26pm Look, over there, it's the last-chance saloon! Who fancies a lock-in? That's where Rajasthan Royals and Punjab Kings are headed in a contest that doesn't even qualify as winner-takes-all. The winner gets the chance to stare into their drink as they lean on the bar and await the results of the final group-stage games, specifically those involving Royal Challengers Bangalore and Mumbai Indians on Sunday. Defeats for those, and yes, there will be a chance of qualification for the play-offs, though NRR will doubtless come into the picture... but it could be an anxious few days either way. Perhaps the sweet release of elimination will be preferable!

Anyway, here we are, up at the top of the world in Dharamsala, where two flawed teams prepare to get it right one last time. It feels a long time ago that Rajasthan were blazing a trail at the top of the table. They lost their way in mid-tournament and haven't quite found their way again, despite Jos Buttler and Yashasvi Jaiswal taking turns to go into boss-mode at the top of the order. preText:
3:28pm The umpires make their way out to the middle, followed by the DC players. Conway and Gaikwad will open the batting for CSK. Gaikwad will take strike to Khaleel first up. Here we go!

Kannan: "I don't understand why Stokes is made to sit out continuously even after back to fitness" -- It is majorly because CSK are very happy with what their four current overseas players are providing. On dry tracks, Moeen's off-spin is very valuable and Theekshana's mystery spin allows him to bowl in different phases. Conway and Pathirana are pretty much un-droppable.

Afeef: "999 sixes for this season so far. Liam Livingstone hit the 1000th six last season. Let's see if it's Conway or Ruturaj for this season." -- I am going to stick my neck out and bet on Dube getting that 1000th six this season, especially considering the form he has been in.

Delhi Capitals XI: David Warner (c), Yash Dhull, Phil Salt (wk), Rilee Rossouw, Aman Khan, Axar Patel, Lalit Yadav, Kuldeep Yadav, Chetan Sakariya, Khaleel Ahmed, Anrich Nortje

Substitutes: Mukesh Kumar, Prithvi Shaw, Praveen Dubey, Ripal Patel, Abishek Porel

Chennai Super Kings XI: Ruturaj Gaikwad, Devon Conway, Ajinkya Rahane, Shivam Dube, Moeen Ali, Ambati Rayudu, Ravindra Jadeja, MS Dhoni (c & wk), Deepak Chahar, Tushar Deshpande, Maheesh Theekshana

Substitutes: Matheesha Pathirana, Mitchell Santner, Subranshu Senapati, Shaik Rasheed, Akash Singh

3pm It's time for the toss. The coin goes up, Dhoni calls heads and it comes down as heads. A massive roar goes up and CSK will bat first. Dhoni says they are going in with the same eleven that played against KKR. He reckons the pitch may slow down as the game progresses, and that that influenced his decision to bat first. Warner says it is about consistency and that today is about spoiling the CSK party. Lalit Yadav comes back in for DC, and there is one other change that we will confirm for you in a bit.

Jaison: "The season has come down perfectly for MI, RCB, LSG and CSK. Their chances of playoff are placed in their own hands (their own win)." -- The more interesting bit is that if all of them win this weekend, one will still miss out on a playoff berth.

2:48pm Let's see what the conditions have in store for us. The pitch is stationed bang in the middle of the square, meaning that both square boundaries are 62m each. The straight boundary is 74m. The surface looks extremely dry and Aaron Finch reckons it will get slower as the game progresses. Interestingly, the ground staff watered the track a few hours ago and then covered it with a cloth, possibly indicating they are worried about how dry this pitch is and the fact that it could crumble, with this being an afternoon fixture. Win the toss and bat first, says Finch.

The last time these sides met, CSK put up 167 on a relatively sluggish surface. They then strangled DC and ended up winning comfortably. Delhi has not been very conducive to stroke-play throughout the season and with this being an afternoon game, the conditions could be quite similar.

This is how the points table looks like, at the moment. CSK are still second, while DC would be hoping to avoid the wooden spoon by winning today.

2:30pm Match 67. We are in Delhi and the Chennai Super Kings' season has come down to this. They currently occupy the second rung on the IPL ladder, although their playoff hopes are still up in the air.

A win today will blow away that uncertainty, and might even take them a step closer to a top-two finish. A defeat and they will have to indulge in a game of permutation and combination, hoping that one of Lucknow Super Giants, Mumbai Indians or Royal Challengers Bangalore also lose their last outing.

CSK have stuttered and stumbled just a little recently. Their successive home wins against the Delhi Capitals and MI were sandwiched by a home defeat to the Punjab Kings, a washout in Lucknow and another home loss to the Kolkata Knight Riders.

They have enough experience to not brood over it too much. But considering what is at stake today, absolutely nothing can be taken for granted.

The Capitals, meanwhile, come into this game high on confidence having dashed PBKS' playoff hopes. Their top four stood up in that contest and powered them to their first 200-plus total this season. The bowling attack has also shown signs of some consistency and while this might sound absurd for a team marooned in the bottom trenches, they are threatening to play their best cricket towards the end of the season.

They have not really enjoyed home advantage this campaign, with skipper David Warner, in particular, being quite critical of the surfaces served up. That said, they would hope to end their season on a positive note, especially in front of their fans.

7.30pm Karan Sharma and Quinton de Kock to open the innings. Harshit Rana has got the ball. Venkatesh Iyer at first slip.

Jonty Rhodes rings the bell and the players walk out on to the field.

Karan: "Suyash won't be bowling today as he is in substitutes already. Kkr basically relying on an extra batsman to get the NRR target in time!"

7.25pm By the way, the two square boundaries are 58 and 71 metres. Down the ground it's 73 metres.

7.20pm For those of you wondering what LSG are channeling by wearing their Mohun Bagan-inspired jerseys, it is simple - success. The Kolkata football club are masters at winning trophies, and this is what they did in the most recent ISL season. Will LSG replicate it? Well, the jersey is definitely a good omen.

Bala: "@Nikhil: "With nothing to lose, Rinku to open with Russel in batting today."" --- Roy and Gurbaz isn't a bad pair, right?

Argon: "What's the reverse calculation...say LSG score 180, KKR chases it down in 10 overs?" --- Then they need to chase it down In 7.5 overs to finish above RCB's current NRR. But they need RCB to lose as well, so in that case RCB's NRR will come down a bit.

Mustafa Moudi : "NRR is so important for this match that Hemant published the comments from NRR too - Nikhil, Roshan and Roy :P"

ROY: "LSG should play fearless cricket today without thinking much of NRR. "WIN IS MORE IMPORTANT TO QUALIFY"." --- Agree. To go past CSK's NRR, they need to win by 97 runs, if KKR score in the range of 160 to 180.

Roshan: "why bowl first??? for a big NRR boost, shouldn't KKR bat first and try to put a huge score on the board???!!" --- Yeah, a strange decision.

Nikhil: "With nothing to lose, Russel should open the batting today."

Lucknow Super Giants: 1 Quinton de Kock (wk), 2 Prerak Mankad, 3 Krunal Pandya (capt), 4 Marcus Stoinis, 5 Nicholas Pooran, 6 Ayush Badoni, 7 Karan Sharma, 8 K Gowtham, 9 Naveen-ul-Haq, 10 Ravi Bishnoi, 11 Mohsin Khan
Substitues: Yash Thakur, Daniel Sams, Yudhvir Singh, Deepak Hooda, Kyle Mayers

Kolkata Knight Riders: 1 Jason Roy, 2 Rahmanullah Gurbaz (wk), 3 Venkatesh Iyer, 4 Nitish Rana (capt), 5 Andre Russell, 6 Rinku Singh, 7 Shardul Thakur, 8 Sunil Narine, 9 Harshit Rana, 10 Vaibhav Arora, 11 Varun Chakravarthy
Substitues: Suyash Sharma, Mandeep Singh, Anukul Roy, N Jagadeesan, David Wiese

7.00pm KKR have won the toss and opted to bowl first. "We need to win by a big margin, so we are looking to play positive cricket," says Nitish Rana. "There are lot of positives but there are lot of things to learn as well. We have the same team."

"If we would have won the toss, we too would have fielded first," says Krunal Pandya. "We know where we stand on the points table, and our destiny is in our hand. What matters is what total we put up on the board and how if defend it. Instead of Hooda, we have Karan. And K Gowtham comes in for Swapnil Singh."

"It has been a good season for me but as a team, we have gone through some ups and downs," says Varun Chakravarthy. "But I feel overall we played a very good brand of cricket. And irrespective of today's outcome, we will hold our heads high. The games against Gujarat and Delhi, those two games were very close and if we had done a few things better, we would have been sitting on 16 points. We are on our way to building an amazing core. All the Indian boys have done well this season and it's a good sign."

6.45pm LSG are the away team but they will be playing today in a maroon jersey, inspired by the Kolkata-based football club Mohun Bagan. Mohun Bagan FC is also owned by Sanjiv Goenka's RPSG group, and now has been rechristened as Mohun Bagan Super Giant.

6.30pm Hello and welcome to game 68 of IPL 2023. It's Kolkata Knight Riders vs Lucknow Super Giants at Eden Gardens. Placed third, LSG need a win to qualify for the playoffs. They will also be keeping an eye on the game between Delhi Capitals and Chennai Super Kings, since they can secure a top-two finish if they beat KKR by a big enough margin to overtake CSK's net run rate.

For KKR, the chances of qualifying to the playoffs are very slim. They need to win by 102 runs (if they score 180) to get ahead of Rajasthan Royals on NRR.

postText:
LSG were 73 for 5 in the 11th over, after which Pooran bashed 58 off 30 balls. KKR needed 41 to win from 12 balls, and Rinku smashed 39. Two classic comebacks, but only one winner. That's it from the last game at Eden Gardens this IPL, as LSG plan for playoffs while KKR ponder for next season. Here's Hemant's report for a quick recall of the day's play, as this is Himanshu signing off on behalf of Vairavan and Hemant!

Nicholas Pooran is the Player of the Match: "I had to take it as deep as possible. I was looking to capitalise. This was a small pitch. I pride myself to play in these situations [after he came out at 73 for 5]. Ayush [Badoni] and I had had a partnership against Chennai as well. Our bowlers have done it in the last two games. We have a young bowling attack."

Krunal Pandya speaks as LSG qualify: "Very happy... we never gave up. At one stage they were 61 for 1, and we felt just two or three tight overs can change the state of the game. There was grip for the spinners. Rinku has been special every game. You can't take him easy. But it's a high-pressure situation when bowling those death overs. I went with my gut [feel] and gave Yash instead of Mohsin the last over. It just paid off."

Time for the presentations

Suhas: "How important was that dot ball at 18.6?"

Ravi Bishnoi after the win: "Always feels good to win. Feels good to qualify too. It was scary in every ball [with Rinku batting that way]. We thought we had enough on the board. The plan was to bowl wicket to wicket."

Rummy: "What a show Rinku! Take a bow!"

Nitish Rana after the defeat: "The result wasn't in our favour, but there are a lot of positives from the season. Hopefully we come back as a better team. You have to win back to back, and I feel bad since we had the ability finish games off. Looks like I have spoken Rinku all 14 times that I have held the mic after a match! I really don't have words to define him. If he can bat that way in that situation, then he can do anything!"

Afeef: "Get Rinku Singh into India's T20I squad immediately"

11.29pm All said and done, LSG are assured of a place in the playoffs. They will finish third no matter what. It came down all the way to the last ball of their last league game to decide that. Too much left for Rinku to do at the end. Painful for KKR, who were carried all along by Rinku. But it's LSG day in the end, as they now shift their focus on what is to come. Hang around for the presentations.

postText:
Over in Bengaluru, Titans have won the toss and will bowl. MI have done their bit to stay alive for now and potentially earn the final playoffs spot. Rajasthan Royals are out. Thanks for tuning in here, take care.

Cameron Green, POTM: Great stand with Rohit, he's experienced. Having his leadership at the other end helped. The setup has been great, I've been well looked after. No pressure despite the price tag. The intent at the top is important, with Ishan and Rohit above and SKY below me. Pollard has helped with range hitting too. When we had 20 to get, I told SKY to finish it. But with two runs to go, we just trickled over the line.

Rohit Sharma, MI Captain: We came with the mindset to win and not worry what happens elsewhere. Just hoping for the best. I haven't spoken to anyone. Even if we don't go through, we got ourselves to blame. If we do, boys get credit. Last year, we did a great favour to RCB. We hope the result there goes our way. We didn't start well but fixed things along the way. If I have to look back, we lost crucial moments and games like against Punjab here and last game vs LSG. We can't look too much into that. Sometimes it doesn't come along which is fair.

Afeef: "Madhwal's spell at the death was very crucial"

MI team doing a lap of honour at the Wankhede.

Suryakumar Yadav: That one at the end was the hardest single I ever took and watched the ball closely. But Green batted brilliantly and deserved the hundred. We didn't have NRR worries and thought it'd be a special ton which it was. We saw what happens when we chased 200 for the first time.We just wanted to restrict themselves and do well in familiar conditions, where the wicket plays completely differently. We were always positive and wanted to have fun. (On his lack of form coming in) I wasn't worried. I was thinking 'what has happened' but I knew what has worked for me focused on things in my control and see how it turned out. (On if intentionally opened the face on 16.3) Yes, I did. I've played that shot in my mind 100-150 times. Now I know I can execute it and I'm glad. Very happy with the way season has gone. Would have been happier if we had qualified already.

Aiden Markram: Not the campaign we hoped for. Decent start with the bat but sadly we couldn't get over 200. Guys tried well but fell short at the end. Lot of learnings along the way, we have a great group of guys. The pressures are high and things get under the microscope but I've learned a lot. Vivrant was great, he and guys like Klaasy and Bhuvi were consistent.

7:22pm: Rajasthan Royals are out and Mumbai Indians help themselves to a victory with backs to the wall. MI now need RCB to lose to GT or for the game to be washed out. RCB need a win but the toss has been delayed in Bengaluru due to rain. In Mumbai, the hosts made light work of a 200 chase. Rohit found some form, Green steered it through and SKY flew at the end as usual. SRH had very little to write home about. The bowlers didn't hit their straps and the fielders dropped catches. It was a sad end to the innings.

preText:
8.24pm Here come the umpires, this is actually happening. What japes. Kohli and Faf du Plessis are out in the middle now, along with the GT fielders. Mohammad Shami has the new ball. Let's play!

8.07pm Right, drama junkies. What have we got in store tonight? Some cricket, I hope... on that, Srinidhi tells us the covers are off, and Kohli is on the boundary's edge, all padded up and gagging for some action. The forecast suggests that the worst of the weather has passed, so here's hoping...

The new start time is 8.25pm. So, about 10 minutes from now. Still 20 overs a side, hurrah!

Bhargav : "Mr. Miller! Do tell me whom do you want to qualify, MI or RCB?" I want cricket to be the winner.

Just to be clear, a washout would have sufficed for RCB, had it not been for Mumbai's thumping win over Sunrisers just now. Now, nothing less than a win will do. But any old win will be enough, seeing as their NRR is superior to Mumbai's. Rajasthan needed both to lose, and so they are already out.

7.57pm And, and... it's drizzling again just three minutes before the first ball. They have covered the pitch now. It is all a circus. The groundsmen are all waiting with the covers outside the boundary, as the drizzle hints to pick up. With that update, here comes Andrew Miller for the first time today. Pray that he brings some cricketing action.

Royal Challengers Bangalore: 1 Virat Kohli, 2 Faf du Plessis (capt), 3 Glenn Maxwell, 4 Mahipal Lomror, 5 Michael Bracewell, 6 Anuj Rawat, 7 Dinesh Karthik (wk), 8 Harshal Patel, 9 Wayne Parnell, 10 Vijaykumar Vyshak, 11 Mohammed Siraj. The subs are: Himanshu Sharma, S Prabhudesai, Finn Allen, Sonu Yadav and Akash Deep

Gujarat Titans: 1 Shubman Gill, 2 Wriddhiman Saha (wk), 3 Hardik Pandya (capt), 4 David Miller, 5 Dasun Shanaka, 6 Rahul Tewatia, 7 Rashid Khan, 8 Mohit Sharma, 9 Noor Ahmad, 10 Mohammed Shami, 11 Yash Dayal. The subs are: Vijay shankar, KS Bharat, Shivam Mavi, Sai Kishore and Abhinav Manohar

7.49pm All right, we are set for the toss, only for it to be delayed by four minutes. GT bowl first on winning the toss. Pandya says that with the weather around, he wanted to see how much they can chase. He says GT are unchanged, so no one resting ahead of the playoffs. Du Plessis would have bowled first too. He says Himanshu Sharma is in for Karn Sharma.

7.34pm Here comes the great news: the toss is at 7.45pm, and match starts at 8pm. No overs lost. So we are all set for some tasty action (so far).

Navneet: "Just hoping rain makes a grand comeback and MI goes through" --- So we've got an MI supporter around here

7.24pm And now the covers are coming off. A loud cheer rings across the ground. Meanwhile, Green's 100* has taken Mumbai to a win against SRH. They hunt down 201 with 12 balls remaining. So with 16 points, they are currently fourth. RCB are fifth for now, which means they have to beat GT to qualify for playoffs. And needless to say, Rajasthan Royals are eliminated.

Thomas: "All summer, we've been praying for rain to beat the sweltering heat in Bangalore, and it arrives full force on the one day we wanted it to stay away. Life is cruel :(" --- Do what you can do, and if you pray...

7.07pm The covers are back on. It's drizzling, even as RCB fans are watching the MI vs SRH match on the big screen there.

6.55pm In some good news, the drizzle has stopped. The groundsmen have come out to take the covers off. There's no rain there at the moment, and the cut-off for a five-over game is 10.56pm local time. So we still have almost four hours remaining for any action to be possible.

Sanjay: "I stay very close to the stadium. Less than 500 mts. No rain. Very dense clouds around though" --- There you go, we were missing a weatherman from outside the ground all along

6.50pm So the news is that the toss has been officially delayed. A "very slight drizzle" is on, Srinidhi informs.

Anil Kumble is chatting to the broadcasters from Chinnaswamy, but he's firmly protected from the rain by a big, white umbrella. So we can only wait and watch for now.

6.30pm Here's an update from Srinidhi, our eyes and ears at Chinnaswamy: It was pouring between 3pm and 4pm. The intensity of the rain has now reduced, but it's still drizzling steadily. Interestingly, there are no puddles of water as one would expect from hours of rain. The Super Sopper is seen waiting near the sightscreen at one end for the rain to stop and get the ground ready.

Mustafa Moudi: "@Skand, If you are a Maths student, then congratulations. You have already done your practice with continuous calculations of NRR since last 3 days!!" --- That's exactly what we encourage

Ranjit B: "@Skand If you're a climatology student and having an exam tomorrow, double benefits" --- That would be a dream which might not be true though

Skand: "Have an exam tomorrow. Still more concerned about Chinnaswamy weather" --- That's the spirit. And talking of an exam, I was concerned about this Chinnaswamy game back in the time no matter I had to study

6pm In what could be good or bad news depending on which side you are on, it's still drizzling in Bangalore. So in the worst of cases if RCB's game against GT does get washed out, one point for the hosts will mean they finish on 15. But, but... if MI happen to beat SRH at home, then two points for them means they will end on 16. And so that will be that for RCB. Welcome to the all-complicated Match No. 70, the final league game of IPL 2023.

10.10pm What a fascinatingly poised contest. Virat Kohli's second hundred in as many innings has lifted his team to a fighting chance. Here he is:

"We'd have taken that with both hands once we were five-down and Anuj the last recognised batsman. A very competitive score and a winnable score. It's about the bowlers to execute their plans and have a crack at them. A lot of people feel my T20 cricket is declining, but I don't feel like that at all. I feel I am playing my best again, enjoying myself, hitting gaps and big ones at the end. You have to rise to the occasion when the situation demands, and I take a lot of pride in doing, and I've been doing it a while now. I feel really good in my game right now. There's enough in this pitch for our bowlers to make a dent. If we can cut down the boundaries and the twos, it's a difficult chase. Ravi's chat in the changing room was to stay in the present [when there's rain around]. I wasn't focussed on the drizzle or the other game. Just focussed on what I needed to do for my team. We're in a great position to defend this."

Well, that says it all really. Here's Himanshu to see who will claim that final play-off spot.

So this is how it's lined up: CSK vs GT in Qualifier 1, and LSG vs MI in the Eliminator. Both matches will be held in Chennai, as IPL 2023's last leg of the journey begins. Gill and co knocked RCB out this evening, and gave MI a lifeline. Here's Monga's report from the day, as we bid you goodbye after what were 70 league games. That's it from Chandan, Miller, and me, Himanshu tonight! Take care.

Shubman Gill is the Player of the Match: "It's all about getting a start and converting it into a big one. Thankfully it's working out for me in the business end. You have to keep applying yourself, that's important. The new ball was holding on a bit. The ball was getting wet with the dew. I thought Vijay Shankar was trying to go too hard. Once he found the momentum, he hit it a long way. I know my game... for any player it's important to know who you are. I think we have a great bowling attack for that [Chennai] wicket."

Hardik Pandya, the winning captain: "We wanted the momentum going, and wanted to finish on a high. As a bowler, Gill doesn't give you a chance. Other batters also get confidence from it. We would have taken 197 at the start. We should have bowled good balls. Special innings from Virat as well. I can't ask for anything better. Last year, everything went our way. This year, we were expecting people to challenge us. A lot of credit goes to all the boys."

Arunabh: "Traffic jam for days, water logging for hours, no trophy for years.. really feel for Bengaluru at times" --- The Cursed One!?

Chasing 200 here, we paced it pretty well. We've been playing good cricket, and we have bowlers among the top wicket-takers. It's just about taking game by game. To face CSK in Chennai will be really special."

Rummy: "The lack of sixes in RCB's innings was definitely a factor in loss. This ground is known for small boundaries and a lot of sixes. RCB hit only 3 in their entire innings"

Faf du Plessis on RCB's loss: "Obviously very disappointing. We got a really strong team tonight; excellent innings by Shuman Gill. There was a lot of grip in the second innings. I thought 195-200 was a good score. We needed that wicket of Shubman. From our batting perspective, our top four contributed really well... We missed a few runs consistently throughout the season, especially in the back-end of the innings. Perhaps in the middle [overs], we didn't get as many wickets as we would have liked. We need a good middle order, and make sure we finish games off. Last season it was DK, but this season it wasn't to be."

6pm: Hello, folks, it's IPL playoffs o'clock: that time of the year where the meaning of life takes a week off to discover its true potential, which is by following the cricket to figure out who will lift the coveted trophy. Generally, the wait might require bated breath or anxious anticipation but this time, all that can take a backseat. Because there's no surprise that Gujarat Titans and hosts, Chennai Super Kings, the two of the best teams that have played premium deluxe pro max cricket so far have qualified as table toppers and will get two chances of making the final. 9:19pm: After a great start, CSK's batters string a few cameos to get up to 172. Looks like there's dew at the ground but the ball wasn't coming on evenly, so it'll be a tricky chase. Nalkande's no-ball gave Gaikwad an early life and the batter capitalised with big shots. Conway tried to play second fiddle, which he did, but failed to change gears as the innings progressed. Pandya stuck to five bowlers, gave the spinners powerplay overs. But it was in the middle overs where they gained some control. 7.00pm Mumbai have won the toss and they will bat first. "Typical Chennai wicket," says Rohit. "I am not sure how much wear and tear will happen. Back in Mumbai we prefer to chase, but here with a longer boundary, we want to bat first. The boys are quite upbeat about it. At the end of the day, we are here. It was a long journey with ups and downs, and because of that we learnt a lot about our team as well. Kumar Kartikeya is out. Hrithik Shokeen comes in."

"We have got really good match-winners," says Krunal Pandya. "Where we are, it's been an entire team effort, it's not one or two individuals. We would have batted as well but at the end of the day, you have to play good cricket. That's what matters."

Krunal Pandya and Rohit Sharma are in the middle. Krunal is having a chat with Andy Flower.

6.45pm Thanks, Himanshu. While we wait for the toss, you can play ESPNcricinfo's first AR-based game - just aim and hit the stumps.

There's only 15 minutes left for the toss, and here comes Hemant to take you through. Let him know the XIs you look forward to tonight.

6.40pm Here's the busy Deiva Muthu scribbling around from Chepauk: "The Eliminator is set to be played on the pitch that had been used for the league fixture between CSK and MI on May 6. The ball didn't turn that much then, but the slowness of the surface handcuffed MI's batters. In that afternoon game, Deepak Chahar had bowled cutters and knuckle balls in the powerplay, with Dhoni up to the stumps. There was a bit of dew around when CSK and GT trained on Monday evening, but there was no dew during the game on Tuesday. Will dew be a factor today?"

Tim David speaks too: "It's nice to have family here sometimes. The game against Chennai here was an important experience... it's all ahead of us. We have got some good momentum. It was awesome to see Green last night."

6.30pm Still some time away from the toss, and here's probably the best comparison: Chawla, Shokeen, Raghav Goyal and Kartikeya vs Pandya, Bishnoi, Mishra and Gowtham. And, and... look away if you're an MI fan, since LSG hold a 3-0 advantage over them across all their meetings so far.

Which side of the wicket will the batter hit the next ball? If you're in India, you can Play and Watch with ESPNcricinfo's new game.

Ravi Bishnoi also has a chat: "I try my best to contribute to a win. Whenever I get to play, my idea is to try and help the side win. I am blessed to have such a season so far. We have played on pretty tough wickets for batters in Lucknow, so we have that advantage. We take one match at a time."

Quinton de Kock speaks ahead of play: "It's a big occasion. It's a big game for us. Just a four games, but it has been quite different. We kept our eyes on the wicket last night; it's slow, [and there's] little bit of spin. If it feels like a good wicket, we want to get off to a flier... we have an over to assess"

You can follow the ball-by-ball commentary in Hindi and in Tamil too.

6.20pm Come to Chennai, have some fantastic south-Indian food, bowl spin at Chepauk and go home. But if you're a left-hand batter from LSG today - like Quinton de Kock, Nicholas Pooran, Kyle Mayers and Krunal Pandya are - you would hate to face offspin. Ask Sidharth Monga why, and he'll tell you through this tactics board piece, as MI hope they can rectify their away record right when it matters.

Vincy: "How many of them are with me for an El Classico finale? CSK are already there, and hoping for MI to join them soon" --- I guess we have seen them play the final more than the number of El Classicos the world has ever seen

If you are seeing this on a mobile device and didn't know it already, ESPNcricinfo is better experienced on our apps. And we have recently rolled out an update for Android, which you can download or update here.

Making the playoffs - and winning - perhaps comes as naturally to Mumbai Indians as the water-logged roads the city has to face during monsoon. As for Lucknow Super Giants, it is barely a year since they were eliminated in the Eliminator - as simple as that - before fate and form combined to give them another chance. But there's no second chance in Chennai tonight, writes Vishal Dikshit in his preview.

6.10pm The boundaries are "contrasting" for today, Ian Bishop reports. Matthew Hayden then checks the pitch out, and calls it "abrasive". He believes spin, as is usual in Chennai, should play a key role. Even 160-165 might be "too much for LSG" if they happen to chase, Hayden reckons. As far as the ground dimensions are concerned, one side is 61 metres, the other 70. Down the ground and the deep midwicket is 77 metres.

6pm This is it: it's the Eliminator. Win it, and you take a step towards the IPL final; lose it, and you start packing your bags. One of the teams has made it here only because some other team did them a favour on the last day of the league stage. The other side required three wins in a row to consolidate their spot here. This is the IPL. And it is in Chennai for the last time this year. Here's Himanshu saying hello for this LSG vs MI game, with Hemant set to give me company soon.

Mumbai perform only how they can when it matters most: first they post 182 on a decent batting pitch, and then fold LSG for 101. Thus, they are into Qualifier 2. Rohit Sharma vs Hardik Pandya. The MI captain who led the allrounder for years at MI. The GT captain who is seeking back-to-back trophies. Join us for that game in two days' time, even as Al Muthu's report takes you through today's play. See you, and take care!

Akash Madhwal is the Player of the Match for his 5 for 5: "I was just practising, and waiting for this opportunity. I did my engineering, and played tennis-ball cricket since it was my passion. Engineers have a tendency to learn early! I just practice, and that is what we execute. I'm proud of myself, but I'll try to be better. Bumrah bhai has his own place, and I'm just trying to play role. Nicholas Pooran was the best wicket. Everyone at home believes I'm working hard."

Rohit Sharma on making the Qualifier 2: "I had definitely thought of making it [to the Qualifier 2]... We managed our work, and scrambled through it. Akash Madhwal was part of the season last year. He didn't get to play. We knew what he had, and we needed somebody to bowl at the back end. Having seen him, I was confident he could get the job done for us. Talking about scouts, we have seen so many guys have gone on to play for India and done well. First and foremost, it's important to make them feel special and part of the team. They play lot of domestic cricket, but this is a different ball game... Our job is to make sure they are comfortable. As a team, we enjoyed the fielding. We want to keep getting better, and throw ourselves... We knew coming to Chennai, one man won't take us through."

Time for the presentations

Vishal Pawar : "You can credit SKY's emergence to MI as well. He was getting wasted in KKR"

Vysakh Vinayan: "Can we also appreciate Green for his wonderful 41 (23)?" --- Yep, the performance that might fly under the radar today

Cameron Green on the win: "It's nice that it's going well at the moment. Our batting's been really good. Madhwal has been the game changer for us; five today, and got four-for the other day. We had a pretty poor game last game [in terms of fielding]. When you bowl second, all the guys who have batted can bring the energy. Madhwal has been awesome: the moment he came, we realised he is special. Gujarat are the best team. It's going to be a tough challenge, especially on their home turf."

Krunal Pandya on LSG's loss: "We were in a really good position. Everything started when I played that shot... that was not on, and I completely take all the blame. The wicket was the same. We just had to bat better, just take that responsibility. But we didn't do after that break (the first time-out). It's always a tough decision; it's just Kyle had a better record here [than de Kock]. We just felt we could go with Kyle. I just thought we could do something different [starting the bowling with spinners]."

11.20pm Mumbai win by a massive 81 runs, and crush LSG. From 69 for 2, to 101 all out. Four of those eight wickets went to Madhwal - who finished with 5 for 5 - and three to comic run-outs. As if it was meant to be for Mumbai to go closer to a spot in the final. As if the forces agree that Mumbai are perhaps the best when it comes to unearthing talent. Madhwal joins a list which consists of Hardik Pandya, Kishan, Bumrah, Varma, Wadhera and others. LSG were well in the game eight overs into the chase, after which came the first time-out. That is when it all turned upside down.

6pm: The final lap of the playoffs race is about to get underway and the group-stage table-toppers Gujarat Titans will take on Mumbai Indians, who are finding a way to muscle and brain their way past obstacles after a rocky start to the season. Titans have been supremely consistent and have a well-rounded side but were stopped in their tracks by a well-oiled CSK machine in the first qualifier. Titans' top spot gives them a second shot at home and they should have full-strength side available. But conditions might not be all familiar. postText:
Gill's perfect turns the IPL 2023 final into a rematch of Qualifier 1. This time, it'll be the Gujarat Titans at home, taking on Chennai Super Kings. Titans have the chance to be the first IPL franchise to win the league in their first two attempts. For now, it's goodbye from me, Ekanth, my co-commentator, Deivarayan Muthu, and our scorers, Thilak Rama and Venkat Raghav.

Lots of content in from today's game to check out. Hemant's match report is up. Here are Rohit's post-match quotes, reactions to Shubman Gill's 129 and Sampath's stats highlights.

KS: "MI fans be like: Gill giveth, Gill taketh.. (beating RCB in league and MI in Q2)"

Shubman Gill, POTM: Playing ball-to-ball, assessing the situation is important. The over I hit three sixes is where I felt it was my day. It was a good wicket to bat on and I wanted to maximise scoring. (On six hitting) Not a conscious decision, you want to keep evolving. Belief is more important, helps when you're coming off a good international season. Success has been a combination of a lot of things. WI tour last year began change. I was injured in 2021 which is when I worked on my batting I made technical changes as well. (Handling expectations) It doesn't matter when you make your way into the playing field. This is my best innings so far in the IPL.

Hardik Pandya, GT Captain: Lot of hard work has gone behind it, guys have worked hard and their success is reflecting. Shubman's clarity and amazing innings is what's keeping him on top. He wasn't rushed or not in control at any point. He's a superstar who will do big things for the franchise and the country. My job is to keep the boys in a good space. Everyone has taken responsibility which has been fantastic. Rashid has been amazing, especially when we've not been in a commanding position. Irrespective of the result, if we play our best cricket we should do well in the final.

Stat from Sampath: MI in IPL 2023:

Six times scored 200-plus - Most by a team in an IPL edition

Six times conceded 200-plus - Most by a team in an IPL edition

Rajkumar Lingav: "Early preparation for Green, Rohit, SKY, Ishan for WTC. Gill, Bharat, Shami, Rahane and Jaddu will join little late."

Mohit Sharma, 5 for 10: I was lucky to have taken a quick five-for. Ball was skidding well even in the chase, looked like game will slip when SKY and Tilak got going. I thought I wouldn't experiment when SKY's batting as that's what we studied ahead of the game. We were okay being hit for six sixes off length balls as that's more difficult. Match wasn't over after SKY was out but there was relief and we were at comfort. The game wasn't over till the last ball, we've learned in the past that it's not over till then.

Rohit Sharma, MI Captain: Shubman batted well, wicket was good. They got 20-25 extra. We were positive after the first-half. Greeny and Surya batted well but we lost our way. We wanted to give it a good crack, be positive. We couldn't get going in the powerplay. We wanted one batter, like Gujarat did, and take the game deep where anything can happen on a good pitch and a ground with a small boundary. But credit to GT, who played well. Kishan's concussion was unexpected. It was a last-minute change. We had to adapt, to different conditions and situations. Not looking at that though. Playing this game, qualifying and coming this far is big, the batting has been a big positive we can take into the next season. All the bowling teams have been challenged. We had a great performance last game. We have to credit Shubman. I hope he continues that form (laughs). Tim's been given a role this season, I wanted to send Vishnu up. It didn't work out today.

Arun Prakash : "Can't blame the toss. MI chose chasing because that's what they were good at in a batting pitch throughout this season. They were just outplayed by a masterclass innings by Gill. Also, some forced injuries for MI made it an one sided game! "

Bala: "See purple cap table ..all top three are from GT Shami -28 , Rashid-27 and Mohit -24"

11:57pm: Titans move on from their Qualifier 1 slip-up with a thumping win, thanks mainly to being the Gillionaire franchise. Sachin Tendulkar praises him in the post-match handshakes. MI came into the mammoth chase with a disadvantage, losing Ishan Kishan to concussion. Nehal Wadhera's promotion to the top didn't work, Rohit missed out too. Shami was the new-ball striker. Green went back retired hurt after being hit in the forearm, Tilak skyrocketed a cameo that kept them in the chase. Green came back, joined SKY who was working his way from mistiming balls to closing in on nearing his best. But Rashid, despite being more expensive than usual, kept his run rate well under the asking rate. Noor did as well. Little and Mohit came on late, the former took out Green and when the latter knocked over SKY, the game was effectively done.

9.40pm Not long to go now. The Titans bowlers are warming up, and Devon Conway and Ruturaj Gaikwad are padded up and helmeted in the CSK dugout.

9.38pm The covers are coming off. Let's hope we don't see them again tonight.

Paul: "If I was in charge of the half-time show it would involve all the IPL the coaching staff playing a six-a-side game."

Gopal : "This has been a moneyball season for GT this year. They have picked amazing talents at base price who were not that famous. Josh Little, Noor Ahmed, Sai Sudarshan, Mohit Sharma etc."

Rohit: "Dhoni's reaction time was 0.1 seconds on Gill's stumping. Unreal for a 40-year-old" -- 40? He'll be 42 in a month and a half!

9.32pm Good evening, everyone. I come bearing news, and it isn't good news. The covers are coming on in Ahmedabad. The weather gods clearly prefer Deiva's commentary to mine. Anyway, Shashank is at the stadium, and he has this for us: "The sky is rumbling. There's lightning. Covers on. Hint of drizzle in the air, rain is imminent."

9.15pm GT have racked up 214 for 4 on a back of a splendid 96 off 47 balls from Sai Sudharsan. He took on one of the best death bowlers of the tournament, hitting 34 off 14 from Pathirana. Special innings. Special player. I'm short of words. Sai's rise continues. Saha also contributed a half-century to GT's tall total. Karthik Krishnaswamy will be back with you for CSK's chase.

shortText: Mohammed Shami to Gaikwad, no run
text: full on off stump, a hint of away shape, good stride forward for a crisp push-drive to mid-off
preText: 9.45pm Alrighty then. CSK need 215, and the Titans need to keep them to 213 or less. There's the possibility that they'll finish on 214 as well, and that we'll all be here for a little longer than planned. In any case, one of these two teams will get their hands on the IPL trophy very, very soon. It's Conway and Gaikwad to open, as always, and Mohammed Shami to gallop in with the new ball, as always. Sai Sudharsan has had an incredible final, and he'll get to spend the rest of it with his feet up in the dugout. Josh Little comes in for him as Titans' impact player. A slip in place with Gaikwad on strike.
