postText:
12.00am, May 30 So, to recap: CSK are chasing 171 in 15 overs. We'll have a four-over powerplay, and each bowler will be allowed a maximum of three overs. We'll still have two strategic time-outs - the bowling time-out from overs 5-6, and the batting time-out in the 10-12 window.

Harsh: ""We'll still have two strategic time-outs". Modern cricket monetization in a nutshell."

Anupam: "How could you miss Rahane? He is also a part of the WTC squad." -- Oh yes.

11.30pm Out come the umpires again. They're looking at that side pitch, and Ashish Nehra just scraped his heel onto the turf and left a big, dark streak on it. He seems to be suggesting to the umpires that it isn't yet ready for fielders to run on. The heavy roller's starting to go up and down this pitch now. This strip is roughly where cover/midwicket would be, so it's a high-traffic zone.

For what it's worth, Ruturaj Gaikwad is still padded up in CSK's dugout.

The match officials are showing a sheet of paper to Hardik Pandya and Stephen Fleming. DLS calculations?

OKAY WE HAVE NEWS: We're going to have a 15-over chase, with a target of 171. The game will resume at 12.10am. We're officially going into day three.

Deepak: "I remember a Test match vs England in this same ground didn't go to day 3 and now we have a T20 going into third day.. weird times!!"

Mustafa Moudi : "Off-Topic: Since this match has already entered its Day 3 , when will be the remaining Indian Players will be able to travel to England for the WTC Final ?? Will they travel the same day in the morning ??" -- Good question. From this match, Gill, Shami, Jadeja and KS Bharat are part of the Test squad.

11.15pm The groundstaff continue to tend to the problem pitch on the edge of the square. Looks like the rest of the outfield is good to go, pretty much.

Sal: "They should use under-soil heating to dry ground quickly, it is used in English Premier League "

Suresh Muthusam: "The Crowd are the real winners. Standing in Rain for 2 contionious days till.midnight. No word to say. Hats Off"

11.00pm There'll be another inspection at 11.30pm. That's half an hour from now.

Lordnrs: "At what time do we start losing overs?" -- We're not sure exactly when, but it should be at around 11.45pm.

Sravan: "We don't need a kinetic sand. We need a potential sand that will sit and garner mass."

Peter S: "In these times of uncertainty about the future of cricket, it's reassuring to know some things never change and an important match can be held up by a bit of wet grass."

10.45pm The umpires are heading out for the inspection. Hardik Pandya just had a super-animated word with them, but then, he'd be super-animated even if that word was "hi".

The groundstaff seem to have sprinkled some sort of sand or sawdust (someone in the ESPNcricinfo office suggested it could be kinetic sand - whatever that is) onto the damp area we've been talking about. They're also using the roller on it. Let's hope all that has the intended effect. The crowd continues to dance.

Vaibhav: "Reduction in overs will definitely work in favour of CSK and will be very unjust for GT, given they'll also have to deal with wet outfield."

Ashish Tandon: ""kinetic sand - whatever that is". Ask a 5 year old and they will tell you what kinetic sand is. Ask their parents and they will tell you how difficult it is to get off a carpet."

Raff: "You know that magic spray they use when a player gets hurt? Is there a version of that to use on wet grass?"

10.30pm The covers are off, and the groundstaff continue to pay extra attention to the damp pitch on the edge of the square. The rain has most definitely stopped, and the crowd are having a good time by all evidence, dancing to 'Radha kaise na jale' from Lagaan.

Shashank: "@Mohan - that's the effect of climate change on cricket "

Sayed Maghfoor : "This month is named " May" because, it may rain, it may hot, it may cool, it may anything with season!! Very bad feeling right now…from Afghanistan "

BolFan: "'Ghanan ghanan' is more apt for this situation from Lagaan" -- Ha!

10.18pm The groundstaff are paying extra attention to that damp side pitch I'd mentioned earlier, using sponges to mop up the surface moisture, squeezing them out into buckets etc. We might have a bit of a wait on our hands thanks primarily to this patch of turf.

We're hearing there'll be an inspection at 10.45pm.

Prajith : "@Aman: Want to watch cricket match not some music show. It was unnecessary when you know there is rain in the air."

Mohan : "Rain-interrupted match in Ahmedabad and that is also in month of May.Now, I have seen everything. Never ever had even a drop of rain in May."

10.07pm Can't say if the rain has stopped, but if it's still there, it can't be much more than a light drizzle. There's quite a bit of dancing in the stands. The Super Soppers are out on the ground, as are a few CSK players, with a padded-up Ambati Rayudu chatting animatedly with the umpires.

There's one potential problem area on the ground - one of the side pitches took in a real soaking before the groundstaff could bring the covers on. It looks saturated with moisture at this point.

Meanwhile, it has been a sporting weekend of the Yellow Seas. While there is one in Ahmedabad now (waiting), another in Germany had their heart broken and title snatched away from them but the noise from Borussia Dortmund's Yellow Wall didn't stop - a reminder of exactly what football means to people.

10.00pm The covers are on now. Like last night, most of the outfield remains uncovered, but the drainage here should be pretty good, assuming the rain doesn't lash down for as long as it did last night. Hopefully we won't have to wait too long before play resumes.

Okay, so here are some DLS targets (and not par scores) if we lose overs: 66 in five overs, 123 in 10 overs, 171 in 15 overs.

Azweer : "Take a break @KK. Ask Deiva to continue the commentary." -- Let the poor man rest his fingers and get some nourishment!

Aman Bansal: "@Taslim It was an extraordinary show. Worthy of a final. Totally worth every single second. You won't it be saying it if you were present in the stadium."

9.50pm It's begun raining, and heavily at that. Off go the players. The pitch is going to get just a bit of unintended watering before the groundstaff manage to get the covers on. It's bucketing down in Motera as we speak.

Taslim: "Wasted 30-40 minutes on an unnecessary half time show and now the rain is pelting down smh."

Rezwan Rahman S: "What's the DLS par score after 5 overs?" -- These are five-over par scores, not adjusted targets: 43 for 0, 49 for 1, 56 for 2, 65 for 3. As you'd expect, the par jumps quite significantly with every wicket lost thereafter.

back of a length close to off stump, punched to extra-cover. Seemed to stop on him slightly
back of a length, angling across to off stump, clears the front leg and pulls along the ground to deep midwicket

slower ball, fullish on off stump, makes a bit of room and drives to the right of Miller at extra-cover. Moves quickly to the ball and throws at the keeper's end, with no one backing up, and concedes an overthrow
preText: No boundaries since the powerplay.

text: shot! First post-powerplay boundary and it's a six. Not a genuine half-tracker, but it sits up nicely outside off for Conway to pull with conviction and clear the midwicket boundary
tossed up on leg stump, gets forward to clip to long-on
preText:
Noor continues. Left-arm over.

It's time for the first strategic time-out. Just for academic interest, the DLS par now would be 58 for no loss. CSK are well ahead of that.

ShahSafeer: "@IS and it reminds me the RCB's blast start to a big chase in 2016 in the final against SRH! " -- We all know what happened next...

Saket: "This seems very difficult chase for CSK. Any break in momentum, and there is no chance to recover."

Sai: "Csk have got to a flying start but the problem with this chase is they need to keep going at the same rate for the rest of the chase. A tough ask no mater what given the pressure of chasing in a finals. Still advantage GT at this stage"

Srikumar M Meno: "What happens to those dudes who paint themselves in their team colours, when a match goes into the reserve day? Do they doff their paint, have a shower and repaint on the second day, or do they sleep with their paints on?"

text: full on off stump, once again too full for elevation. Driven down to the left of long-on, and Gaikwad is interested in a second but Conway sends him back

wkt_text: RD Gaikwad c Rashid Khan b Noor Ahmad 26 (30m 16b 3x4 1x6) SR: 162.50
text: wrong'un, dangled across Gaikwad and pitching outside off before turning further away. Don't know if he picked it, and if he did he's been done in the air by some dip. Looks to go over long-on, ends up getting a top-edge that skews high in the air before Rashid settles under it at backward point
wrong'un, full and turning in from off stump, gets forward and clips to deep backward square leg
preText:
In walks Shivam Dube. He was bowled by Noor in Qualifier 1. Dube is CSK's impact player, replacing Matheesha Pathirana.

Tallfred: "Is it Chennai Supersopper Kings now? "

text: another wrong'un, pitching just short of driving length outside off. Looks to chip to long-off's right, I think, and it turns in and hits the inside half of the bat, and he ends up chipping to long-off's left

wkt_text: DP Conway c Sharma b Noor Ahmad 47 (34m 25b 4x4 2x6) SR: 188.00
text: Noor bags his second of the over. What an over. Back of a length, and this one turns away from Conway, and it stops on him as well. Lets out a yell of frustration after mishitting it straight down long-off's throat. Was probably looking to hit it over extra-cover off the back foot, not an easy shot to play at all
another wrong'un, ends up a long way down the leg side this time, eluding Conway's sweep
short, gets up to shoulder height over off stump. Pulled in the air, but lands dafely in front of Noor running to his right from deep square leg
preText: Ajinkya Rahane walks in at No. 4, with 93 required from 48 balls. Little to continue to Dube.

text: Now he goes short at Rahane, and he doesn't middle his pull at all. Checks his shot and picks up two, since the fielder has to run in a long way from deep midwicket
preText: Rahane began the season in absolutely blistering ball-striking form. He's cooled off a little since then. Will he bring his A game to the final.

text: walloped. Little slants this back-of-a-length ball across Rahane, finishing just outside off, and he just stands there and baseballs it over the midwicket boundary. Somewhere in between a horizontal-bat and a straight-bat shot
full outside off, punched to extra-cover
preText: Deep backward square leg, deep midwicket, long-on, deep cover point and deep third are the fielders back for Rahane.

text: is this the shot of the match? Half-volley on off stump, but how sweet was the timing? Just gets his front leg out of the way and extends his arms through a straight-bat drive to launch it effortlessly over the straight long-off boundary
short now, gets up to chest height, pulled along the ground towards deep midwicket
length ball turning in from an off-stumpish line. Presses forward  and dabs into the off side to bring Dube on strike
full stock ball turns down the leg side, and Rahane, looking to flick, overbalances a little and leaves the crease, but Saha fumbles it. Missed stumping?
preText: Titans still ahead on win probability according to our predictor. 63.07%, apparently. Noor to finish his quota now. Left-arm over as always.

text: back of a length, flat, straightens close to off stump, punched to long-off
preText: The umpires have called for a ball change. Not sure why they're changing the ball - has it gotten too damp?

text: back of a length close to off stump. Looks to make room and cut, and gets a thick edge that rolls towards short third

shortText: Noor Ahmad to Dube, no run
text: beats him with turn. Flat length ball fairly wide of off stump, and Dube was looking to make a bit of room and crash it over long-off, probably. Beats his outside edge, and Saha whips off the bails. He hasn't lifted his back foot or dragged it out, though
fullish on off stump, clipped down to long-on

shortText: Noor Ahmad to Rahane, no run
text: quickish wrong'un, pitching outside leg, and Noor finishes with figures of 2-17 in three overs after Rahane misses the flick and gets hit on the pad. Superb bowling in difficult circumstances in a massive, massive game
back of a length, straightens towards middle stump. Gets his front leg out of the way and muscles it along the ground to deep midwicket
preText: Rashid returns. Right-arm over.

text: steps out, and Rashid widens his line. Looks to hit over extra-cover, and gets a thick edge that loops up and lands to the right of short third

Clears his front leg to go over long-on, but Rashid fires this too full for that. Thick inside edge dribbles out into the square leg region, and there's no one in the circle there. Rashid gives chase himself, and the batters sneak a quick second run

Dube isn't in rhythm just yet. Quickish and fairly full, turning from leg stump towards his cleared front leg. Inside half of the bat as he looks to go big, and the ball lands well short of long-on, to his left
wrong'un, turns down leg, and Rahane sinks onto his back knee quickly and sweeps it away to the left of short fine leg

four more! Similar shot, more of a kneeling pull than a proper sweep, and again he hits the wrong'un to the left of short fine. Deep backward square leg gives chase to his right and puts in a full-length dive, but it's in vain
back of a length, angling away from off stump, flat-batted along the ground to the right of long-on
preText: 30 balls, 59 runs. Rahane is on 26 off 11. Here comes Mohit Sharma, who's looked unhittable in so many games this season. Over the wicket to the left-hander.

text: slower ball on the pads, clipped to the left of short fine leg. No pace to work with at all
preText:
Raj Patel : "Fiancée supporting GT .. mom supporting CSK … not sure how good my sleep tonight is going to be .. hahah "

Panda: "Take Noor's spell out and CSK have scored 91 in 7 overs. Brilliant Bowling."

text: slower ball slanting away from the left-hander and landing wide of off stump. Dube is in position for the big hit weeks before thre ball reaches him, and in the end he just lets the ball hit his bat, bewildered, and the ball loops over the bowler's head and lands roughly where he began his run-up
goes short and into the pitch, offcutter finishing chest high just outside off. Pulled along the ground to deep midwicket

text: gone. Mohit's lack of pace gets another wicket. Back of a length, outside off, it's there for the slash over point in everry way except it's the back-of-the-hand slowie. Stops on Rahane, and he ends up punching it in the air and straight to the man at deep point
quick length ball nipping in towards middle stump, and Rayudu gets forward for a punch to long-on
preText: Ambati Rayudu walks in for the final time in the IPL with CSK needing 54 off 25 balls. This is still doable, but it needs doing immediately.

text: short outside off, turns away further. Pulled along the ground to deep midwicket
preText: Rashid.

text: flat length ball straightening from an off-stumpish line. Looks to go over the top, but loses his shape and ends up dragging it to deep midwicket, all along the floor

shortText: Rashid Khan to Rayudu, no run
text: quick legbreak outside off, goes back and punches it back to the bowler
full now, too full to get underneath, driven along the ground to long-off

finally, Dube finds some rhythm. Wrong'un, turning away from off stump, and it lands just a touch too full from Rashid. It's in Dube's arc, and he clears his front leg, keeps his head still, and hits it clean and flat over the straight long-on boundary

six more. Dube has arrived alright. This is a legbreak straightening towards off stump, and again it's in Dube's hitting arc. Clears that front leg again, and hits this one higher but just as cleanly, all the way over long-on
postText:
It's time for the final time-out of IPL 2023. CSK need 38 in 18, and Shivam Dube is looking like Shivam Dube now.

Cheithanya: "Should someone from Tamil Nadu support CSK or GT, with more TN boys in GT (with Sai Sudharshan, Vijay Shankar and Sai Kishore)???" -- Be like me: neutral in the IPL, firm Tamil Nadu fan in the Ranji Trophy.

text: trademark Rayudu shot. Mohit bowls a rare slot ball. It's a slower ball but it's the wrong length, and Rayudu steps leg side to create hitting room, and launches it high over long-off
preText: Here's Mohit once again.

text: Four more, and Rayudu is finishing in style. Another error from Mohit. Full-toss outside off, and Rayudu lashes it to the right of the diving extra-cover fielder

terrific shot. Stunning. Back of a length outside off, and Rayudu sits on the back foot, deep in his crease, and launches it with a  straight bat over the long-off boundary, finishing with his bat following through over his left shoulder. Incredible

wkt_text: AT Rayudu c & b Sharma 19 (8m 8b 1x4 2x6) SR: 237.50
text: gone, but what a terrific little cameo to end his IPL career. Quick, hard length, on the stumps, and Rayudu, looking to go over long-on, ends up slicing the ball with his bat turning in his hand. No distance on it, and he pops back the simplest of return catches

preText: Well, well. With 22 needed off 14 balls, MS Dhoni walks out to an absolute wall of noise. And that's just the ESPNcricinfo office I'm talking about. Ahmedabad must be absolutely exploding with Thala fever right now.

text: full, slanting away from off stump, driven with an open face to the right of deep point
preText: What an over this has been. Pure T20. 646WW. Mohit is on a hat-trick. In walks Ravindra Jadeja. Over the wicket.

in the blockhole, angling in towards off stump, clipped to the right of deep midwicket
preText: 18 off 9. Round the wicket now.

text: length ball, angling in towards off stump, ends up a little cramped for room even though he clears his front leg. Drags a swipe to deep backward square leg off the inside half of his bat

full-toss, low full-toss, angling in towards off stump, and Jadeja completely mishits it. Looks to go over long-on, and ends up scooping it towards deep backward square leg. Noor runs in quickly off the rope and dives forward, but he can't reach the ball in time
perfect off-stump yorker, and all Dube can do is get his front leg out of the way and jam his bat down. Jabbed straight back to the bowler
preText: Whodathunk at the start of this tournament that Mohit Sharma, net bowler last season, would bowl the final over of the final, against his former team? CSK need 13 off six balls. Shivam Dube is on strike. Over the wicket.

text: another excellent blockhole ball, slanting across to off stump. This time Dube manages to jab it for a single down to long-off
low, unhittable full-toss on leg stump. Clears his front leg, and he tries to manufacture some sort of elevation but all he can do is hit it to long-on, on the bounce, for a single
preText: 12 off 4, with Ravindra Jadeja on strike. He hasn't had the greatest season with the bat, but all will be forgotten if he middles a couple of big hits.

text: low full-toss slanting away from off stump, and again it's too low for any elevation. Goes down the ground, hits it on the bounce to long-off. Another single
preText: Three incredibly good balls so far. Inch-perfect.

text: SIX! You only have to miss the yorker by a few inches, and you disappear. Looks for the stump yorker, lands it slightly short of where he's aiming, and ends up offering a slot ball that Jadeja launches over long-on, clean and flat. Stunning
preText: 10 off two balls. Mohit grabs a quick glug of water.

text: Jadeja's done it! CSK have won their fifth IPL title! CSK's players run onto the field as one, but MS Dhoni remains in the dugout, eyes closed. An incredible final over from Mohit Sharma ends with two marginal errors. First, an error of length, ended up as a straight six. Then an error of line. Low full-toss, but it's on the pads, and Jadeja swings at it and gets enough bat on it to get it into the gap, fine of short fine leg. What a match. Shame it's been shortened by rain, but the finish has been worth everything that went before
preText: Four to win, three to tie. One last ball to end a sensational tournament. Three-day final, but it's been worth all the waiting and sky-watching.
postText:
3.01am Dhoni collects the IPL trophy and hands it over to Rayudu and Jadeja. CSK celebrate under the fireworks. Dhoni has indicated that he will come back, if his body allows him to. It's all yellow. Hope you enjoyed our coverage as much we did bringing it to you. Until next time, this is Deivarayan Muthu signing off on the behalf of Karthik Krishnaswamy, Thilak Ram, and Venkat Raghav. Goodbye and cheers.

Dhoni: If you circumstantially see, it's the best time to announce the retirement. The easy thing for me to say is thank you and retire. But the hard thing to do is to work hard for nine months and try to play one more IPL season. The body has to hold up. But the amount of love I have received from CSK fans, it would be a gift for them to play one more season. The way they've shown their love and emotion, it's something I need to do for them. It's the last part of my career. It started over here and the full house was chanting my name. It was my same thing in Chennai, but it will be good to come back and play whatever I can. The kind of cricket I play, they feel they can play that cricket. There's nothing orthodox about it and I like to keep it simple. I think every trophy or bilateral series you win, it has its own challenges. When it comes to the crunch, you need to have your individuals ready. The amount of pressure every individual can deal with is different. We tried to do that. Ajinkya [Rahane] is experienced, but if they [youngsters] are confused we chat with them. The special thing about Rayudu if he's on the field he always gives his 100%. We played for India A together - he played spin and fast bowlers equally well. I felt always he will do something special. He's also like me who doesn't use a phone a lot.

2.50am Hardik: I think we tick a lot of boxes and we play with our heart. We've always been a team that has stood together and no one gave up. We win together and we lose together. Maybe one of those games today. I mean, I'm not one of those guys who makes excuses. Special mention to Sai as well. CSK played better cricket. Sai is going to do wonders in his life. Yeah, I mean really happy for the guys. We've been backing them and their success has been their success. Mohit, Shami, Rashid everyone…the way they put their hand up. Special mention to the coaching staff as well. I can't ask anything more from them. I'm very happy for him [Dhoni]. Destiny had this written for him. If I had to lose, I don't mind losing to him. Good things happen to good people.

CSK head coach Stephen Fleming collects the winners' medals on the behalf of the entire team.

2.30am Good morning, NZ fans. Devon Conway is the Player of the Match: It was a long time to wait and nervous for a long period. Rutu and I talked about doing our thing. Personally for me, the biggest win that I've had in my career. Being part of CSK and the fans..it was special. I've got to give a lot of credit to Mike Hussey and nice to be in those shoes.

Gill, the MVP of IPL 2023 and also the Orange Cap winner: Means a lot. The hard work that I've put in is going in the right direction for me. I think it was very important to start well and I started well. By the business end of the tournament, I converted the starts into big ones. I practiced a lot of [sixes] and I changed my technique a little bit for the death. The SRH hundred was about control and the MI was knowing the situation and taking on the opposition. For any batsman, it was important to anticipate and I did that

Mohammed Shami, Purple Cap winner: People watching enjoy it a lot but it is difficult for those doing it. Only two fielders outside, it is a challenge. There is extra responsibility in T20s. I am also a human, the white ball and red ball make a big difference, and you have to adjust."

RR's Yashasvi Jaiswal is the Emerging Player of IPL 2023. He's with India's WTC squad in the UK. So, Dube collects the award on the behalf of Jaiswal.

2.15am Dhoni is now having a chat with the Pandya brothers and Vijay Shankar. He still has that smile on his face. CSK's CEO Kasi now has a chat with Dhoni.

Manu Ajmani: "The best moment was when Dhoni sat there, expressionless, unmoved, no smile, no celebration for a few moments until he gathered his thoughts and joined the rest of the team. Not sure what to do if he announces his retirement because my gut says the famous last words "from this moment onwards, consider me retired" are a few minutes away!"

1.55am Thanks, Karthik. Hello, again, everyone. The broadcaster shows replays of a teary-eyed Dhoni lifting Jadeja up. Such an emotional moment. Gujarat boy Jadeja then hugs his wife under the fireworks. Some fireworks are also going off in my locality in Chennai. Dhoni has a smile on his face and celebrates with his boys in yellow. Nice to see the injured Mukesh Choudhary part of the celebrations too. Mukesh has been travelling with the squad since CSK's away game in Bengaluru. Dhoni is yet to speak at the post-match presentation. Do make yourself a brew and stick around with us.

Rayudu: It's a fairytale finish. I couldn't have asked for more. I'm fortunate to have played in really great sides. I can smile for the rest of my life. All the hard work I've done in the last 30 years, I'm happy I got to finish on this note. I would really like to thank my family, my father. Without them this wouldn't have been possible.

Jadeja: Feels amazing, winning my fifth title in front of my home crowd. I'm from Gujarat, and it's a special feeling. This crowd has been amazing. They were waiting for rain to stop till late night, I'd like to say a big congratulations to the CSK fans who came to support us. I'd like to dedicate this win to a special member of the CSK side, MS Dhoni. I was just thinking I need to swing hard, as much as I can. Where the ball will go, I was not thinking about that, just looking to swing hard. I was backing myself and looking to hit straight, because I know Mohit can bowl those slower balls.

Hussey: Hats off to Gujarat as well, they've been amazing through the season, but thankfully Jaddu got us over the line.Dhoni is an amazing human being. A good example is, in the qualifier, he was telling Senapati to remain calm, and he got us a crucial run-out. Some of those shots from Rayudu, the slower balls that he hit over cover, not many people can do that.

Fleming: It's a real caravan of cricket, and it comes down to the last two balls, and you're just sitting and watching. You age quickly when that happens. We were a little bit short in the bowling department to start, and Deshpande stepped up. Pathirana gave us a sting in the tail in the end overs.

Conway: I was just thinking positive intent, swing for the hills. It's been great batting alongside Rutu, such a clean hitter of the ball. Our partnership has worked really well, left-right combination, and we enjoy our time together. I think this environment is really good. We've got some top players, gives me the oportunity to speak to them about batting and learn so much.

Bravo: It's a great journey, and I've got to give credit to our entire bowling unit and also coach Eric Simons. It's a great combination between Eric and myself, and we're proud to see this young bowling group go out and showcase their talent. I hope my best friend Kieron Pollard is watching. He has some catching up to do.

Deshpande: As I said before the tournament started, I wanted to win the IPL title, and with DJ by my side, all my plans are clear.

Moeen: You're always learning from MS, how to deal with players and situations. It's a massive part of IPL, and that's why we've done so well.

Rahane: Credit goes to CSK management for backing me. They said they would back me completely if I got an opportunity. The victory is really special. Great team man [on Rayudu]. The knock he played today was really special.

Gaikwad: This one was special, because of how it went last year for us. To come back in style, win away games, win in Chepauk, and the finish was unbelievable. We would like to dedicate this win to Rayudu.

Chahar: He [Rayudu] was telling me, I'll win the final. That belief that he has is unbelievable.

1.35am One thirty-five AM. We began this final day before yesterday, and we've had just 35 overs in all this time, but we'll remember it for a long time. Dhoni has finally gotten out of the dugout and joined his celebrating team-mates. Ravindra Jadeja ends the tournament with a six and a four when CSK needed 10 off two balls. We'll remember that, but don't forget the four balls Mohit Sharma bowled before that, four unhittable balls that almost, almost won the tournament for Gujarat Titans. And don't forget B Sai Sudharsan, who went from making everyone wonder if he should retire out to playing one of the great IPL final knocks. Sweet, sweet finish to Ambati Rayudu's IPL career too. He's been around for so long, and he's played so many impact innings, and he's won multiple titles with the two most successful franchises in the tournament, but he's flown under the radar for most of that time. I'll hand over to Deivarayan Muthu to bring you the player interviews and presentation.

Dhruv: "For me the best moment was not the Jadeja and Dhoni one but the one where Hardik Pandya hugged Mohit Sharma immediately after the game."

Shyam: "Chennai lad Sai gave GT the total an impetus but it was down to a gujarathi rockstar in Jadeja to finish the match for CSK... Now that's IPL"

Sharad Rajaseka: "If Dhoni retires it will be surreal! An innings that started with a duck against Bangladesh! Now a duck in his potentially last innings"

CSK fan: "Why do we watch sports? Because of moments like these."

Aman: "Is that a full circle for MS Dhoni? 0 for 1 in 2004 debut, 0 for 1 in the end."

Adhiyan : "Chennai boy took the way from CSK, and then Gujurat boy got the last ball 4 to win"

edwin: "Who will play today's Rayudu's innings? :'( Surely he will be missed in CSK's team. "

Ramc: "I can say Jaddu is Thalapathy of CSK"
